scopeNotes.notes:
Covered: ardi, the audio sample entry (readAudioSampleEntryBox, createAudioSampleEntryReader, mp4a, enca), avc1 to avc4 (through readVisualSampleEntryBox and writeVisualSampleEntryBox), ctts, dinf, dref, edts. For each I read the type in src/boxes, the reader, the writer, the tests, the API report, and the clause in the 2015 spec text (8.5.2.2, 8.6.1.3, 8.6.5, 8.7.1, 8.7.2, 12.1.3, 12.2.3, and the template rule in clause 4.2). I read url and urn only as the entries of dref, so two findings (trimmed reader key, lower-case aliases) overlap the scope of those boxes. Two findings describe a package-wide pattern that I confirmed by grep outside my boxes and reported once: `entryCount` handling in writers and exposed reserved fields. The `template` naming finding concerns the field functions and uses my boxes as evidence.

Verification method: read only. I ran no build and changed no repo file. I ran the source files directly with node 24 from a scratch script (<scratchpad>/probe-scope1.ts) and ran `tsc --noEmit` on a scratch file (<scratchpad>/types-scope1.ts) to confirm the behavior and type claims quoted as "probe" and "tsc".

Could not check: the `ardi` box is not in the 2015 text or in the CMAF and CENC texts, so I did not compare its syntax, clause number, or value range with a spec. ISO/IEC 14496-15 was not available, so the statement about the `VisualSampleEntryBox` clause rests on 14496-12:2015 clause 12.1.3 only. Editions after 2015 may add child boxes or fields to these boxes that I could not see.

No defect found in: the byte layout, order, sizes, and signedness of the readers for the visual sample entry (78 bytes), the audio sample entry (28 bytes), ctts versions 0 and 1, dref, dinf, and edts. They match the 2015 syntax.

Covered: elng, elst, emsg, encv, free, skip, frma, ftyp, styp, grpl, hdlr. For each box I read the type in src/boxes, the reader, the writer, the existing tests, and the syntax in the 14496-12:2015 text (ftyp 4.3.2, free 8.1.2, hdlr 8.4.3, elng 8.4.6, elst 8.6.6, frma 8.12.2, styp 8.16.2, SampleEntry 8.5.2.2, VisualSampleEntry 12.1.3). I also read IsoBoxReadView.ts, IsoBoxWriteView.ts, the shared visual sample entry reader and writer, the string utils, the cursor RFC, the API report, and the fixture round-trip test.

Behavior claims marked "probe" come from two throwaway scripts in the scratchpad (<scratchpad>/audit-b/probe.ts and probe2.ts) that import the src files with node. No repo file was changed and no build ran.

Not checked or not available:
- The text of ISO/IEC 23009-1 was not available. The emsg field order and sizes in readEmsg and writeEmsg match what the code comments state, but I could not compare them with the spec text. The CMAF text (7.4.5) holds semantics only, no syntax. The statement about which 23009-1 edition adds version 1 is unconfirmed.
- grpl is not in the 2015 edition. I did not check its syntax or its allowed children. The name GeneralTypeBox for the ftyp and styp base class is from memory of a later edition and is unconfirmed.
- The compile error in the finding on writeVisualSampleEntryBox is read from the signatures. I did not compile it.
- No reader against spec defect was found for elng, elst (sizes, signedness, and the version 1 rule match the literal syntax), free, skip, frma, hdlr, or the visual sample entry field layout. The reader and the writer agree on field order and sizes for every box in scope.

Overlap: the findings on VisualSampleEntryBox, SampleEntryBox, the four-character code fields, and the count fields apply to boxes outside this scope too (avc1 and the other sample entries, schm, sbgp, stts, stco, stss, stsc). I reported them once from the encv, frma, ftyp, hdlr, and elst side.

Covered: hev1, hvc1, the visual sample entry (type, readVisualSampleEntryBox, createVisualSampleEntryReader, writeVisualSampleEntryBox), iden, imda, kind, labl, mdat, mdhd, mdia, meco. For each I read the type in src/boxes, the reader, the writer, the tests in test/readers and test/writers, and the related entries in IsoBoxMap, IsoBoxReader, IsoBoxReadView, IsoBoxWriteView, the API report, the docs, and the RFC. I compared mdat (8.1.1), mdia (8.4.1), mdhd (8.4.2), SampleEntry (8.5.2.2), kind (8.10.4), meco (8.11.7), and VisualSampleEntry (12.1.3) with the 2015 text of 14496-12.

No defect found against the spec for: the field order, sizes, and signs of the visual sample entry reader and writer (78 bytes, `pre_defined` read as signed), the mdhd reader and writer for versions 0 and 1, mdat, kind, mdia, and meco.

Could not check: `imda` and `labl` are not in the 2015 edition, so I did not compare their syntax (field sizes, the meaning of flag bit 0x1 of `labl`, the clause numbers). ISO/IEC 14496-30 (`iden`) and ISO/IEC 14496-15 (`hev1`, `hvc1` coding names) were not available. I therefore did not report the name `WebVttCueIdBox` or the choice of `readUtf8(-1)` in `readIden`. I ran no build, no test, and no compiler, so the statement that a direct call of `writeVisualSampleEntryBox` with a `VisualSampleEntryBox<'av01'>` fails to compile comes from the signatures only.

Seen outside this scope, not audited: the audio sample entry has the same argument order, factory, `any` children, and writer constraint as the visual sample entry. Required `reserved` and `preDefined` fields also exist in TrackHeaderBox, MovieHeaderBox, HandlerReferenceBox, SoundMediaHeaderBox, SegmentIndexBox, and TrackFragmentRandomAccessBox. `readStsd` types every entry as `AudioSampleEntryBox | VisualSampleEntryBox` by default, also for an entry type with no reader in the map. Four more files use the edition placeholder "202x".

Covered all ten box types (mehd, meta, mfhd, mfra, mfro, minf, moof, moov, mvex, mvhd): the type in src/boxes, the reader, the writer, the tests, and the syntax in 14496-12:2015 (clauses 8.2.1, 8.2.2, 8.4.4, 8.8.1, 8.8.2, 8.8.4, 8.8.5, 8.8.9, 8.8.11, 8.11.1, 6.2.2) plus 23001-7:2016 8.1.1 for the pssh container. Field order, sizes, signedness, and version conditions of readMvhd, readMehd, readMfhd, and readMfro match the 2015 syntax, and each writer mirrors its reader. I found no wrong-data defect in those four leaf boxes. The track ID naming (`nextTrackId`, `trackId`) is consistent across the package.

To confirm the type findings I ran `tsc --noEmit` on one scratch file in the scratchpad (<scratchpad>/audit-mvhd/probe.ts) that imports the src types. No file in the repo was changed, and no build or test ran. `git status` is clean.

Not checked: run-time behavior (the TypeError statements for a missing `matrix`, `reserved2`, or `preDefined` come from reading the code, not from a run). Editions after 2015 were not available, so I could not verify `grpl` as a meta child or later children of moov, moof, and mvex. `leva`, `trep`, `idat`, `xml `, and `bxml` have no type in IsoBoxMap, so I only report their absence from the child unions. Two findings reach beyond the ten boxes and other auditors may report them too: the child typing for boxes with no reader (package-wide typing rule) and the `template` naming (view and cursor API). The reserved-field and matrix findings apply in the same form to tkhd, smhd, hdlr, sidx, and the sample entries, which are outside this scope.

Covered: payl, prft, prsl, pssh, schi, schm, sdtp, sidx, sinf, smhd. For each box I read the type in src/boxes, the reader, the writer, and the tests in test/readers and test/writers (plus test/containerReaders.test.ts, test/containerWriters.test.ts and the count table of test/fixtureRoundTrip.test.ts). I also read src/IsoBoxReadView.ts, src/IsoBoxWriteView.ts, src/utils/readTemplate.ts, the API report, the cursor RFC, and the changelog entries for these boxes.

Spec checks done against the supplied text: prft (14496-12:2015, 8.16.5.2), schm (8.12.5.2), schi (8.12.6.2), sinf (8.12.1.2), sdtp (8.6.4.2), sidx (8.16.3.2), smhd (12.2.2.2), pssh (23001-7:2016, 8.1.2). The field sizes, the order, the signedness and the version and flag conditions of the readers and writers match those clauses. I found no wrong-data defect in the ten readers.

Not checked: the syntax of prsl and EntityToGroupBox (not in the 2015 text) and of payl (ISO/IEC 14496-30 was not available). The flag values 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x4000 of prsl and the string type of payl are therefore unverified. The 2012 and 2011 editions that the TSDoc cites were not available, so I could not confirm clause 8.4.5.3 for smhd or the content of 23001-7:2011.

Nothing was run. The claims about writer behavior with mismatched counts come from reading writePssh.ts, writePrsl.ts and IsoBoxWriteView.writeArray, not from execution. References to hls.js and shaka-player come from the local checkouts under ~/dev.

Several findings name the same pattern in boxes outside this scope (count fields, reserved fields, number[] byte fields in tenc, the 4CC of frma, explicit undefined keys in tfhd). I listed those only as context. Their own auditors should confirm them.

Covered all eleven box types (ssix, stbl, stco, sthd, strk, stsc, stsd, stss, stsz, sttg, stts): type declaration, reader, writer, tests, and the syntax in 14496-12-2015.txt. Reader field sizes, signedness, and order match the 2015 syntax for ssix, stco, stsc, stsd, stss, stsz, stts, and sthd. No spec deviation found in the readers. The text of ISO/IEC 14496-30 (sttg) was not available, so the sttg findings use only evidence from the package.

Method notes: I ran three scratch scripts and one tsc type check from the scratchpad folder <scratchpad>/audit-st against src (node type stripping, no build, no file in the repo changed). The heap numbers in the stss finding come from one run each and are not a benchmark.

Not reported, by instruction: the RFC items (view classes, size code, view/size fields), a read past the end of a box for an entry_count larger than the box (issue 668, closed), and value range checks in writers (a writer does not throw).

Seen outside this scope, not verified in depth, for the other auditors: (1) `DataReferenceBox` has the same `entries` field for child boxes as stsd. (2) `CompTimeToSampleEntry` duplicates `CompositionTimeToSampleEntry` (src/boxes/CompTimeToSampleEntry.ts). (3) Lower-case type aliases `co64`, `stz2`, `url`, `urn` exist for four boxes only (for example src/boxes/ChunkLargeOffsetBox.ts:17). (4) `IsoBoxMap` has types with no reader and no writer in src, for example co64, stz2, stsh, stdp, saiz, saio, sbgp, sgpd. (5) `IsoBoxMap` lists `subs` before `stz2` (src/IsoBoxMap.ts:181-182). (6) The TSDoc of the internal `writeContainerBox` names `IsoBmffWriter` and a `view` property (src/utils/writeContainerBox.ts:9-16). (7) `ChunkLargeOffsetBox.chunkOffset` is `number[]` with no `V` parameter, so adding co64 to `SampleTableBoxChild` may later require `SampleTableBox<V>`.

Covered all ten box types: subs, tenc, tfdt, tfhd, tfra, tkhd, traf, trak, tref, trex. For each one I read the type in src/boxes, the reader, the writer, the tests, and the syntax in the spec text (tenc from ISO/IEC 23001-7:2016 clause 8.2, the others from ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015). I also read IsoBoxReadView, IsoBoxWriteView, writeBox, writeContainerBox, IsoBoxMap, IsoBoxContainerMap, the API report, the CHANGELOG entries for these boxes, the reading guide table of 64-bit fields, and the cursor RFC.

No defect found against the spec in the field order, sizes, signedness, or version and flag conditions of readSubs, readTfdt, readTfhd, readTfra, readTkhd, and readTrex, or in their writers for a box whose fields are consistent. The `trackId` form is consistent across the package. The 64-bit table in docs/reading-boxes.md is correct for tfdt, tfhd, tfra, and tkhd.

Not checked: I ran no build, no test, and no compiler. The statements about TypeScript errors (closed child unions) and about the TypeError for a hand-built TrackReferenceTypeBox come from reading the code. I did not consult the CMAF text. The 2012 edition was not available, so I could not confirm that the clause numbers cited as 2012 match that edition.

Overlap with open issues: issue 625 (writers use the count field) covers the writer side of the count finding and names writeTfra and writeSubs. Issue 652 (co64, stz2 have a type and no reader) is the same defect class as the senc, saiz, saio finding and does not list those types. Several findings apply to boxes outside this scope (reserved fields in mvhd, smhd, hdlr, sidx and the sample entries, number[] byte fields in pssh, count fields in about 20 box types, closed child unions in other containers). Other scopes may report the same rule for their boxes.

One proposal touches a settled area and needs a decision: parsing the children of `tref` inside `readTref` removes `tref` from the group of containers that read the same with and without the named reader. The finding gives a second option that keeps the automatic handling.

Covered: trun, udta, url, urn, vlab, vmhd, vttC, vttc, vtte. For each box I read the type in src/boxes, the reader, the writer, the tests in test/readers and test/writers, the container tests, test/fixtureRoundTrip.test.ts, the API report, and the related dispatch code (IsoBoxReadView.ts, IsoBoxWriteView.ts, utils/writeBox.ts, IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts). I compared trun (8.8.8), url and urn (8.7.2), udta (8.10.1) and vmhd (12.1.2) with the 2015 text of ISO/IEC 14496-12. Read only: I ran no build and no test, so every behavior claim comes from reading the source.

Not checked: the WebVTT boxes (vlab, vttC, vttc, vtte) are defined in ISO/IEC 14496-30, and that text was not available. I therefore did not compare their field names, the string definition, or the child list of the cue box with the spec. Two items need that text before a decision: (1) the type name `WebVttEmptySampleBox` for `vtte` may differ from the spec class name, which I recall as an empty cue box and could not confirm, (2) the package has no types for other possible cue children such as `vsid` and `ctim`, and no `wvtt` sample entry, so the default reader never reaches a `vttC` or `vlab` box inside a real `stsd` box. I also did not verify the clause numbers of the 2012 edition, only those of the 2015 edition.

Checked with no finding: the reader of trun matches the spec for field order, sizes, flag conditions and signedness. `graphicsmode` and `opcolor` follow the package rule for spec names with no underscore (as `samplerate`, `channelcount`). `readUrl` and `writeUrl` follow the self-contained flag rule. `readUdta`, `writeUdta`, `readVttc` and `writeVttc` delegate to the shared container code. Items that the cursor RFC already covers (size code in writers, view classes, `view`/`size` fields) are not repeated. The count-field pattern (`entryCount`, `sampleCount` beside an array) exists in many boxes outside this scope (stts, ctts, stsz, stss, subs). I reported it only for trun.

Covered: exact set comparison of IsoBoxMap keys (100), reader files and index (82 box readers plus 2 generic readers, 2 factories, defaultReaderConfig), writer files and index (82 box writers plus 2 generic writers, defaultWriterConfig), and src/boxes (120 type files against boxes/index.ts). Results: readers and writers match each other exactly. Every reader and writer file is in its index. Only CompTimeToSampleEntry.ts is missing from boxes/index.ts. CONTAINERS and IsoBoxContainerMap both hold the same 19 types, and each has a named reader and writer. defaultReaderConfig and defaultWriterConfig hold the same 63 keys, which is the 82 implemented types minus the 19 container types. Nothing is missing from either default, and `meta` is in both because it is not in CONTAINERS.

Method: I read the source in src/, the API report, the guides, the two RFCs, and the tests. I checked the type claims with tsc 6.0.3 on a scratch file outside the repo, and the run-time claims with Node 24 on the test fixtures, also outside the repo. The scratch files are deleted and `git status` is clean. I ran no build and edited no repo file.

Could not check: ISO/IEC 14496-30 was not available, so the allowed children of `vttc` and the place of `vlab` are not verified against the spec. The 2012 and later editions of 14496-12 were not available, so `grpl`, `prsl`, `labl`, `elng` clause numbers, `kind`, `ardi`, and `imda` are not verified. No fixture has a `tref` box, so the `tref` finding rests on the code and the type check. I did not review field-level correctness of the 82 implemented readers and writers.

Observations outside my scope, not reported as findings: (1) `writeIsoBox(box, config?)` has an optional config and `writeIsoBoxes(boxes, config)` requires it (src/writeIsoBox.ts:19, src/writeIsoBoxes.ts:22). The cursor RFC table keeps that difference. (2) `IsoBoxReadableStream` and `createIsoBoxReadableStream` are two exports for one thing. (3) The cursor RFC contract says a container box with no map entry is `read and written through its boxes field` and that `writeIsoBoxes` throws only for a box with `no writer, no boxes field, and no bytes field`. The current rule from issue 651 (docs/writing-boxes.md:18) is that a box outside CONTAINERS with a `boxes` field and no writer is not written as a container, because `meta`, `prsl`, and the sample entries have fields before their children. The RFC wording may bring back the data loss that issue 651 fixed. (4) readVtte.ts and writeVtte.ts carry `// eslint-disable-next-line` comments, and the repo no longer uses ESLint.

Covered: the complete API report (libs/iso-bmff/config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md, 1883 lines), src/index.ts and the four sub-indexes, every root type file, src/IsoBoxFields.ts, src/utils (public and internal), IsoBoxReadView.ts, the stream files, the entry points, about 40 box type files, about 25 readers and writers that a naming question touched, the three guides, the README, the changelog, and the API reports of id3 and cmcd. I did not edit, build, or commit anything in the repo.

Checks I ran, all from the scratchpad: (1) tsc on a scratch file that imports the package source, for the claims about `IsoBoxType`, `box.type === 'uuid'`, `senc` narrowing, the `traf` child union, the `tref` child type, and the writer constraint of the sample entries. (2) A Node script on the package source and test/fixtures/hvc1_init.mp4, for the claims about `findIsoBox` under `stsd`, the `url` map key, `isFullBox(null)`, `writeIsoBox` with no config, mutation of `CONTAINERS`, and the keys of a `senc` box.

Comparison with id3 and cmcd. Both put the package token in nearly every public name (`Id3Frame`, `getId3Frames`, `CmcdKey`, `CMCD_V1`). cmcd has two exceptions, `createFetchTransport` and `createXhrTransport`. cmcd names constants `CMCD_*` and enum objects in the singular with a same-named type (`CmcdEventType`). cmcd uses `*Options` for the argument of a call and `*Config` for a long-lived object. id3 marks its helpers `@internal`. iso-bmff differs in each point: unprefixed constants (`DATA`, `CONTAINERS`), unprefixed helpers (`isContainer`, `isFullBox`, `fourCcToUint32`, `defaultReaderConfig`), a plural enum (`IsoBoxFields`), `Config` for call arguments with one `options` parameter, and helper types with no token (`Box`, `FullBox`, `TypeBox`, `Entity`). The API report has no `@internal`, `@alpha`, `@beta`, or `@deprecated` export.

Not checked: the text of ISO/IEC 14496-30 (WebVTT box names) and the 2012 edition of 14496-12 were not available. The 2015 text has no `emsg`, `imda`, `prsl`, `labl`, `ardi`, or `grpl`, so I made no claim about their syntax. I did not audit every reader and writer field by field, and I did not review the methods of `IsoBoxReadView` and `IsoBoxWriteView`, because the RFC replaces them. I read only the titles of open issues 584, 625, 629, and 652. Issue 652 overlaps the finding on types with no reader, and issue 625 overlaps any proposal about count fields. Findings on `TrackEncryptionBox` field names touch the rules of PR 658, which were made under a no-break constraint. The findings on field types (`number[]` bytes, four-character codes, `SegmentIndexReference`, child unions) are at the edge of the "exported names" scope and may duplicate a per-box audit.

Scope covered: all 22 named type files, all 121 files in src/boxes (every box type, not a sample of 25), IsoBoxReadView.ts, readIsoBoxes.ts, traverseIsoBoxes.ts, findIsoBox.ts, filterIsoBoxes.ts, isIsoBoxType.ts, the utils folder, defaultReaderConfig.ts, defaultWriterConfig.ts, 38 readers, 20 writers, the three guides, the Unreleased changelog section, config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md (by grep), and rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md.

Method: read only. No repo file was changed, no build was run. Type claims were checked with the repo's tsc 6.0 (`--noEmit`) on scratch files that import libs/iso-bmff/src/index.ts. Run-time claims were checked with node 24 on a scratch script against src and the fixtures test_frag.mp4 and hvc1_init.mp4. The scratch files are in <scratchpad>/tc (t1.ts to t4.ts, r1.ts).

Spec checks used the 2015 text of ISO/IEC 14496-12 and the 2016 text of 23001-7. Not available, so not checked: ISO/IEC 14496-30 (WebVTT boxes, including the allowed children of vttc), 14496-15, 23009-1 (emsg), and the later 14496-12 editions that define ardi, elng children, labl, prsl, imda, and kind. Clause numbers in comments that cite the 2012 edition were only compared with the 2015 text.

Not reported because the RFC covers them: the view classes, the size code of the writers, the fields view/size/largesize/usertype, IsoBoxStreamable, the return type of writeIsoBoxes, and the second parameter `type` and type parameter `T` of IsoBoxReader. Three findings touch the RFC on purpose, because the RFC text leaves the point open: the result type of readIsoBoxes with raw boxes, the three Parsed* aliases, and the IsoBoxFields exports.

On the prompt item "types that leak V where no 64-bit field exists": I found no such leak. Every container type with `V` has a child that can hold a 64-bit field. The only parameter with no field use is `V` of ParsedBox, which types `view` and goes away with the RFC. The reverse case exists and is in the finding on the 18 types with no reader (co64, saio).

Names were out of scope and are not reported (for example the lowercase field names `channelcount`, `horizresolution`, `graphicsmode`, or the type names `DecodingTimeSample` against `CompositionTimeToSampleEntry`).

The 12-writer count, the 24-type count, the 21 reserved fields, and the 14 types with `boxes` outside IsoBoxContainerMap come from grep and tsc output, not from memory. Writers and readers that I did not open (about 50 readers and 66 writers, mostly one-line container and sample entry functions) may hold more cases of the same patterns.

Covered: src/IsoBoxReadView.ts, readIsoBoxes.ts, IsoBoxReadViewConfig.ts, readers/defaultReaderConfig.ts, utils/readInt.ts, readUint.ts, readString.ts, readTemplate.ts, readUtf8String.ts, getTerminatedStringLength.ts, readInt64AsBigInt.ts, createInt64OverflowReader.ts, IsoFieldTypeMap.ts, IsoBoxFields.ts, IsoBoxType.ts, ParsedBox.ts, ParsedIsoBox.ts, IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts, IsoBoxReader.ts, IsoBoxReaderMap.ts, utils/CONTAINERS.ts, isContainer.ts, traverseIsoBoxes.ts, findIsoBox.ts, utils/writeBox.ts, the integer, string and template methods of IsoBoxWriteView.ts (for symmetry only), docs/reading-boxes.md, docs/utilities.md, README.md, the Unreleased section of CHANGELOG.md, and the tests readBoxes, readIsoBoxes, incompleteBoxHeader, readData, readString, readUtf8, readTemplate, readInt. I read about 20 reader files only as evidence for the read primitives. I did not audit each reader against the specification.

Method: every runtime claim marked "Probe" comes from a script in the session scratchpad that imports the files in src directly with Node 24. Every compile claim comes from a scratch file checked with the repo tsc against src/index.ts, with negative controls. No file in the repo was changed, and no build ran.

Not reported on purpose: the three signatures of readIsoBoxes, the two signatures of defaultReaderConfig, and the conditional rest parameter. rfc/uint64-reader-config.md (lines 200 to 209, 468, 469) defines them as rules of the accepted int64 RFC. The signed 64-bit read (readInt(8), readInt64AsBigInt with BigInt.asIntN) is correct for the test cases and I found no defect. readData returns a view, which is documented and tested, so I report only the missing statement in the guide (inside the byte field finding). The class design items that the cursor RFC replaces (slice, jump, done, the truncated flag, Object.assign of the reader result, the uuid usertype) are mentioned only as evidence.

Could not check: ISO/IEC 14496-30 was not available, so the vttC and payl difference is reported as a difference between readers, not as a specification defect. The 2015 edition of 14496-12 was the only text for the size 0 rule and the template rule. Findings 9 and 10 (four-character codes, byte fields) and finding 2 (stsd entries) touch box types and traversal, so another scope may report the same items.

Covered: src/IsoBoxWriteView.ts, writeIsoBox.ts, writeIsoBoxes.ts, IsoBoxWriteViewConfig.ts, IsoBoxWriter.ts, IsoBoxWriterMap.ts, IsoBoxStreamable.ts, IsoBoxReadableStream.ts, createIsoBoxReadableStream.ts, every file in src/utils, src/writers/defaultWriterConfig.ts, and all 85 writers (about 70 read in full, the container writers and the sample entry aliases by search, since each is one forwarding call). For symmetry I read IsoBoxReadView.ts, the read utilities, about 35 readers, the box types those writers use, IsoBoxMap.ts, the five named tests, test/fixtureRoundTrip.test.ts (header), docs/writing-boxes.md, the writer lines of README.md and of the Unreleased changelog section, the API report, and the RFC.

Method: no repo file was changed, no build and no test suite ran. I ran three read-only probe scripts with Node 24 against src (the scripts are in the session scratchpad, outside the repo). Every "read-only run of the source" in the evidence comes from those runs.

Spec checks against the supplied text: 14496-12:2015 for clause 6.2.2 (template, pre-defined, fixed-point, no wrap), ftyp, hdlr, mdhd, mvhd, tfra, frma, schm, the visual and audio sample entries, and the clause numbers in the TSDoc. 23001-7:2016 for tenc. The 2012 edition was not available, so the claim that the cited clause numbers belong to the 2015 edition rests on the 2015 text only. I did not compare the other writers line by line with the specification (ardi, prsl, labl, imda, and the WebVTT boxes are not in the 2015 text).

Checked with no finding: no writer changes its input (the only reassignment is a local parameter in writeBytes). Every reader file has a writer file, and the two default configs have the same 63 keys. The version rules of elst, mdhd, mvhd, tkhd, mehd, tfdt, tfra, sidx, prft, subs, pssh, ctts, and emsg match their readers and the settled literal-syntax decisions. writeTemplate rounding (Math.round) is exact for every value that the field can hold.

Not reported because the RFC covers them: the class design, the size code, the fields view/size/largesize/usertype, the IsoBoxStreamable union, the single returned array, the write of an edited parsed box from its old view bytes when no writer exists, the intermediate child arrays (three TODO comments), and the arrow-field form of the class methods. Findings 1 and 4 concern gaps in the RFC contract, not those items.

Overlap with other scopes is likely for the type findings (count fields, reserved fields, four-character codes, number[] byte fields, tenc, SegmentIndexReference, IsoBoxMap, CONTAINERS, the vtt names). Proposed rule set for every 2.0.0 reader and writer, collected from the findings: (1) one object literal for each box and each entry, all keys in spec order, absent fields `undefined`, no spread, no property added later. (2) Every test on version, flags, or a header field is computed before the loop. (3) Arrays are created with the known count. A table with one column is a typed array. (4) Bytes are `Uint8Array` views, never `number[]`. (5) The array is the only source of a count. (6) No reserved, pre_defined, or derived duplicate fields. (7) Child boxes are always in `boxes`. (8) A four-character code is a string, decoded with one call. (9) No statement at module scope except declarations and literals, and lazy creation of TextDecoder and TextEncoder. (10) Map keys are exact box types.

Scope: resource use and failure mode for hostile or damaged input, measured by running libs/iso-bmff/src/index.ts on Node 24.22.3 (arm64, Apple M1 Pro). Matrix results:
(a) Cuts: 15 fixtures, every byte offset, 5,806,033 cuts, defaultReaderConfig. All return the complete top-level boxes before the cut. 0 throw, 0 above one second (maximum 4.1 ms, heap delta at most 1.1 MB). For fixtures above 30 KB the script reads only the top-level box that contains the cut and adds the count of the boxes before it. For the smaller fixtures it reads the complete prefix. spliced_10000.m4v is itself cut (9,663 of 10,000 bytes are complete boxes).
(b) Byte changes: first 4 KB of each fixture, 8 to 10 replacement values for each byte, 367,642 cases. Read: 365,626 return, 1,995 throw (all `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`, no other type or message), 21 end the process. The script also wrote every returned result with writeIsoBoxes: 0 write errors. No returned result contains NaN.
(c) Counts: 0xFFFFFFFF and a count above the box content for stts, ctts, stsc, stco, stss, stsz, elst, sidx, ssix, subs, tfra, pssh, prsl, dref, stsd, sdtp, trun, tenc. All finish below 0.4 ms and 0.3 MB, except the known `trun` case. Only `stsd` and `dref` differ in error behavior (finding 3).
(d) Sizes: 0, 1 with a largesize of 0, 8, 15, 16, 2^53+2 and 2^64-1, 2 to 7, a child above its parent, `uuid` with 0, 3 and 15 body bytes. All return, none throws, none is slow. The silent stop is the known finding. Only the child with size 0 is new (finding 6).
(e) A container inside `mdat`, `free` or an unknown type is not read. A container inside `dref`, `stsd`, a sample entry or `meta` is read with the generic rule and writes back to the same bytes. Nothing new beyond the known findings on `entries` and child types.
(f) Graph that contains itself: see finding 1. A graph with a shared child (2 references for each level) writes 2^levels copies (22 levels: 64 MB, 5.3 s). I do not report that, because a shared child is legal input.
64-bit modes: short 64-bit fields give the same RangeError with number, readInt64AsBigInt and createInt64OverflowReader.

Measurements for findings that are already known (not reported again):
- `trun` count: the 21 process aborts are one changed byte in the sample_count of a `trun` box with flags 0x000001 (captions_fragmented.mp4 offsets 2695 and 3486, dash-chunks-prft.m4s offset 152). Node ends with `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit` (heap limit 1024 MB), which no try/catch can handle. A count of 0x00800001 returns after 1.7 s with 510 to 550 MB. A 16-byte `trun` box with count 0x00100000 costs 77 MB. This raises the priority of the known finding.
- View for each box (RFC motivation 1): each parsed box keeps about 1.3 KB of heap. 1,000,000 boxes of 8 bytes (8 MB of input) need 1.0 to 1.6 s and 1.2 GB of heap, about 160 times the input.

confirmed.title: `compressorName` is a `number[]` of 32 raw bytes, but the spec defines a counted string.
confirmed.breakingReason: The type of a public field changes from `number[]` to `string`, and the parsed value changes.
confirmed.evidence: VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:28 `compressorName: number[]`. readVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:39 `compressorName: readArray(UINT, 1, 32)`. The test must compare 32 numbers and explains them in a comment: readAvc1.test.ts:43 `// length + 'GoPro AVC encoder'`. Spec 12.1.3.3: "Compressorname is a name, for informative purposes. It is formatted in a fixed 32-byte field, with the first byte set to the number of bytes to be displayed, followed by that number of bytes of displayable data, and then padding". An adopter who writes a box must build the length byte and the padding by hand.
confirmed.proposal: Type the field as `string`. The reader takes the first byte as the length (at most 31), decodes that many bytes, and skips the padding. The writer writes the length byte, at most 31 bytes of the string, and zero padding to 32 bytes. An empty string writes 32 zero bytes, which the spec allows ("The field may be set to 0").

One detail the proposal leaves open: the spec does not name the character encoding of the displayable bytes. The implementation must choose one (UTF-8 matches the other string fields of the package). value.reason:
The facts are correct. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:28 has `compressorName: number[]`. readVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:39 has `compressorName: readArray(UINT, 1, 32)`. writeVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:72 has `writer.writeArray(box.compressorName, UINT, 1, 32)`. The spec text 14496-12-2015.txt:9340 has `string[32] compressorname;`, and lines 9352 to 9355 define the count byte, the displayable bytes, the padding to 32 bytes, and "The field may be set to 0". test/readers/readAvc1.test.ts:36-43 and test/readers/readHvc1.test.ts:36 compare 32 raw numbers. ~/dev/dash.js/src/mss/MssFragmentMoovProcessor.js:342 builds the 32 numbers by hand. ~/dev/hls.js/src/remux/mp4-generator.ts:657 writes a count of 0, so the common streaming case is an empty name.

No prior decision exists. `git log -S'compressorName' -- libs/iso-bmff` returns only the original commits (8ac3ef9b9 CML Version 1, d615e5bf0 add iso box writers, 69489be50 alpha.3). `git log --grep compressor` returns nothing. CHANGELOG.md, the RFCs in rfc/, the docs, and the README do not mention the field. `gh issue list` and `gh pr list` with the search term `compressorName` return nothing. The array form came with the first port and nobody chose it on purpose. The proposal does not conflict with a settled decision. The package already moved its text fields to strings with a stated encoding (CHANGELOG.md:63 and :80, issues 631 and PR 643), so a string here follows the existing direction.

The proposal has three gaps. (1) The proposal does not name the encoding. The spec clause only says "displayable data". The package has two string forms: one byte for each character (IsoBoxReadView.ts:267 `readString`, IsoBoxWriteView.ts:226 `writeString`) and UTF-8 (`readUtf8`, `writeUtf8TerminatedString`). The choice changes the returned value for a name that is not ASCII, so the choice must be explicit. (2) With UTF-8, a cut at 31 bytes can split a multi-byte character. (3) A string is a normalizing form. The writer today pads a short array with 0 (IsoBoxWriteView.ts:298 `data[i] ?? 0`) and keeps any 32 bytes of the source. After the change, a source with a count above 31, with a name that has no count byte, or with padding bytes that are not 0 does not write back the same bytes. This loss is acceptable under the settled rule that no field exists only to keep bytes, but the changelog must state it.

Performance favors the change. The reader today makes 32 read calls and one array of 32 numbers for each visual sample entry. With a count of 0, a string reader makes one read call and one jump (`jump` exists at IsoBoxReadView.ts:347) and allocates nothing. src/utils/readUtf8String.ts:14 already returns '' for length 0 without a decoder call.

The wrong citation from F376 is correct and separate: VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:13 says `ISO/IEC 14496-15:2014 - 12.1.3.1`, and the clause is ISO/IEC 14496-12, 12.1.3. That fix is documentation only and does not break adopters.
value.correction:
Type the field as `compressorName: string` on `VisualSampleEntryBox` (all visual sample entry types share the type). State the encoding as UTF-8, the same rule as `hdlr`, `url `, `schm`, and `emsg` (issue 631, PR 643). A name with only ASCII characters reads and writes the same bytes with either encoding.

Reader: read the count byte, limit the count to 31, decode that many bytes, then jump over the rest of the 32 bytes. A count of 0 returns '' with no decoder call.

Writer: encode the string, keep at most 31 bytes, and remove an incomplete multi-byte sequence at the cut. Write the count of the kept bytes, the bytes, and zero padding to 32 bytes. An empty or missing string writes 32 zero bytes, so the writer does not throw for a missing field.

Changelog: state that the reader returns only the displayable name. State that a box with a count above 31, with no count byte, or with padding that is not 0 does not write back the same 32 bytes. Give the migration: replace the array of 32 numbers with the name string.

Separately, at any time: correct the citation in VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:13 to ISO/IEC 14496-12, 12.1.3.

Open question for the maintainer: UTF-8 adds the `TextEncoder` requirement to the visual sample entry writers (the same cost that CHANGELOG.md:121 records for `writeHdlr`). The alternative is one byte for each character with `readString` and `writeString`, which needs no encoder and gives wrong text for a name that is not ASCII. Measure the bundle cost of both before the choice.

confirmed.title: The package cannot express `AudioSampleEntryV1`: `entry_version` is hidden in the high half of `reserved2[0]`, there is no `srat` box, and a sample rate above 65535 writes a wrong value without an error.
confirmed.breakingReason: A new `entryVersion` field replaces part of `reserved2` in the parsed result and in the type. A range rule for `samplerate` changes the written bytes or throws.
confirmed.evidence: readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:27 `reserved2: readArray(UINT, 4, 2)`. Spec 12.2.3.2: `class AudioSampleEntryV1 ... { unsigned int(16) entry_version; // must be 1 ... const unsigned int(16)[3] reserved = 0; ... template unsigned int(32) samplerate = 1<<16; // optional boxes follow SamplingRateBox();`. So an adopter finds the entry version only with `reserved2[0] >>> 16`. `grep -i srat src` returns nothing. writeAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:58 `writer.writeTemplate(box.samplerate, 4)` and IsoBoxWriteView.ts:312 `Math.round(value * Math.pow(2, shift))` then `writeUint`. Probe with node: `samplerate: 96000` writes `77000000`, which reads back as 30464. The spec route for such a rate is `AudioSampleEntryV1` with a `srat` box.
confirmed.proposal: Add `entryVersion: number` (0 for `AudioSampleEntry`, 1 for `AudioSampleEntryV1`) when the reserved fields leave the type. Without that field, a read and a write of a V1 entry loses the version. Add a reader and a writer for `srat` (`SamplingRateBox`, one `unsigned int(32) sampling_rate`). Decide one rule for a fixed-point value that does not fit: saturate, as `writeUint` does for 64 bits, or document the wrap.

confirmed.title: Writers handle a missing field in three different ways: 0 for a number, an empty string for text, and a TypeError for an array or bytes
confirmed.breakingReason: A call that throws a TypeError today would write an empty field instead.
confirmed.evidence: A probe against src shows: writeElng with no `extendedLanguage` writes an empty string. writeEmsg version 1 with no numeric field writes zeros. writeEmsg with no `messageData` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` from `let contentSize = box.messageData.length`. writeFree with no `data` and writeFtyp with no `compatibleBrands` throw the same TypeError. writeElst with no `entries` throws `TypeError: box.entries is not iterable`. writeEmsg has `box.presentationTimeDelta ?? 0` and `box.presentationTime ?? 0`, although both fields are required in the types and the write of `undefined` already gives 0. The types mark all these fields as required, so only JavaScript callers and casts reach the difference. The settled rule says that a writer does not throw for a missing field.
confirmed.proposal: State one rule in the writing guide and apply it: a missing array or byte field is empty, as a missing number is 0. Remove the two `?? 0` defaults, or add the default to every field. The cursor API is the cheap moment for this change, because every writer is rewritten.

alsoReportedAs.title: The missing-field rule gives 0 for a number, an empty string for most strings by accident, and an unclear `TypeError` for a four-character code, a byte array, or a list.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Explicit defaults exist for some fields: `writer.writeWideUint(box.baseDataOffset ?? 0, 8)`, `encodeText(box.schemeUri ?? '')`, `encodeText(box.preselectionTag ?? '')`. Other fields have none: `encodeText(box.schemeUri)` in writeKind, `const dataSize = box.data.length` in writeMdat, `box.compatibleBrands.length * 4` in writeFtyp, `writer.writeString(box.handlerType)`, `for (const entry of box.entries)`. Read-only run of the source with a cast: `mfhd` with no `sequenceNumber` writes 0. `kind` with no `value` writes an empty string, because `new TextEncoder().encode(undefined)` returns no bytes. `mdat` with no `data` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`. `hdlr` with no `handlerType` throws the same error. The settled rule says a writer does not throw for a missing field.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: 2.0.0 states the rule for each kind of field and the field functions apply it: a missing number writes 0, a missing string writes an empty string, a missing byte array writes no bytes, a missing list writes a count of 0. A missing four-character code is the only open case. Decide between four spaces and a `RangeError` from `writeFourCc`. Document the rule one time in the writing guide.

The box has one byte for each sample, so a view costs no allocation for each sample, and the writer becomes one `writeBytes` call (IsoBoxWriteView.ts:268). The decoded alternative allocates one object for each sample and conflicts with priority 1. The fix breaks adopters: `Uint8Array` is not assignable to `number[]`, `Array.isArray` and JSON output change, and a writer caller that passes `number[]` no longer compiles. value.correction: Choose the `Uint8Array` form and drop the decoded alternative. The facts hold. The proposal needs three adjustments.

1. `IsoBox<V>` alone is the wrong child type for sample entries. src/IsoBoxMap.ts has `sinf` (line 164) and has no `avcC`, `esds`, `hvcC`, `btrt` or `pasp`. Most real children of a sample entry are therefore outside the `IsoBox` union. The raw box member of the cursor RFC (`IsoRawBox`, rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:159) is required, not optional: `boxes: (IsoBox<V> | IsoRawBox)[]`. The sample entry types then need a `V` parameter.

2. `IsoBoxWriter<any>` in IsoBoxWriterMap cannot become `IsoBoxWriter<unknown>`. The box is a function parameter, so a writer of one box type is not assignable to a writer of `unknown`. Use a mapped type over IsoBoxMap with an index fallback, or `IsoBoxWriter<never>`, or keep `any` with a lint exemption. The cursor RFC keeps the name IsoBoxWriterMap (line 154), so this position stays in 2.0.0.

The names appear only in the type files, IsoBoxMap.ts:128 and 162, SampleTableBox.ts:31 and ProtectionSchemeInformationBox.ts:13. The package never produces `ipmpDescr` or `entries`. fact.reason:
The core defect is real at HEAD 8ce63c212. I reproduced every factual statement.

Code read:
- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts:63 is `ParsedBox<([string] extends [R] ? IsoBox<V> : Exclude<IsoBox<V>, { type: R }>) | Box, V>`. Every built-in type without a reader key stays in the union.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/ParsedIsoBox.ts:11 is `ParsedBox<IsoBox<V> | Box, V>`. libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBox.ts makes `IsoBox` every value of `IsoBoxMap`.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:463-467 assigns fields only inside `if (parser) { Object.assign(box, parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type)) }`.
- libs/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md:8 has the quoted sentence "By default, the function reads only the box header."
- rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:168 says "The signature does not change". Line 191 says `isIsoBoxType` does not change. Line 159 declares `type IsoRawBox = { type: IsoBoxType; bytes: Uint8Array }`.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/isIsoBoxType.ts:38 tests only `box.type === type`, so a raw `mdat` box would pass the guard.

Type check (repo tsc, strict, scratch file outside the repo, imports from src): all of these compile. `readIsoBoxes(data, { readers: { tfdt: readTfdt } })` then `b.type === 'trun'` gives `b.sampleCount: number`. `readIsoBoxes(data)` gives `tfdt.baseMediaDecodeTime: number` and `ftyp.majorBrand: string`. `readIsoBoxes(data, defaultReaderConfig())` gives `senc.sampleCount: number`. A `@ts-expect-error` line on a field that does not exist passed, so the check was active.

Run time (node on src, fixture libs/iso-bmff/test/fixtures/test_frag.mp4): with no readers the tfdt box has the keys `size, type, view` and `baseMediaDecodeTime` is undefined. With only a tfdt reader the trun box has the keys `size, type, view` and `sampleCount` is undefined.

The 18 map entries without a reader file also hold: co64, hmhd, iinf, iloc, imif, infe, ipro, iref, nmhd, pitm, saio, saiz, sbgp, senc, sgpd, stdp, stsh, stz2.

Two details are wrong.
1. A call with no config selects the second overload (libs/iso-bmff/src/readIsoBoxes.ts:44-49, `ParsedIsoBox<V>[]`), not the signature at line 63. The type is the same, so the conclusion holds.
2. The proposal as written breaks the main narrowing pattern. See the correction.

The breaking reason is also too narrow. Correct code breaks too: a config in a variable of the type `IsoBoxReadViewConfig` has no literal keys, so its result loses every built-in type. The test at libs/iso-bmff/test/readIsoBoxes.test.ts:87-103 asserts today's behavior for a key that is not a literal and must change.

Severity high is defensible: the compiler accepts a field read that returns undefined, against the rule "Incorrect usage should fail at compile time".
fact.correction:
The proposal adds one `IsoRawBox` member with `type: IsoBoxType` to the result union. `IsoBoxType` is a template string type that accepts any 4-character literal (libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxType.ts). I tested the shape with tsc: for `Tfdt | Moof | IsoRawBox`, the check `a.type === 'tfdt'` narrows to `Tfdt | IsoRawBox`, and `a.baseMediaDecodeTime` fails with TS2339. So the proposal would break `box.type === 'tfdt'` for every box that has a reader. The current code avoids this with `Box<never>` (`type: never`).

Corrected proposal: build the union from the map, and give each built-in type without a reader its own raw member, `{ type: K; bytes: Uint8Array }` for each `K` in `Exclude<keyof IsoBoxMap, keyof R | container types>`. I tested that shape: `b.type === 'tfdt'` narrows to the reader result alone, and `b.type === 'trun'` narrows to the raw member with `bytes`. Keep one member with `type: never` for types outside `IsoBoxMap`, as `Box` does today. Decide separately what a map without literal keys returns (a config in a variable of the type `IsoBoxReadViewConfig`). That case needs either `isIsoBoxType` plus a `'bytes' in box` test, or the present fallback to every built-in type.

Also correct the cited line: a call with no config resolves to the overload at readIsoBoxes.ts:44-49, not line 63.
fact.priorDecision: No decision states that a box without a reader should keep its full built-in type. The accepted RFC rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:360 ("The default union", PR 614) documents the present state: `ParsedIsoBox` includes every built-in box type, PR 614 excludes only the types that a required reader key replaces, and "When a key is not a literal, every built-in type stays." The test libs/iso-bmff/test/readIsoBoxes.test.ts:87 ("should keep the built-in box types when the reader map has no literal keys") and the TSDoc at libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts:25-26 pin that fallback. These describe the inherited union and do not defend the typed fields of a box that no reader decoded.

value.reason:
The facts hold. libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts:63 adds `Exclude<IsoBox<V>, { type: R }>` to the union, and libs/iso-bmff/src/ParsedIsoBox.ts:11 is `ParsedBox<IsoBox<V> | Box, V>`. libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:463-467 only runs `Object.assign(box, parser(...))` when the map has a reader. libs/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md:8 states the run-time rule ("reads only the box header"). So a typed field of a box with no reader is undefined at run time. No reader file exists for senc, saio, saiz, sbgp, sgpd, co64, stz2 (ls src/readers).

Prior decisions: I found none that chooses this state on purpose. PR 614 (8d0b4b393) only removed the built-in type of a box whose reader the map replaces. Its description says a computed key leaves the result "the same as today", and libs/iso-bmff/test/readIsoBoxes.test.ts:87-103 pins that fallback. rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:360 describes the same scope. Neither text weighs the fields of a box with no reader. `gh issue list` and `gh pr list` for IsoBoxReaderReturn and the return type returned no issue on this point. The change breaks no settled decision. rfc/iso-bmff-container-readers-writers.md:150 only requires that a `moov` box still narrows to `MovieBox`, and the proposal keeps the container types.

The proposal is incomplete in three places. (1) The container types hold their children as static built-in types: libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/TrackFragmentBox.ts:15-22 lists `TrackFragmentBaseMediaDecodeTimeBox<V> | TrackRunBox | SampleEncryptionBox ...`, and MovieFragmentBox.ts:10-12 the same. tfdt, trun, tfhd, mvhd, and mdhd are nested boxes, so a fix of the top-level union alone leaves the main case wrong. (2) rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:159 types the raw box as `{ type: IsoBoxType; bytes }`, and IsoBoxType is a template of four strings (src/IsoBoxType.ts). `box.type === 'tfdt'` then keeps the raw box in the union, so correct code with a registered reader also stops compiling. The guide uses that pattern at docs/reading-boxes.md:79, 134, 157. (3) rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:168 says "The signature does not change", which is false once raw boxes exist. The RFC needs the new result type.

The change is type-only, with no run-time or bundle cost except one `in` check in the guard. No built-in box type has a `bytes` field (grep of src/boxes), so that field is a safe discriminator.
value.correction:
Put the result type in the cursor RFC and replace the line "The signature does not change" (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:168).

1. Top level: the union is the return type of each reader in the map, the container types, and `IsoRawBox`. Remove the `Exclude<IsoBox<V>, { type: R }>` member. If the reader keys are not literal (a plain `IsoBoxReadViewConfig`, a computed key), the union is `IsoBox<V> | IsoRawBox`.

2. Nested boxes: add `IsoRawBox` to every child union of the container types (`MovieFragmentBoxChild`, `TrackFragmentBoxChild`, and the others). That type is also true for the writer, because `writeIsoBoxes` copies a raw child. Do not make the 38 container types generic on the reader map. The recursive type costs compile time and makes error messages hard to read.

3. Narrowing: `IsoRawBox.type` is a string, so `box.type === 'tfdt'` gives `TrackFragmentBaseMediaDecodeTimeBox | IsoRawBox`, and a field access is a compile error until the code excludes the raw box. Make `isIsoBoxType(type, box)` return `false` for a value with a `bytes` field, and add a guard `isIsoRawBox(box)` for the raw case (or document `'bytes' in box`). Rewrite the guide examples at docs/reading-boxes.md:79, 134, 157 with the guard. Decide this point in the RFC, because it changes the documented pattern for correct code.

4. `defaultReaderConfig()` may return a type with literal reader keys. The existing helper inside `IsoBoxReaderReturn` (rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:344-358) already maps a generic reader in a variable to the `V` fields. The declaration file grows by about 60 entries.

5. The 18 entries of `IsoBoxMap` with no reader and no writer are a separate finding. Decide them there.

For `MetaBoxChild` and `MovieExtendsBoxChild`, where the spec permits boxes that the package has no type for (`other_boxes[]`, `leva`, `trep`), use the same open form as udta, meco, grpl, and strk: `IsoBox<V>` plus the raw box type of version 2. alsoReportedAs.title: SchemeInformationBoxChild allows only TrackEncryptionBox, but the spec allows any box in `schi`.

The same box type is also a child of `rinf` and `srpp`. readSchi.ts:23 returns every child box that the view finds, `view.readBoxes<SchemeInformationBoxChild>()`, so the type claims `tenc` for a child of any type.

alsoReportedAs.title: `SampleTableBoxChild` omits five box types that the spec places in `stbl` and that `IsoBoxMap` has, so a type test for them does not compile.

IsoBoxMap.ts has `co64: ChunkLargeOffsetBox` (:106), `saio` (:155), `saiz` (:156), `subs` (:181), `stz2: CompactSampleSizeBox` (:182). The 2015 spec text gives `Container: Sample Table Box ('stbl')` for 'stsz', 'stz2' (line 3207), 'stco', 'co64' (line 3329), 'subs' (3410), 'saiz' (3493), 'saio' (3588). alsoReportedAs.proposal: Add `ChunkLargeOffsetBox`, `CompactSampleSizeBox`, `SubsampleInformationBox`, `SampleAuxiliaryInformationSizesBox`, and `SampleAuxiliaryInformationOffsetsBox` to `SampleTableBoxChild`. `TrackFragmentBoxChild` already has the last three. The spec also lists `cslg` and `padb`, but the package has no type for them.

alsoReportedAs.title: `WebVttCueChild` omits `WebVttSettingsBox`, so the type of a `vttc` box rejects its own `sttg` child.

Scratch type check with tsc 6: `vttc.boxes.find(b => b.type === 'sttg')` fails with `TS2367 ... '"iden" | "payl"' and '"sttg"' have no overlap`. The fixture `vttc.mp4` has a `vttc` box with a `sttg` child (writeSttg.test.ts:55-60). The text of ISO/IEC 14496-30 was not available, so the full child list of `vttc` is not confirmed from the spec.

alsoReportedAs.title: The child unions of `traf` and `trak` are closed and omit boxes that the spec allows in those containers.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: TrackFragmentBox.ts:15-22 lists `tfhd`, `tfdt`, `trun`, `saiz`, `saio`, `senc`, `subs`. Spec 14496-12:2015 also names `traf` as a container for `sbgp` (8.9.2, 'Sample Table Box (stbl) or Track Fragment Box (traf)'), `sgpd` (8.9.3), `udta` (8.10.1), and `meta` (8.11.1). The package has the types `SampleToGroupBox`, `SampleGroupDescriptionBox`, `UserDataBox`, and `MetaBox`. TrackBox.ts:13-18 lists `tkhd`, `tref`, `edts`, `mdia`, `udta`. By the type declaration, `{ type: 'traf', boxes: [tfhd, sbgp] }` does not compile, and a comparison `child.type === 'sgpd'` is an error for no overlap. Encrypted CMAF content with key rotation has `sbgp` and `sgpd` in `traf`. Four other containers already use the open form: `UserDataBoxChild<V> = IsoBox<V>` (also `meco`, `grpl`, `strk`).
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Use one rule for every container in 2.0.0. Preferred: `boxes: (IsoBox<V> | IsoRawBox)[]` for all containers, because real files contain vendor boxes and unknown boxes in any container, and the reader returns them. If the closed unions stay, add the missing types from the spec to `TrackFragmentBoxChild` (`sbgp`, `sgpd`, `udta`, `meta`) and to `TrackBoxChild` (`meta`, `meco`), and add the raw box type to both.

alsoReportedAs.title: The child type of the `vttc` box omits the `sttg` box and its name `WebVttCueChild` does not follow the `<Box>Child` pattern.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: WebVttCueBox.ts:9 `export type WebVttCueChild = WebVttCueIdBox | WebVttCuePayloadBox`. A typed `vttc` box with an `sttg` child does not compile, and `child.type === 'sttg'` is a type error on a parsed `vttc` box. Every other container child type ends in `BoxChild` (`UserDataBoxChild`, `TrackFragmentBoxChild`, `MovieBoxChild`, 25 in total). `WebVttCueChild` is the only exception.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Rename to `WebVttCueBoxChild` and define it as `WebVttCueIdBox | WebVttSettingsBox | WebVttCuePayloadBox`. The text of ISO/IEC 14496-30 was not available for this audit. Check that text for the other children of the cue box (the package has no type for `vsid` or `ctim`) before the union is final.

alsoReportedAs.title: The types of the `moof` and `traf` children do not allow a `udta` box, and the spec lists both as containers of `udta`.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015, 8.10.1.1: `Container: Movie Box ('moov'), Track Box ('trak'), Movie Fragment Box ('moof') or Track Fragment Box ('traf')`. MovieBox.ts:16 and TrackBox.ts:18 have `| UserDataBox<V>`. MovieFragmentBox.ts:10-12 is `MovieFragmentHeaderBox | TrackFragmentBox<V>`, and TrackFragmentBox.ts:15-22 lists seven types with no `UserDataBox`. A typed `moof` or `traf` box with a `udta` child does not compile for `writeIsoBoxes`, and `child.type === 'udta'` is a type error on a parsed `traf`.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Add `UserDataBox<V>` to `MovieFragmentBoxChild<V>` and `TrackFragmentBoxChild<V>`.

alsoReportedAs.title: The child unions of the container types are closed, so a valid child box type is a compile error
alsoReportedAs.evidence: `MovieBoxChild = MovieHeaderBox | TrackBox | MovieExtendsBox | UserDataBox`. tsc reports TS2367 `types '"mvex" | "mvhd" | "trak" | "udta"' and '"pssh"' have no overlap` for `child.type === 'pssh'`. The same error occurs for `meta` in `moov`, `elng` in `mdia`, `co64`, `stz2`, and `subs` in `stbl`, `sbgp` in `traf`, and `sttg` in `vttc`. The specs allow each: 23001-7 `pssh` Container `Movie ('moov') or Movie Fragment ('moof')`. 14496-12 `elng` Container `Media Box`, `meta` Container `File, Movie Box, Track Box, ...`, `subs`, `saiz`, `saio`, `sbgp`, `sgpd` Container `Sample Table Box or Track Fragment Box`, and `free`, `skip` Container `File or other box`. `co64` and `stz2` are keys of IsoBoxMap and are in no child union. Four containers already use the open form: `UserDataBoxChild<V> = IsoBox<V>`. The 14496-30 text was not available, so the `vttc` case rests on the package's own `readSttg`.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Give every container `boxes: IsoBox<V>[]`, as `udta`, `grpl`, `meco`, and `strk` have today. Remove the 26 `*Child` types, or keep each as an alias of `IsoBox<V>`. If the name stays, rename `WebVttCueChild` to `WebVttCueBoxChild` to match the other 25. A closed list per container cannot be correct, because `free`, `skip`, and `uuid` are valid in any container.

alsoReportedAs.title: SampleDescriptionBox and DataReferenceBox type their entries as a closed list, and other entries arrive as raw boxes
alsoReportedAs.evidence: `E extends SampleEntryBox = AudioSampleEntryBox | VisualSampleEntryBox`, and the two defaults cover nine types: `'mp4a' | 'enca'` and `'avc1' | ... | 'encv'`. `e.type === 'av01'` on `stsd.entries` is TS2367 (checked with tsc). Both are raw boxes with no `width` or `channelcount`, and the type says they have those fields.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Type the default as `entries: IsoBox<V>[]` plus the raw box type of version 2.0.0, or derive it from the reader map. Keep `E` for a caller that knows the entry type.

alsoReportedAs.title: The closed `<Box>Child` unions omit child boxes that the spec allows, so a valid `type` check on a child is a compile error.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: `TrackFragmentBoxChild` lists tfhd, tfdt, trun, saiz, saio, senc, subs. PR 659 already made the children of udta, strk, grpl, and meco `IsoBox<V>`.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Type the children of every container as `IsoBox<V>` (plus the raw box of the RFC), as the four boxes of PR 659 already do. Then remove the `*Child` aliases, or keep one generic alias. A closed union cannot stay correct, because the readers map decides what a child is.

alsoReportedAs.title: The element type of `boxes` has three conventions, and the closed child unions reject child boxes that the spec allows.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: (1) Closed union, 19 types (dinf, edts, iinf, ipro, iref, mdia, minf, meta, moov, mvex, moof, mfra, sinf, schi, stbl, traf, trak, tref, vttc). Example: `MovieBoxChild = MovieHeaderBox<V> | TrackBox<V> | MovieExtendsBox<V> | UserDataBox<V>`. (2) `IsoBox<V>`, 4 types (udta, grpl, strk, meco): `UserDataBoxChild<V> = IsoBox<V>`. (3) `any`, 3 types plus the base: `AudioSampleEntryBoxChild = any`, `VisualSampleEntryBoxChild = any`, `PreselectionGroupBoxChild = any` with the comment `// TODO: Find documentation on what children are allowed`, and `SampleEntryBox<T, C = any>`. The closed unions are narrower than the spec. ISO/IEC 23001-7:2016 clause 8.1.1: pssh `Container: Movie ('moov') or Movie Fragment ('moof')`, but `MovieBoxChild` and `MovieFragmentBoxChild` have no pssh. ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 clause 8.11.1: meta `Container: File, Movie Box ('moov'), Track Box ('trak'), ... Movie Fragment Box ('moof') or Track Fragment Box ('traf')`, but none of those unions has meta. Clause 8.7.7: subs `Container: Sample Table Box ('stbl') or Track Fragment Box ('traf')`, and saiz the same, but `SampleTableBoxChild` has neither, and also lacks co64 and stz2, which have types in the package. `SchemeInformationBoxChild = TrackEncryptionBox` only. The reader puts every child in `boxes` at run time. A test such as `child.type === 'pssh'` on a `moov` child should be the TypeScript error for a comparison with no overlap. I did not compile that line.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: One rule for every box with child boxes: `boxes: IsoBox<V>[]`, the rule that issue 646 already applied to udta, grpl, strk, and meco. With the RFC, the element type is `IsoBox<V> | IsoRawBox`. Replace the three `any` aliases with the same type. Either delete the 26 `*Child` aliases or keep them only as documentation of the usual children.

alsoReportedAs.title: The child unions of moov, moof, traf and stsd omit boxes that the specs allow there and that players read, so a correct lookup does not compile.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: MovieBoxChild is `MovieHeaderBox | TrackBox | MovieExtendsBox | UserDataBox`. MovieFragmentBoxChild is `MovieFragmentHeaderBox | TrackFragmentBox`. tsc reports TS2367 for `box.boxes.find(child => child.type === 'pssh')` on a moov box and on a moof box, for `child.type === 'meta'` on moov, and for `c.type === 'sbgp'` on a traf box. ISO/IEC 23001-7:2016 states for pssh "Container: Movie ('moov') or Movie Fragment ('moof')". ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 states for sbgp and sgpd "Container: Sample Table Box ('stbl') or Track Fragment Box ('traf')". The stsd entry union is `AudioSampleEntryBox | VisualSampleEntryBox` with nine literal types, so `e.type === 'av01'` and `e.type === 'ec-3'` are TS2367 too. dash.js reads pssh from moov (src/mss/MssFragmentMoovProcessor.js), and shaka-player registers 'pssh' four times.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Add pssh and meta to MovieBoxChild, pssh and meta to MovieFragmentBoxChild, and sbgp and sgpd to TrackFragmentBoxChild. Add the raw box type to every child union, so a child of a type that the package does not name still compiles. Widening a union is not a break for code that reads the listed children.

fact.reason:
Core problem holds at HEAD 8ce63c212. Two counts and the breaking analysis are wrong.

Confirmed in src:
