- MovieFragmentBox.ts:10-12 (mfhd, traf). TrackBox.ts:13-18 (tkhd, tref, edts, mdia, udta). MediaBox.ts:11-14 (mdhd, hdlr, minf). TrackFragmentBox.ts:15-22 (tfhd, tfdt, trun, saiz, saio, senc, subs). SampleTableBox.ts:19-31 (12 types, no co64, stz2, subs, saiz, saio). MetaBox.ts:17-25 (8 types). SchemeInformationBox.ts:8 `= TrackEncryptionBox`. WebVttCueBox.ts:9 `WebVttCueIdBox | WebVttCuePayloadBox`. SampleDescriptionBox.ts:12 default `AudioSampleEntryBox | VisualSampleEntryBox`. DataReferenceBox.ts:13 `(DataEntryUrlBox | DataEntryUrnBox)[]`.
- IsoBoxMap.ts has co64 (:106), elng (:111), meta (:139), pssh (:154), saio (:155), saiz (:156), sbgp (:157), senc (:161), sgpd (:162), sttg (:178), subs (:181), stz2 (:182).
- Only UserDataBox.ts:9, GroupsListBox.ts:9, SubTrackBox.ts:9, AdditionalMetadataContainerBox.ts:9 are `IsoBox<V>`.
- Run time: IsoBoxReadView.ts:456-474 yields every box, with a reader or without one, and readBoxes (:414-422) casts with `box as T`. readMoov.ts:23 and readSchi.ts:23 call `view.readBoxes<...Child>()`. So the closed type is a cast, not a check.
- test/readers/readSttg.test.ts:19 needs `(boxes[1].boxes[1] as WebVttSettingsBox).settings`.

Confirmed in the spec text:
- 23001-7:2016 line 639-640, 8.1.1 pssh `Container: Movie ('moov') or Movie Fragment ('moof')`. Line 564-565, 7.2.1 senc `Container: Track Fragment Box ('traf') or Track Box ('trak')`.
- 14496-12:2015 line 4841-4844, 8.11.1.1 meta container list includes moov, trak, meco, moof, traf. Line 2307, 8.4.6.1 elng in mdia. Lines 4420 and 4485, 8.9.2 and 8.9.3 sbgp and sgpd in stbl or traf. Lines 3207, 3329, 3410, 3493, 3588 for stz2, co64, subs, saiz, saio in stbl.

Confirmed with tsc 6.0.3 (--noEmit, scratch file outside the repo, imports from src): TS2367 for 'pssh' and 'meta' on a moov child with the exact quoted message, 'pssh' on moof, 'meta' and 'senc' on trak, 'elng' on mdia, 'sbgp' and 'sgpd' on traf, 'co64', 'stz2', 'subs', 'saiz', 'saio' on stbl, 'sttg' on vttc, 'av01' on stsd entries, and a non-url type on dref entries.

Wrong details:
1. "24 exported *Child aliases" is wrong. `grep "export type .*Child"` in src gives 26, and config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md has 26. Split: 19 closed, 4 `IsoBox<V>`, 3 `any` (AudioSampleEntryBoxChild, VisualSampleEntryBoxChild, PreselectionGroupBoxChild). The finding does not mention the 3 `any` aliases.
2. The title says 12 containers. The files list has 11 entries, and 2 of them (stsd, dref) have `entries`, not `boxes`. The closed-union problem applies to all 19 closed aliases, not only the ones named.
3. `IsoRawBox` does not exist in src. The name exists only in rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:159 as `{ type: IsoBoxType; bytes: Uint8Array }`, and IsoBoxType.ts:6 is a template string type that accepts any string.
4. The breaking reason understates the break. I checked with tsc: with `(IsoBox | IsoRawBox)[]`, the line `if (c.type === 'tfdt') c.baseMediaDecodeTime` fails with TS2339 (`Property 'baseMediaDecodeTime' does not exist on type 'IsoRawBox | TrackFragmentBaseMediaDecodeTimeBox<number>'`). With `IsoBox[]` alone the same line compiles. So the proposed type breaks every field read after a `type` test, not only exhaustive switches.

No prior decision keeps the closed unions on purpose. Issue 646 and PR 659 only replaced `any` with `IsoBox<V>` on four boxes and did not rule on the other 19.
fact.correction:
The package exports 26 `*Child` aliases, not 24: 19 closed unions (dinf, edts, iinf, ipro, iref, mdia, minf, meta, moov, mvex, moof, mfra, sinf, schi, stbl, traf, trak, tref, vttc), 4 `IsoBox<V>` (udta, grpl, strk, meco), and 3 `any` (AudioSampleEntryBoxChild, VisualSampleEntryBoxChild, PreselectionGroupBoxChild). The rule must cover all 26, plus the `entries` of stsd and dref.

Corrected proposal: split the two steps, because their break sizes differ.
(a) `boxes: IsoBox<V>[]` for every container. This step only widens the union. `child.type === 'tfdt'` still narrows, so the break is limited to exhaustive switches and to code that reads a field with no type test. It also replaces the 3 `any` aliases with a checked type.
(b) Adding `IsoRawBox` to the element type is a much larger break. `IsoRawBox.type` is `IsoBoxType`, which accepts any string, so `child.type === 'tfdt'` no longer removes the raw member and every field read after a type test fails with TS2339. If the RFC adds the raw box to child lists, it needs a narrowing path that still works, for example `isIsoBoxType('tfdt', child)` as the documented form, or a raw box type whose `type` excludes `keyof IsoBoxMap`. Decide this in the cursor RFC, not as a side effect of this finding.

`IsoRawBox` is an RFC name only (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:159). It is not in src today.

value.reason:
The facts are right. I read the 13 box files. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/MovieBox.ts:12-16 is `MovieHeaderBox<V> | TrackBox<V> | MovieExtendsBox<V> | UserDataBox<V>`. MovieFragmentBox.ts:10-12, TrackBox.ts:13-18, MediaBox.ts:11-14, TrackFragmentBox.ts:15-22, SampleTableBox.ts:19-31, MetaBox.ts:17-25, SchemeInformationBox.ts:8 (`= TrackEncryptionBox`), WebVttCueBox.ts:9 (`WebVttCueIdBox | WebVttCuePayloadBox`), SampleDescriptionBox.ts:12 and DataReferenceBox.ts:13 are closed lists. UserDataBox.ts:9 is `IsoBox<V>`. The spec text agrees with the finding: 23001-7-2016.txt:640 (pssh in moov or moof), 14496-12-2015.txt:2307-2308 (elng in mdia), 4420-4421 and 4485-4486 (sbgp, sgpd in stbl or traf), 4635-4637 (udta in moov, trak, moof, traf), 4841-4844 (meta), 1720-1721 (free, skip in "File or other box"), 5759-5760 (`Box scheme_specific_data[]` in schi). The run time is open: IsoBoxReadView.ts:414-430 `readBoxes` pushes every box with `box as T`, and readSchi.ts:23 and readStsd.ts:28 pass the closed type as `T`. A scratch type check with tsc 6.0.3 against src (file <scratchpad>/f189/probe.ts) gave TS2367 for `c.type === 'pssh'` on a moov child, and no error for the same test on a udta child.

Prior decisions: none makes the closed lists intentional. The lists come from d615e5bf0 (2025-12-30, "feat: add iso box writers"). PR 659 (1337aaed4, issue 646) changed udta, grpl, strk and meco from `any` to `IsoBox<V>` and left the other containers out of scope. Its text says only that the typed containers "already reject the same three kinds of code". PR 659 is a precedent for the open form, not against it. rfc/iso-bmff-container-readers-writers.md does not state a rule for child types. The proposal breaks no settled decision.

The proposal needs one change. The same probe shows that the literal type `IsoBox<V> | IsoRawBox`, with `IsoRawBox = { type: IsoBoxType; bytes: Uint8Array }` from rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:159, breaks the common test. `if (child.type === 'tfdt') child.baseMediaDecodeTime` fails with TS2339, "does not exist on type 'TrackFragmentBaseMediaDecodeTimeBox<number> | IsoRawBox'". `IsoBoxType` is a template string type (IsoBoxType.ts:6), so the raw member stays after the comparison. `isIsoBoxType('tfdt', child)` narrows correctly, and a raw member with `type: never` narrows correctly too. Version 1 already uses that second form at the top level: Box.ts:8 `Box<T extends IsoBoxType = never>` inside ParsedIsoBox.ts:11.

Other corrections: the API report has 26 `*Child` aliases, not 24 (config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md, 26 lines match `export type .*Child`). Three of them are `any` (AudioSampleEntryBox.ts:10, VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:10, PreselectionGroupBox.ts:10). No README or guide uses an alias. Only 23 reader files and one test use them. One cost exists: an open container accepts a wrong child at compile time. The probe compiled `{ type: 'udta', boxes: [mfhd] }`. That cost is small, because the lists are wrong today and no writer validates children.

Break for adopters, at compile time only: a field read on a child with no type test (`schi.boxes[0].defaultKID` compiles today), an exhaustive switch with a `never` default, and every import of an alias name. No run-time value, written byte, or bundle size changes.
value.correction: Use one element type for every `boxes` array, and make that type the same type that `readIsoBoxes` returns at the top level. Do not write `IsoBox<V> | IsoRawBox` with the raw type of the RFC as it stands: `IsoRawBox.type` is `IsoBoxType`, so `child.type === 'tfdt'` no longer narrows to the typed box (TS2339 in a scratch check with tsc 6.0.3). Two forms keep the narrowing. (1) `boxes: IsoBox<V>[]`, the rule of PR 659, with the raw box found by `'bytes' in child`. (2) A raw member whose `type` is `never`, as `Box<never>` is in `ParsedIsoBox` today. The cursor RFC must decide the form once, for the top level and for children together, and document `isIsoBoxType` as the guard that works in both forms. Delete the 26 exported `*Child` aliases (not 24) in 2.0.0 with no deprecated copies, including the three `any` aliases and the name `WebVttCueChild`. Keep the `E` parameter of `SampleDescriptionBox` and `readStsd` for a caller that knows the entry type, and change only the default to the open element type. Apply the same default to the entries of `dref`. State in the changelog the three kinds of code that stop compiling: a field read on a child with no type test, an exhaustive switch over child types, and an import of an alias name.

confirmed.title: Twenty-four box types have a required count field that duplicates an array length, and the writers use three different rules for it.
confirmed.breakingReason: The count fields leave the public types and the reader results. A writer writes the array length, so a box whose count and array disagree writes other bytes.
confirmed.evidence: Pattern count plus array, with a reader: stco, ctts, stts, elst, dref, stsd, stsc, stss, subs, ssix, tfra, trun, prsl (`numEntitiesInGroup`), pssh (`kidCount`, `dataSize`). With no reader: co64, stz2, iloc, iinf, ipro, saio, senc, sgpd, sbgp, stsh. Nested entry types: `SubsampleEntry.subsampleCount`, `Subsegment.rangesCount`, `SingleItemTypeReferenceBox.referenceCount`. Lists with no count field: sidx `references`, ftyp and styp `compatibleBrands`, sdtp, stdp, `ItemLocation.extents`, `EncryptedSample.subsampleEncryption`. Rule 1, 12 writers size the buffer from the count and loop over the array: writeTrun.ts:28 `const samplesSize = sampleSize * box.sampleCount` then `for (const sample of box.samples)` (also ctts, elst, pssh, prsl, ssix, stco, stss, subs, stsc, tfra, stts). Rule 2, writeStsd.ts:23 and writeDref.ts:20 use `box.entries.length` and ignore the required `entryCount`. Rule 3, sidx has no count field. Checked with node: stts with `entryCount: 1` and 2 entries throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`. With `entryCount: 3` and 2 entries the writer writes a third entry of zeros. stsd with `entryCount: 99, entries: []` writes a count of 0.
confirmed.proposal: Remove every count field that equals an array length. The reader reads the count and returns only the array. The writer writes `array.length`. Keep `sampleCount` in stsz, stz2, and saiz, because the box has no array when the default size is not 0. Decide ctts of version 2 or above separately: the settled rule keeps `entryCount` with an empty `entries` list there. tenc `defaultConstantIvSize` follows the rule of PR 658 and stays.

alsoReportedAs.title: `entryCount` duplicates `entries.length`, and the writers disagree on which one they write: `writeCtts` uses `entryCount`, `writeDref` ignores it.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeCtts.ts:22 `const entriesSize = hasEntries ? box.entryCount * 8 : 0`, line 28 `writer.writeUint(box.entryCount, 4)`, line 31 `for (const entry of box.entries)`. writeDref.ts:20 `const entryCount = box.entries.length` and `box.entryCount` is never read. Probe with node on the source: `writeCtts({version: 0, entryCount: 1, entries: [a, b]})` throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`. `writeCtts({version: 0, entryCount: 2, entries: [a]})` writes `entry_count` 2 and one entry of zero bytes. `writeDref({entryCount: 5, entries: []})` writes `entry_count` 0. The same split exists outside my scope: `writeElst`, `writeStsc`, `writeStco`, `writeStss`, `writeStts`, `writeSubs` write `box.entryCount`, and `writeStsd` and `writeSidx` write the array length.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: One rule for the package: a writer writes the length of the list as `entry_count`. Remove `entryCount` from `DataReferenceBox`. For `ctts`, keep `entryCount` only as an optional field that the writer uses for version 2 or above, where the syntax has no entries (settled rule of issue 670). For version 0 and 1 the writer writes `entries.length`. Document the migration: delete `entryCount` from box literals.

alsoReportedAs.title: EditListBox.entryCount duplicates entries.length, and writeElst trusts the count for the size and the count field while it loops over entries
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Type: `entryCount: number` next to `entries: EditListEntry<V>[]`. Writer: `const entriesSize = box.entryCount * entrySize`, `writer.writeUint(box.entryCount, 4)`, then `for (const entry of box.entries)`. A probe against src confirms both failures. With entryCount 1 and two entries, writeElst throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`. With entryCount 2 and one entry, it writes entry_count 2 and 12 zero bytes, which a reader returns as a second entry. writeStsd and writeDref already ignore the field: `const entryCount = box.entries.length`. The same trust in entryCount appears in writeStts.ts:19, writeStco.ts:19, writeStss.ts:19, writeStsc.ts:19 (outside this scope).
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Remove `entryCount` from `EditListBox`. readElst uses the count only to size the loop. writeElst writes `box.entries.length`. If the field must stay, make it optional and make the writer ignore it, as writeStsd and writeDref do. Apply one rule to every box with a count next to an array. ctts version 2 or above is the known exception, because that box keeps a count with no entries.

alsoReportedAs.title: The count fields of pssh and prsl duplicate an array length, and the writers trust the count over the array.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writePssh.ts:36-37 `writer.writeUint(box.kidCount, 4)` then `writer.writeArray(box.kid, UINT, 1, kidSize)` with `kidSize = box.kidCount * 16`. writeArray pads with `data[i] ?? 0` (IsoBoxWriteView.ts:298). So `kidCount: 1, kid: []` writes a KID of 16 zero bytes, and `dataSize: 0, data: [1,2,3,4]` writes no Data. No error reaches the caller. writePrsl.ts:32 computes `entitiesSize = box.numEntitiesInGroup * 4`, but line 55 loops `for (const entity of box.entities)`. With more entities than the count, the DataView throws a RangeError. With fewer entities, the box has zero bytes at its end and the tags move into the entity list. writeSidx.ts:49 already does the correct thing: `writer.writeUint(box.references.length, 2)`, and SegmentIndexBox has no count field.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Remove `kidCount` and `dataSize` from ProtectionSystemSpecificHeaderBox and `numEntitiesInGroup` from PreselectionGroupBox. The reader uses the count only to read the array. The writer writes the array length, as writeSidx does. The same pattern exists in other boxes (`entryCount` in stco, elst, ssix, `sampleCount` in trun), so apply one rule to the whole package.

alsoReportedAs.title: Six writers take the size and the count from a count field but loop over the array, so a mismatch throws a raw RangeError or writes a box that contradicts itself.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeStco.ts:19 `const entriesSize = box.entryCount * 4`, :25 `writer.writeUint(box.entryCount, 4)`, :27 `for (const offset of box.chunkOffset)`. writeStsc, writeStss, writeStts have the same three lines. writeSsix.ts:23 `rangesSize += subsegment.rangesCount * 4` and :31 `writer.writeUint(box.subsegmentCount, 4)`, but both loops iterate the arrays. writeStsz.ts:20 `box.sampleSize === 0 ? box.sampleCount * 4 : 0`, :31 `for (const size of box.entrySize)`. In contrast writeStsd.ts:23 `const entryCount = box.entries.length` ignores `box.entryCount`, and `SegmentIndexBox` has no `referenceCount` field at all (writeSidx.ts:49 writes `box.references.length`). Scratch probe against src (node, no repo change): stco `entryCount: 2` with 3 offsets throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`. stco `entryCount: 3` with 2 offsets writes a third offset of 0. ssix `subsegmentCount: 5` with 1 subsegment writes a 24-byte box whose count field is 5. stss `entryCount: 0` with 1 entry throws the same RangeError. The cursor API of the RFC removes the size code, so the RangeError case then becomes a silent write of a wrong count.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Use one rule for every counted table: the array is the source, as in `sidx`, `stsd`, and `dref`. Remove `entryCount` from `ChunkOffsetBox`, `SampleToChunkBox`, `SyncSampleBox`, `DecodingTimeToSampleBox`, and `SampleDescriptionBox`. Remove `subsegmentCount` from `SubsegmentIndexBox` and `rangesCount` from `Subsegment`. Each writer writes `array.length`. `stsz` needs one decision: `sampleCount` must stay for a box with `sampleSize` not 0. For `sampleSize` 0, write `entrySize.length` as the count. If the count fields stay instead, every writer must still write `array.length` entries and that length as the count.

alsoReportedAs.title: Count fields duplicate list lengths in `subs`, `tfra`, and `tenc`, and the writers mix the count and the list in different ways.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeSubs.ts: the box size comes from a loop over `box.entries` (line 20), the written count is `writer.writeUint(box.entryCount, 4)` (line 34), the size of each entry is `entry.subsampleCount * (...)` (line 23), and the loop writes `entry.subsamples` (line 40). An `entryCount` that differs from `entries.length` writes a box whose count disagrees with its data, with no error. A `subsampleCount` below `subsamples.length` writes past the buffer. writeTfra.ts:34 `const entriesSize = box.numberOfEntry * entrySize` and line 50 `for (const entry of box.entries)`: the same split. writeTenc.ts:21 `box.defaultConstantIvSize ?? defaultConstantIv?.length` is a third rule. An adopter who pushes an entry must also update a second field. Open issue 625 describes the writer side and lists `writeTfra` and `writeSubs`. Other boxes have no count field: `SegmentIndexBox` has `references` only, and writeSidx.ts:49 writes `box.references.length`. The name also varies: `numberOfEntry` in `tfra`, `entryCount` in 20 other box types.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: In 2.0.0 remove the count field wherever a list of the same box gives the count: `SubsampleInformationBox.entryCount`, `SubsampleEntry.subsampleCount`, `TrackFragmentRandomAccessBox.numberOfEntry`, `TrackEncryptionBox.defaultConstantIvSize`. Readers use the count only to size the loop. Writers write `list.length`. This rule closes issue 625 for these boxes. Keep a count only where the syntax has a count and no list (`stsz` with a constant `sampleSize`).

alsoReportedAs.title: writeTrun takes the box size and the count field from sampleCount, and takes the rows from samples, so a mismatch throws or writes a corrupt box.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeTrun.ts:28 `const samplesSize = sampleSize * box.sampleCount`, :35 `writer.writeUint(box.sampleCount, 4)`, :45 `for (const sample of box.samples)`. With `samples.length > sampleCount` the `DataView` write goes past the buffer and throws a `RangeError`. That result conflicts with the settled rule that a writer does not throw. With `samples.length < sampleCount` the box declares rows that are zero bytes. An adopter who adds or removes a sample and does not update `sampleCount` gets one of the two results. Other writers already use the array: writeSidx.ts:49 `writer.writeUint(box.references.length, 2)`, writeDref.ts:20 `const entryCount = box.entries.length`. The cursor RFC removes the size code, so the `RangeError` disappears and the count mismatch becomes silent.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Use one source for the row count. Preferred: remove `sampleCount` from `TrackRunBox`, and `writeTrun` writes `box.samples.length`, as `writeSidx` and `writeDref` do. Alternative: keep `sampleCount` as the one source, and the writer loops `sampleCount` times with `box.samples[i]` and the default 0. Decide this item together with the finding about rows of a `trun` box with no per-sample flag, because that case is the only reason to keep `sampleCount`.

alsoReportedAs.title: The writers use three different rules for a count field and its array, so a count that differs from the array length throws an unclear error, writes zero entries, or is ignored.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Rule A, the count field is written and the array is iterated: writeStts `const entriesSize = box.entryCount * 8` / `writer.writeUint(box.entryCount, 4)` / `for (const entry of box.entries)`. The same form is in ctts, elst, stco, stsc, stss, subs, ssix, trun (`box.sampleCount`), tfra (`box.numberOfEntry`), prsl (`box.numEntitiesInGroup`), pssh (`box.kidCount`, `box.dataSize`), stsz. Rule B, a required count field is ignored: writeStsd `const entryCount = box.entries.length`, writeDref the same, but both types require `entryCount: number`. Rule C, the type has no count field: writeSidx `writer.writeUint(box.references.length, 2)`. Read-only run of the source: stts with entryCount 1 and 2 entries throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`. stts with entryCount 2 and 1 entry writes a second entry of zeros. trun with sampleCount 2 and 1 sample writes a second sample of zeros. stsd with entryCount 5 and no entries writes 0. pssh with dataSize 1 and 3 data bytes writes 1 byte. With the growing buffer of the RFC, the first case no longer throws and writes a count that does not match the entries.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: 2.0.0 defines one rule: the array length is the count that every writer writes. The count fields stay in the reader result but become optional in the box types, and the writers ignore them. The only exception is a box whose syntax has a count and no entries: `ctts` of version 2 or above writes `entryCount ?? 0`. Nested counts follow the same rule: `subsampleCount`, `rangesCount`, `kidCount`, `dataSize`.

alsoReportedAs.title: Thirteen writers size and count a table from a stored count field but loop over the array, so a mismatch writes phantom entries or throws
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeStts: `const entriesSize = box.entryCount * 8`, `writer.writeUint(box.entryCount, 4)`, then `for (const entry of box.entries)`. With entryCount 3 and 2 entries, the box holds a third entry of zeros. With entryCount 1 and 2 entries, `DataView` throws a RangeError. The same pattern is in writeCtts, writeElst, writeStco, writeStsc, writeStss, writeStsz, writeSubs (two counts), writeSsix (two counts), writeTfra, writeTrun, and writePrsl. writePssh follows the count and pads or cuts the array: `writer.writeArray(box.data, UINT, 1, box.dataSize)`. Three writers ignore the stored count: writeDref `const entryCount = box.entries.length`, writeStsd the same, writeSidx `writer.writeUint(box.references.length, 2)`. `DataReferenceBox.entryCount` and `SampleDescriptionBox.entryCount` are required fields that no writer reads. With the growing buffer of the cursor RFC, no size check remains, so a mismatch becomes a count field that silently differs from the entries.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Rule for 2.0.0: the array is the only source of a count. Remove `entryCount` (ctts, dref, elst, stco, stsc, stsd, stss, stts, subs), `subsampleCount`, `subsegmentCount`, `rangesCount`, `numberOfEntry`, `numEntitiesInGroup`, `kidCount`, `dataSize`, and trun `sampleCount` from the box types. Each writer writes `array.length`. Keep `stsz.sampleCount`, because the box has no table when `sampleSize` is not 0. This rule also matches the settled rule that no field exists only to keep the bytes of a box that breaks the spec.

alsoReportedAs.title: Writers do not agree on the source of a count field: some write `entries.length`, and others write and size the buffer from the count field of the box.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeStsd and writeDref: `const entryCount = box.entries.length`, so the required field `entryCount` of the box has no effect. writeStco: `const entriesSize = box.entryCount * 4`, then `for (const offset of box.chunkOffset)`. A box with one more offset than `entryCount` writes past the buffer. A box with fewer offsets writes a wrong count and zero entries. writeElst, writeStsc, writeStss, writeStts, writeSubs, and writeTrun follow the same pattern as writeStco. The test for boxes that code builds states both values: `entryCount: 1, entries: [...]` and `subsampleCount: 3, subsamples: [...]`.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Use the array length as the count in every writer for the versions with defined syntax, and remove the count fields from those box types. Keep a count field only where the settled rule for literal syntax needs it, such as `entryCount` of a ctts box of version 2 or above with `entries: []`. The cursor RFC removes the size code, and this change removes the second source of the count.

alsoReportedAs.title: A count field and the array it counts are both public, and the writers use four different rules when the two values differ.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Table of count field, array, and writer rule. (A) Writer ignores the count and writes the array length: `dref` (`const entryCount = box.entries.length`), `stsd` (same), `sidx` (`writer.writeUint(box.references.length, 2)`, the type has no `referenceCount` at all). (B) Writer sizes the buffer from the count, writes the count, then loops over the whole array: `ctts`, `elst`, `stco`, `stsc`, `stss`, `stts` (`entryCount` with `entries` or `chunkOffset`), `stsz` (`sampleCount` with `entrySize`), `trun` (`sampleCount` with `samples`), `tfra` (`numberOfEntry` with `entries`), `prsl` (`numEntitiesInGroup` with `entities`). Example: `const entriesSize = box.entryCount * 8` then `for (const entry of box.entries)`. Count below the length gives a RangeError from the DataView. Count above the length gives zero-filled entries. (C) Writer sizes from the array and writes the count field: outer loops of `ssix` (`writer.writeUint(box.subsegmentCount, 4)` after a size loop over `box.subsegments`) and `subs` (`box.entryCount`). A difference gives a box whose count does not match its bytes, with no error. (D) Writer truncates or pads the array to the count: `pssh` (`writer.writeArray(box.kid, UINT, 1, kidSize)`, `writeArray(box.data, UINT, 1, box.dataSize)`) and `tenc` (`box.defaultConstantIvSize ?? defaultConstantIv?.length`). libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:146 does `stsd.entries.unshift(box)` and never updates `stsd.entryCount`. The code works only because `stsd` is in group A. With the cursor of the RFC the buffer grows, so group B stops throwing and silently writes a wrong count.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: One rule: the array is the only source of a count. Remove the count field from every type where the count always equals the array length: `entryCount` (ctts, dref, elst, stco, stsc, stsd, stss, stts, subs, and the type-only co64, saio, sbgp, sgpd, stsh, iinf), `subsegmentCount`, `rangesCount`, `subsampleCount`, `numberOfEntry`, `numEntitiesInGroup`, `kidCount`, `dataSize`, `defaultConstantIvSize`, `itemCount`, `protectionCount`, `referenceCount`, and `sampleCount` of `senc`. The readers stop returning them and the writers write `array.length`, as `writeSidx` does today. Keep a count only where the box can have a count with no array: `sampleCount` of `stsz`, `stz2`, and `saiz`. Decide `trun` explicitly: its `samples` array has one empty object per sample when no per-sample flag is set.

alsoReportedAs.title: Writers trust a stored count field over the length of the array, and a stale count writes a corrupt box or throws.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeTrun sizes the box with `sampleSize * box.sampleCount` and then loops `for (const sample of box.samples)`. Probe: `sampleCount: 1` with two samples throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`. `sampleCount: 3` with one sample writes a count of 3 and two zero samples. writePssh has `writer.writeArray(box.data, UINT, 1, box.dataSize)`: `dataSize: 2` with four data bytes wrote two bytes and no error. writeStts, writeCtts, writeStsc, writeStss, writeStco, writeElst, writeSubs, writeTfra and writePrsl use the stored count in the same way. writeStsd and writeDref use `box.entries.length`, writeSidx uses `box.references.length`, and writeSdtp uses the array length. The package has two rules. The generators of hls.js (src/remux/mp4-generator.ts:1038) and shaka-player (lib/util/mp4_generator.js:837) take the count from the sample array and store no count.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Remove the count field where the array states it: entryCount (stts, ctts, stsc, stss, stco, elst, subs, dref, stsd), sampleCount (trun), kidCount and dataSize (pssh), numberOfEntry (tfra), numEntitiesInGroup (prsl), subsampleCount (subs entry). Each writer writes the array length. Keep sampleCount on stsz, because the box has no array when sampleSize is not 0. After the RFC removes the size code, the count stays the only source of this error, so the cursor writers must not copy `box.sampleCount`.

fact.reason:
Checked at HEAD 8ce63c212. The core problem is real and I reproduced it.

Types: every cited line holds. TrackRunBox.ts:14 `sampleCount: number`, DecodingTimeToSampleBox.ts:13, SampleDescriptionBox.ts:15, ProtectionSystemSpecificHeaderBox.ts:13 and :18, TrackFragmentRandomAccessBox.ts:14 `numberOfEntry`, SubsegmentIndexBox.ts:11, Subsegment.ts:9, SubsampleEntry.ts:10, PreselectionGroupBox.ts:24. The count of 24 matches the source: 14 types with a reader (stco, ctts, stts, elst, dref, stsd, stsc, stss, subs, ssix, tfra, trun, prsl, pssh) and 10 with no reader (co64, stz2, iloc, iinf, ipro, saio, senc, sgpd, sbgp, stsh). src/readers has no file for those 10. The lists with no count field also hold (SegmentIndexBox, TypeBox.compatibleBrands, sdtp, stdp, ItemLocation.extents, EncryptedSample.subsampleEncryption).

Writers: writeTrun.ts:28 `const samplesSize = sampleSize * box.sampleCount`, :35 writes `box.sampleCount`, :45 `for (const sample of box.samples)`. writeStts.ts:19/25/27 same form. writeStsd.ts:23 and writeDref.ts:20 `const entryCount = box.entries.length`, and neither file reads `box.entryCount`. writeSidx.ts:49 `writer.writeUint(box.references.length, 2)`.

Probe against src (scratch file outside the repo): stts with entryCount 1 and 2 entries throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView`. stts with entryCount 3 and 2 entries writes count 3 and a third entry of zeros. stsd with entryCount 99 and no entries writes count 0. trun with sampleCount 3 and 1 sample writes count 3 and two zero rows. All match the finding.

Details that are wrong or imprecise:
1. stz2. The proposal keeps `sampleCount` in stz2 "because the box has no array when the default size is not 0". The spec (14496-12:2015, CompactSampleSizeBox, text line 3252) has no default size: `sample_count` is always followed by `entry_size` for every sample. CompactSampleSizeBox.ts:12 has a required `entrySize: number[]`. The finding also lists stz2 among the 24 types, so it contradicts itself. Only stsz (spec line 3228) and saiz (spec line 3542) have a count with a conditional array.
2. "Rule 1, 12 writers size the buffer from the count and loop over the array" holds as written for 9: trun, stts, ctts, elst, stco, stss, stsc, tfra, prsl. writePssh.ts:37 and :41 do not loop over the array: `writeArray(box.kid, UINT, 1, kidSize)` runs to the count and IsoBoxWriteView.ts:297-298 pads with `data[i] ?? 0`, so it pads or truncates and never throws (probe: kidCount 1 with kid [] writes 16 zero bytes, dataSize 0 drops 4 data bytes). writeSsix.ts:21-31 and writeSubs.ts:20-34 size the outer level from the array and write the outer count field as given, so an outer mismatch writes a wrong count with no error. Only their nested counts (rangesCount, subsampleCount) size the buffer. writeStsz.ts:20/31 has the Rule 1 pattern for sampleSize 0 and is not in the list. The package therefore has four or five behaviors, not three.
3. trun. readTrun.ts:29 calls `readEntries(sampleCount, ...)`, so `samples` has one object per sample even when no per-sample flag is set (empty objects). The spec says the rows can be empty. Without `sampleCount`, an adopter who writes a trun that uses tfhd defaults must build N empty objects. The proposal does not address this case.
4. The count equals the array length only for well-formed input. readStsd.ts:28 and readDref.ts:19 call `readBoxes(entryCount)`, which returns fewer boxes when the box ends early (IsoBoxReadView.ts:414-430). Removal drops that information, which agrees with the settled rule against fields that only keep the bytes of a non-compliant box.

No other package reads these fields. libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:146 mutates `stsd.entries` and never updates `entryCount`, which works only because writeStsd ignores the field.
fact.correction: Keep the core rule: the array is the only source of a count, the reader stops returning the count, the writer writes `array.length`. Corrections: (a) Remove `sampleCount` from stz2 as well. Its syntax always has the `entry_size` array. Keep `sampleCount` only in stsz and saiz, where the array is absent for a default size that is not 0. (b) Describe the writer behaviors accurately: 9 writers size from the count and loop over the array (trun, stts, ctts, elst, stco, stss, stsc, tfra, prsl), plus stsz for sampleSize 0. writePssh pads or truncates the array to the count and never throws. writeSsix and writeSubs size the outer level from the array, write the outer count field as given, and use the nested count for the inner size. writeStsd and writeDref ignore a required field. sidx has no field. (c) Decide trun explicitly. With no per-sample flag (0x100 to 0x800), `samples` holds only empty objects, so `sampleCount` is the only real information. Options: keep `sampleCount` for trun as the stsz-style exception, or require `samples` to have one (possibly empty) object per sample and document that rule. (d) ctts of version 2 or above keeps `entryCount` with `entries: []` (issue 670), so `entryCount` stays in that type, optional for version 0 and 1.
fact.priorDecision: None that makes the general pattern intentional. Issue 625 (open, no decision) already reports the writer side and names the same writers. It states that the choice may need an RFC. The only settled exception is ctts of version 2 or above: issue 670 / PR 674 keep `entryCount` with an empty `entries` list (libs/iso-bmff/CHANGELOG.md:99-100). CHANGELOG.md:62 (issue 666) describes dref and stsd in terms of the count ("keeps the count of 0"), which stays true with `entries.length`.

value.reason:
Facts hold. I read the writers in libs/iso-bmff/src/writers: writeTrun.ts:28 `const samplesSize = sampleSize * box.sampleCount`, :35 `writer.writeUint(box.sampleCount, 4)`, :45 `for (const sample of box.samples)`. writeCtts.ts:22 and :28 use `box.entryCount`. writeStsd.ts:23 and writeDref.ts:20 use `const entryCount = box.entries.length` and never read the required `entryCount`. writePssh.ts sizes `kid` and `data` from `kidCount` and `dataSize`. libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:146 does `stsd.entries.unshift(box)` and never updates `entryCount`, so the package's own consumer already treats the array as the source.

No prior decision keeps the current state. `git log -S'entryCount' -- libs/iso-bmff` and `-S'box.entries.length'` show the split dates from the first writer commits (8ac3ef9b9, a4f84a560, d615e5bf0, a974b5a0b) with no design commit. Issue 625 (OPEN, no comments) reports the same problem and names the same two possible rules. It says the choice may need an RFC. The cursor RFC (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md) says nothing about count fields. The settled rules support the proposal: a writer does not throw (the RangeError case breaks that today), and no field exists only to keep the bytes of a box that breaks the spec (a count that differs from its list is such a field). The readers always return count equal to the list length, so the reader result loses no information.

Three points of the proposal need a change:
1. `stz2` is wrong in the keep list. Spec 14496-12:2015 line 3252: `unsigned int(32) sample_count; for (i=1; i <= sample_count; i++) { unsigned int(field_size) entry_size; }`. The box has no default size, so the array always exists. Only `stsz` (`sampleSize` not 0) and `saiz` (`default_sample_info_size` not 0, spec line 3551) have a count with no array.
2. `pssh.kidCount` does not equal `kid.length`. readPssh.ts:29 `kid = readArray(UINT, 1, kidCount * 16)`, and CHANGELOG.md:89 (issue 649, PR 657) states "The `kid` field has 16 numbers for each key ID". PR 657 kept the flat list only to avoid a type break in a minor. "The writer writes array.length" gives a count 16 times too high here.
3. `trun` and `senc` have rows that can be empty. Spec line 3959: "also the number of rows in the following table (the rows can be empty)". The array length is still a valid count, so removal works, but the result is a list of empty objects when no per-sample flag is set. The proposal must state this result, not leave it open.

The ctts exception in the proposal matches CHANGELOG.md:99-100 (issue 670, PR 674). The tenc carve-out matches PR 658 (writeTenc.ts:21 `box.defaultConstantIvSize ?? defaultConstantIv?.length`). Two duplicates (F96, F397) propose to remove `defaultConstantIvSize`. That part conflicts with PR 658 and must not be done.
value.priorDecision: None for the current state. Issue 625 is open with no decision and lists both rules. Related decisions that limit the proposal: PR 674 / issue 670 (ctts version 2 or above keeps `entryCount` with `entries: []`), PR 658 (tenc `defaultConstantIvSize` stays), PR 657 / issue 649 (`pssh.kid` is a flat list with 16 numbers for each key ID, kept in a minor to avoid a type break).
value.correction:
Rule for 2.0.0: the list is the only source of a count. Remove the count field from the box type and from the reader result, and each writer writes the list length. This rule closes issue 625.

Changes to the proposal:
- Keep `sampleCount` only in `stsz` and `saiz`. For `stsz` with `sampleSize` 0 and `saiz` with `defaultSampleInfoSize` 0, the writer writes the list length. For the other case the writer writes `sampleCount`. Remove `sampleCount` from `stz2`: its syntax always has the list.
- `pssh`: `kidCount` is `kid.length / 16`, not `kid.length`. Change `kid` to a list with one 16-byte entry for each key ID in the same major, then the writer writes `kid.length`. If `kid` stays flat, the writer writes `kid.length >>> 4`. `dataSize` goes away and the writer writes `data.length`.
- `trun` and `senc`: remove `sampleCount`. `samples` has one entry for each sample, and the entry is an empty object when no per-sample flag is set. The spec describes the same model ("the rows can be empty"). Document this case in the TSDoc of `TrackRunBox`.

confirmed.title: The readers map has no key check, and a reader under the wrong key silently changes the `type` of the box.
confirmed.breakingReason: The result keeps the `type` from the box header where it has the `type` of the reader result today, or the call fails to compile.

fact.reason:
Checked at HEAD 8ce63c212. The core problem is real and I reproduced each evidence statement. The proposal has two errors.

Confirmed facts:
- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReaderMap.ts:10-13 is `Record<IsoBoxType, IsoBoxReader<unknown, IsoBoxType, V>>`. IsoBoxType is a template of four `${string}` parts (src/IsoBoxType.ts), so the map has no key list and no pairing of key and reader.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:463 looks up `readers[type] || readers[type.trim()]`, and line 466 is `Object.assign(box, parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type))`. The reader result overwrites `type` from the header.
- Run time, checked with node against src and test/fixtures/test_frag.mp4: `readers: { tfdt: readTfdt }` gives 3 tfdt and 3 mfhd boxes. `readers: { tfdt: readMfhd }` gives 0 tfdt and 6 mfhd boxes.
- Types, checked with tsc 6.0.3 against src: `readIsoBoxes(data, { readers: { tfdt: readTrun } })` compiles. In the result, `box.type === 'tfdt'` is error TS2367 (no overlap), and `box.type === 'trun'` narrows to a box with `sampleCount`. IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts:38-50 adds the return type B of each reader, and lines 54-63 remove the built-in type of the key. The static type therefore agrees with the wrong run-time result.
- No RFC, changelog entry or guide states that a reader under a different key is intended. docs/reading-boxes.md:47 only says that the result type follows the custom reader. The cursor RFC keeps IsoBoxReaderMap and the literal `type` in readers (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:107, 146), so the finding does not repeat an RFC item. No map in src, test, docs or the other packages uses a mismatched key.

Details that are wrong or imprecise:
- "Every built-in reader returns a literal `type`": ten sample entry readers (readAvc1 to readAvc4, readHvc1, readHev1, readEncv, readEnca, readMp4a, and the two factories) pass the type as an argument to readVisualSampleEntryBox or readAudioSampleEntryBox (src/readers/readVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:21-27). The effect is the same.
- The proposed type does not compile as written. IsoBoxReader has three type parameters, `<B, T extends IsoBoxType, V>` (src/IsoBoxReader.ts:12-16). `IsoBoxReader<{ type: K }, V>` puts V in the position of T and gives TS2344.
- With the arity corrected, I tested the proposed type in the scratchpad. The wrong key is rejected (TS2322, '"trun"' is not assignable to '"tfdt"'). The bigint instantiation of a generic reader still works with the NoInfer configuration. Inline readers keep the contextual `view`. A `url` key with readUrl still compiles through the index signature. But a custom reader under a known key that returns no `type` field, such as `tfdt: (view) => ({ v: view.readUint(4) })`, no longer compiles. That reader works today and keeps the header type. The finding does not state this second break.
fact.correction: Corrected proposal: `type IsoBoxReaderMap<V extends IsoInt64 = number> = { [K in keyof IsoBoxMap]?: IsoBoxReader<{ type: K }, IsoBoxType, V> } & { [type: string]: IsoBoxReader<unknown, IsoBoxType, V> | undefined }` (three type arguments, not two). State both compile breaks: a reader under the wrong known key, and a custom reader under a known key that returns no `type` field. To avoid the second break, type the known keys as `IsoBoxReader<{ type?: K }, IsoBoxType, V>`, or apply only the run-time fix. The run-time fix is one assignment after line 466 of IsoBoxReadView.ts: set `box.type` from the header again. If only the run-time fix lands, IsoBoxReaderReturn must also change, because it would still report the `type` of the reader result. Also correct the evidence sentence: the sample entry readers take the type as an argument and do not write a literal.

Facts confirmed in source. libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReaderMap.ts:10 is `Record<IsoBoxType, IsoBoxReader<unknown, IsoBoxType, V>>`, and IsoBoxType (src/IsoBoxType.ts:6) is a template of four `${string}` parts. A tsc 6.0.3 probe showed `string extends IsoBoxType`, so the map is `Record<string, ...>`: no key completion and no pairing. src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:466 is `Object.assign(box, parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type))`, so the reader result overwrites the header `type`. src/IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts:42 keys the union member on the `type` of the reader result.

Prior decision search: `git log -S'IsoBoxReaderMap'` gives d615e5bf0, 3102f626e, 2aca3e3e9 (int64 `V` parameter only). `git log -S'IsoBoxReaderReturn'` gives 8d0b4b393 (PR 614). No commit, changelog entry, RFC, or issue discusses a check between the map key and the reader `type`. gh searches for 'readers map iso-bmff', 'IsoBoxReaderMap', 'IsoBoxReaderReturn' returned only 652, 619, 663 (unrelated). The current state is an omission, not a choice. Two intentional rules constrain the fix: (1) PR 614 and rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:105 ("the result type keeps whatever the reader returns"), CHANGELOG.md:64. (2) docs/reading-boxes.md:83: a reader under the trimmed key `url` reads the `"url "` box.

I tested the proposed type in a scratchpad probe against src (file <scratchpad>/f198/probe.mts, no repo file changed). It works with the current IsoBoxReaderReturn: built-in readers in number and bigint mode narrow correctly, `tfdt: readTrun`, `tfdt: readMfhd`, `enca: readMp4a` fail, `url: readUrl` and `'ac-3': createAudioSampleEntryReader('ac-3')` pass, the documented emsg ID3 reader and `type: 'tfdt' as const` readers pass, a generic reader in a variable passes, `defaultReaderConfig()` passes, the dynamic string-key pattern of libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:41 passes, a reader that returns `any` passes.

The finding understates the break. The probe also rejects two reader forms that compile and run correctly today: a known-key custom reader declared outside the call that returns `type: string` (no `as const`), and a known-key custom reader that returns no `type` (the header `type` stays today). `map[key]` reads also become `| undefined`. An unknown key such as `'ac-3': readMp4a` still compiles, so the check covers only keys of IsoBoxMap.

The second run-time alternative ("let readers omit `type`") conflicts with rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md: line 63 calls `readTfdt(cursor)` standalone after `seekIsoBox`, the custom reader example at lines 93 to 113 returns `type: 'mfhd'`, and writers select by `box.type`. A box from a standalone reader needs its `type`.

No settled decision is broken. The compile check has zero run-time and bundle cost and matches AGENTS.md Developer Experience ("Incorrect usage should fail at compile time", literal types for autocomplete). Severity is nearer low than medium: only adopter error reaches the wrong `type`.
value.priorDecision: None for the missing key check. Related intentional rules that the fix must keep: PR 614 (8d0b4b393, CHANGELOG.md:64) and rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:105 make the reader return type the result type, and docs/reading-boxes.md:83 documents the trimmed `url` and `urn` keys as aliases.
value.correction:
Keep the compile-time part and fold it into the cursor RFC, which already redefines `IsoBoxReaderMap<V>` and `IsoBoxReader<B, V>`:

`type IsoBoxReaderMap<V extends IsoInt64 = number> = { [K in keyof IsoBoxMap]?: IsoBoxReader<{ type: K }, V> } & { [type: string]: IsoBoxReader<{ type: string }, V> | undefined }`

Changes against the finding's proposal:
1. Require `{ type: string }` for unknown keys too, not `unknown`. In version 2 the tree reader returns the reader result and no longer merges it onto a header box, so nothing else guarantees that every box has a `type`. The probe variant with this index signature compiled for the same cases.
2. Drop the alternative "let readers omit `type`". Standalone readers after `seekIsoBox` and the writers need `type` on the box.
3. Treat the run-time override (`box.type = headerType` after the reader call) as a separate, optional question for the cursor RFC. It costs one store per box and was not measured. It also makes the static type and the run-time value differ for an unchecked unknown key. The compile check already covers the known keys.
4. State the full break in the changelog: a wrong-key reader fails to compile, a known-key custom reader must return the literal `type` of its key (add `as const` or a return type), a known-key reader with no `type` fails, and `map[key]` is possibly `undefined`. The `url` and `urn` aliases and readers for unknown keys do not change.

confirmed.title: Byte fields are `number[]` in pssh, tenc, and the sample entries, but `Uint8Array` in emsg, mdat, free, imda, and senc.
confirmed.breakingReason: The public field types and the values that the readers return change from `number[]` to `Uint8Array`, and `kid` changes shape.
confirmed.evidence: ProtectionSystemSpecificHeaderBox.ts: `systemId: number[]`, `kid: number[]` (documented as "one after the other ... `kidCount * 16` numbers"), `data: number[]`. readPssh.ts:33 `const data = readArray(UINT, 1, dataSize)` pushes one array element for each byte of the system data. TrackEncryptionBox.ts: `defaultKid: number[]`, `defaultConstantIv?: number[]`. VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:28 `compressorName: number[]`, where the specification has `string[32] compressorname` (12.1.3.2). Against that: EventMessageBox.ts:18 `messageData: Uint8Array`, MediaDataBox, FreeSpaceBox, IdentifiedMediaDataBox `data: Uint8Array`, EncryptedSample `initializationVector?: Uint8Array`. Checked with node: `pssh.data.constructor.name` is `Array`. A caller must copy `data` into a `Uint8Array` before a protection system parser or an EME call can use it.
confirmed.proposal: Use `Uint8Array` for every opaque byte field: `systemId`, `data`, `defaultKid`, `defaultConstantIv`. The reader returns a view over the input (`readBytes` in the RFC), so the read allocates no element array. Change `kid: number[]` to `kids: Uint8Array[]` with one 16-byte view for each key ID. Change `compressorName` to `string` (the reader decodes the length byte and the text, and the writer pads to 32 bytes). The writers accept `Uint8Array`, and may also accept `ArrayLike<number>` to ease migration.

- The other form: EventMessageBox.ts:18, MediaDataBox.ts:8, FreeSpaceBox.ts:8, IdentifiedMediaDataBox.ts:9, EncryptedSample.ts:9 use `Uint8Array`.

Spec check. 23001-7:2016 text lines 676 to 691 declare `unsigned int(8)[16] SystemID` and a list of `KID` entries with `[KID_count]`. Lines 758 to 761 declare `unsigned int(8)[16] default_KID` and `unsigned int(8)[default_constant_IV_size] default_constant_IV`. 14496-12:2015 text line 9340 declares `string[32] compressorname`. Lines 9352 to 9355 state the count byte and the padding. A list of 16-byte key IDs matches the spec better than one flat list.

Prior decisions. No decision chose `number[]` as the design. The type comes from the first commit 8ac3ef9b9 (CML Version 1). PR 657 (83716b139) kept `kid` as a flat `number[]` only to avoid a type change in a minor version. PR 658 (60ae65d0f) added `defaultConstantIv?: number[]` to match `defaultKid`. The RFC rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:186 maps `readData` to `readBytes` and line 189 replaces `readArray` with a loop in the reader. The RFC does not state the types of byte fields. `gh issue list` found no issue on this subject. Issue 625 (open) covers count fields.

Why partly. The core change is good: the reader allocates no element array, the writer uses one `set` call, and a key ID has one type in the package. The proposal has five gaps, listed in the correction.
value.priorDecision: None that makes the current state intentional. PR 657 (commit 83716b139, issue 649) states: "The kid field stays a number[] with 16 numbers for each key ID, so the type ProtectionSystemSpecificHeaderBox does not change." The commit kept the type to avoid a break in a minor version. The same commit leaves the `kidCount` question to issue 625 (open). PR 658 (commit 60ae65d0f, issue 648) set the rule that `writeTenc` writes a 0 for each byte that `defaultConstantIv` does not have. That rule must stay.
value.correction:
Keep the core: `systemId: Uint8Array`, `data: Uint8Array`, `kids: Uint8Array[]` (one 16-byte view for each key ID, empty for version 0), `defaultKid: Uint8Array`, `defaultConstantIv?: Uint8Array`. The readers return views over the input with `readBytes`. Type the fields as `Uint8Array`, per the AGENTS.md rule for a view over the input.

Change these five points:

1. Do not add `ArrayLike<number>` to the field types. One box type is the reader result and the writer input. A wider type makes every consumer of a reader result handle two forms. `Uint8Array.prototype.set` already accepts a plain array at run time, so JavaScript callers lose nothing.

2. State the writer rule for fixed sizes. The writer writes exactly 16 bytes for `systemId`, each key ID, and `defaultKid`. A short value gets zero bytes, and a long value is cut. This rule keeps the settled decision that a writer does not throw, and the padding rule of PR 658. One `set` call with no `subarray(0, 16)` would move the next fields for a long value.

3. Do not remove or rederive `kidCount`, `dataSize`, and `defaultConstantIvSize` inside this finding. Issue 625 (open) owns the count rule. Decide both in the same major version, because `kids.length` and `kidCount` can differ.

4. Decide `compressorName` as a separate finding. A `string` matches `string[32] compressorname` and the settled rule about bytes that break the spec. The decision needs three rules that the proposal does not state: the text encoding (the 2015 text says only "displayable data"), a count byte above 31, and how the writer cuts a long name. The change also adds a string function to every visual sample entry reader.

5. Add the cost to the plan. `@svta/cml-drm` has the public option `EnsureEncryptedInitOptions.defaultKid: number[]` (libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:94 and 119, libs/drm/config/cml-drm.api.md:64) and passes the value to the `tenc` writer. The drm package must change or convert the value. Also document that each view field keeps the input buffer in memory and shows later changes of the input, as the TSDoc of `readData` states today.

Leave `reserved1: number[]` (SampleEntryBox.ts:10) and `sdtp.sampleDependencyTable` out of this rule. `reserved1` is a reserved field, and `sdtp` holds one packed entry for each sample. Neither is an opaque byte string.

Issue 647 (closed as not planned) supports the removal of the `reserved*` fields: a writer that follows the spec has no defect.

The proposal is too broad in two places.

(1) `pre_defined` is not `reserved`. Clause 6.2.2 (2015 text, lines 1274-1279) says a pre-defined field that is not used "must be copied un-inspected when boxes are copied, and ignored on reading". The syntax has no `const` on these fields (`unsigned int(32) pre_defined = 0;` in hdlr, `bit(32)[6] pre_defined = 0;` in mvhd). A non-zero value does not break the spec, so the settled rule of issue 647 does not cover these 7 fields. Removal makes a read and a write unable to follow the copy rule. I scanned the fixtures: `240fps_go_pro_hero_4.mp4` has three hdlr boxes with `6d686c72` (`mhlr`) in pre_defined and one mp4a entry with `fffe` in pre_defined.

(2) `AudioSampleEntryBox.reserved2` is the only place that holds `entry_version` of AudioSampleEntryV1. Clause 12.2.3.2: `unsigned int(16) entry_version; // must be 1` and then `const unsigned int(16)[3] reserved = 0;`, in the same 8 bytes that readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:27 reads as `reserved2: readArray(UINT, 4, 2)`. If the writer writes 8 zero bytes, a compliant V1 entry becomes a version 0 entry. That result is a defect in a spec-compliant box.

Cost that the finding did not state: `time_to_sample.mp4` has an hdlr box with `6170706c` (`appl`) in the first reserved word. The fixture test (test/fixtureRoundTrip.test.ts:29-35) has two EXCEPTIONS lines today. Removal of `reserved` adds one line for that box. The box breaks `const unsigned int(32)[3] reserved = 0`, so the settled rule accepts that cost.

The gain is clear: fewer allocations in the readers (`readArray` for 6, 2, and 3 values in each sample entry), a box literal with only fields that have meaning, and one writer rule in place of three.
value.priorDecision: None shows that the current state is intentional. Issue 647 (closed as not planned, 2026-11-13) supports the removal of the `reserved*` fields: a writer that follows the spec has no defect, and the package adds no field that only keeps the bytes of a box that breaks the spec. That rule does not cover the `pre_defined` fields, because clause 6.2.2 of ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 permits a non-default value and requires a copy.
value.correction:
Apply one rule in 2.0.0, in three parts.

1. Remove the 14 `reserved*` fields: mvhd `reserved1`, `reserved2`. tkhd `reserved1`, `reserved2`, `reserved3`. hdlr `reserved`. smhd `reserved`. sidx `reserved`. tfra `reserved`. SampleEntryBox `reserved1`. VisualSampleEntryBox `reserved2`, `reserved3`. AudioSampleEntryBox `reserved2`, `reserved3`. The reader skips the bytes with no allocation. The writer writes 0.

2. Before the removal of `AudioSampleEntryBox.reserved2`, add `entryVersion?: number` (default 0). The reader reads the first 16 bits of that area as `entryVersion` and skips the other 48 bits. The writer writes `box.entryVersion ?? 0`. This keeps AudioSampleEntryV1 of clause 12.2.3.2 correct.

3. Keep the 7 `preDefined*` fields and make them optional: mvhd `preDefined`, hdlr `preDefined`, mdhd `preDefined`, VisualSampleEntryBox `preDefined1`, `preDefined2`, `preDefined3`, AudioSampleEntryBox `preDefined`. The reader still returns them. The writer uses the default of the spec for an absent field: 0, and -1 for `preDefined3` (`box.preDefined3 ?? -1`, which also fixes the wrong 0 at writeVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:74). Add one TSDoc line that cites clause 6.2.2.

Changelog and test: state that a box with a non-zero reserved value writes zeros. Add one EXCEPTIONS line to test/fixtureRoundTrip.test.ts for the hdlr box of `time_to_sample.mp4` (`appl` in the first reserved word). The GoPro hdlr and mp4a boxes keep their bytes because `preDefined` stays.

If Casey prefers the full removal of all 21 fields, the cost is a deviation from the copy rule of clause 6.2.2 and four more changed boxes in the GoPro fixture. Part 2 is required in both cases.

value.correction:
Keep the proposal with these changes.

1. sidx: remove `reference` and `sap` from `SegmentIndexReference`. Keep the six spec fields. `0 | 1` for `referenceType` and `startsWithSap` is optional. The fields are `bit(1)`, so the type is accurate, but it needs a cast in readSidx and a narrowing step for adopters who pass a `number`.

For version 0, write 0 for the second byte. For version 1 or above, write `((defaultCryptByteBlock ?? 0) << 4) | (defaultSkipByteBlock ?? 0)`. Then write `defaultIsProtected`. The changelog needs the migration: `defaultIsEncrypted & 0xff` becomes `defaultIsProtected`.

confirmed.title: Readers set 12 absent optional fields to an explicit `undefined`, while the types declare them optional and other readers omit the key.
confirmed.breakingReason: The key set of the returned objects changes, which `in`, `Object.keys`, and strict equality checks observe.
confirmed.evidence: readTfhd.ts:25 `baseDataOffset: flags & 0x01 ? view.readWideUint(8) : undefined` (5 fields). readPrsl (3 fields), readSchm (1), readStsz (1), and readTrun (`dataOffset`, `firstSampleFlags`) do the same. In the same file, readTrun.ts:30 starts each sample as `{}` and adds only the fields that the flags declare, and readTenc.ts:36 assigns the optional fields in an `if`. The reader results do not compile under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` as written, and `assert.deepStrictEqual` against a hand-built box fails.
confirmed.proposal: Use one rule in every reader: a field that the flags or the version do not declare has no key. The optional `?:` types then describe the result exactly, and a hand-built box equals a parsed box. If a stable object shape matters more for a hot box such as trun samples, choose the other rule everywhere (`field: T | undefined`, key always present) and state it in the guide. Do not keep both.

- src/readers/readSchm.ts:23 `schemeUri: flags & 0x000001 ? view.readUtf8(-1) : undefined`.
- src/readers/readPrsl.ts:25-27, three fields, returned at lines 36-38.
- src/readers/readStsz.ts:33 `entrySize: sampleSize === 0 ? view.readArray(UINT, 4, sampleCount) : undefined`.

Key absent:
- src/readers/readTrun.ts:30 `const sample: TrackRunSample = {}`, with assignments under `if (flags & 0x100)` and the next three flags (lines 32-43).
- src/readers/readTenc.ts:35-38 `if (version > 0) { box.defaultCryptByteBlock = ...`, and lines 40-43 for the constant IV.

Types use `?:` for both forms: src/boxes/TrackFragmentHeaderBox.ts:12-16, TrackRunBox.ts:15-16, TrackRunSample.ts:7-10, SchemeTypeBox.ts:12, PreselectionGroupBox.ts:29-31, SampleSizeBox.ts:12.

The trun box (flags 0xb05) has the keys `dataOffset` and `firstSampleFlags`. Its first sample has only `sampleDuration`, `sampleSize`, and `sampleCompositionTimeOffset`. `assert.deepStrictEqual` against a hand-built tfhd without the absent keys fails.

Compile check, run by me with tsc 6.0.3, `--noEmit --strict --exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: TS2375 on readTfhd.ts(20), readTrun.ts(48), readSchm.ts(17), readPrsl.ts(29), and readStsz.ts(27). readTenc.ts has no error. The repo does not enable that option (no match in any tsconfig or vite.config.ts), so the error is hypothetical for the package build.

Two small notes that do not change the verdict. The file list cites TrackFragmentHeaderBox.ts:14, and the quoted `baseDataOffset?: V` is on line 12. In test_frag.mp4 the trun flags declare both box fields, so the fixture shows real values there. The always-present keys for trun follow from the code at lines 48-56.

No library code depends on the presence of these keys. The `in` checks in src cover only `type`, `view`, `buffer`, `version`, `flags`, and `boxes`. Writers decide by the flags (src/writers/writeTfhd.ts:23-27 and 43-60 use `box.flags & ...` and `?? 0`), so written bytes do not change with either rule.

No prior decision makes the mixed state intentional. Related documented behavior: readStsz.ts:9 states `entrySize` is `undefined` when `sampleSize` is not 0, and test/readers/readStsz.test.ts:96 asserts the value. The TSDoc of TrackEncryptionBox.ts:32-34 states that `readTenc` sets the pattern fields for version 1 or above. Both statements describe the value, not the presence of the key. The existing tests assert `strictEqual(x, undefined)` (readTrun.test.ts:10, readSchm.test.ts:59), which pass under either rule.
fact.correction: The finding is accurate. Two additions for the proposal. First, the choice between the rules has a performance side, and performance is priority 1. One object literal with every key gives one object shape for each box type. The omit-key rule gives one shape for each flag combination, and the `{}` plus conditional assignment form in the trun samples builds each sample through shape transitions. For tfhd and trun, which a player reads for every fragment, the form "one literal, every key, absent value is `undefined`, types stay `?:`" is the cheaper one, and it changes only the trun samples and tenc. Measure before the rule is chosen. Second, the `entrySize` of stsz is a separate question (variant F86): the settled rule for ctts version 2 or above returns an empty array for a table that the syntax omits, so `entrySize: number[]` with `[]` is consistent with that precedent and should be decided apart from the key-presence rule. The cursor API RFC rewrites every reader, so applying one rule there adds almost no cost.

Facts confirmed in src. The types use `?:` for both forms (TrackFragmentHeaderBox.ts:12-16, TrackRunSample.ts:7-10, TrackEncryptionBox.ts:29-57, SampleSizeBox.ts:12). These six readers are the only readers with optional fields. The other optional box fields (saio, saiz, sbgp, sgpd, iloc, infe, senc) have writers only.

Prior decision: none for the rule. `git log -S'baseDataOffset: flags & 0x01'` and `-S'const sample: TrackRunSample = {}'` both return only 8ac3ef9b9 (CML Version 1, #265), so both forms are inherited code. readTenc got the `if` form in 60ae65d0f (#658) with no statement on keys. The cursor RFC, the int64 RFC, the container RFC, CHANGELOG.md, README and docs say nothing on absent fields. `gh issue list` with five keyword sets returned nothing. The one deliberate statement is PR 621 (e01b41b3a): "`readStsz` returns `entrySize` as `undefined` when `sampleSize` is not 0", repeated in the TSDoc at readStsz.ts:9 and asserted in readStsz.test.ts:96. That statement fixes the value, not the key.

Settled decisions: no conflict with either rule. Every writer reads the fields through `??` (writeTfhd.ts:44-60, writeTrun.ts:38-56, writeTenc.ts:21-52, writeSchm.ts:19, writePrsl.ts:25-65), so a missing key and an `undefined` value write the same bytes.

Value check of the preferred proposal (omit the key): I measured both forms for trun samples in a scratch benchmark (node 24.22.3, <scratchpad>/f202/bench.mjs, create 4096 samples and read three fields, best of five). One flag combination: omit 6.7 ns per sample, one literal with all keys 6.3 ns. Six flag combinations in rotation: omit 16.3 ns, literal 7.1 ns. The omit form creates one object shape for each flag combination, and adopter loops over samples of audio and video tracks then read more than one shape. The benchmark is synthetic, so the size of the gap in a player is not proven, but the literal form is never slower. Performance is priority 1, so the finding's preferred direction is the wrong one for the hot path. The finding's alternative (F105, F299) is the right one.

Sub-proposals: F404's change of pssh `kid` and url `location` to optional fields makes adopters write `kid?.length` and conflicts with the direction of PR 674 and PR 676 (absent lists stay as empty values). F86 (stsz `entrySize: number[]` with `[]`) follows that same direction and reverses the PR 621 statement, so it is a separate, optional item.
value.priorDecision: None for the key rule. Both forms come from 8ac3ef9b9 (CML Version 1, #265). PR 621 (e01b41b3a) states on purpose that `readStsz` returns `entrySize` as `undefined` when `sampleSize` is not 0, which matters only for the F86 sub-proposal. PR 674 (ctts version 2: `entries: []`) and PR 676 (emsg unknown versions keep the known fields with empty values) show that absent lists stay as required fields with empty values.
value.correction: Use the stable-shape rule, not the omit rule. In 2.0.0 every reader returns one object literal with every key of its box type in syntax order, and a scalar field that the flags or the version exclude has the value `undefined`. Only two places change: the trun samples (readTrun.ts:30-43) and readTenc (the four fields set at readTenc.ts:35-43). tfhd, schm, prsl, stsz and the trun box already follow the rule. Declare the fields as `field?: T | undefined`, so the type states what the reader returns under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and an adopter who builds a box can still omit the field or pass `undefined`. State the rule once in the reading guide, with the note that `in` and `Object.keys` do not show presence and that the flags and the version do. Do not make pssh `kid` or url `location` optional. alsoReportedAs.title: Tables with one column have three representations: `number[]` in stco and stsz, one object for each entry in stss and prsl, and a byte list in sdtp
alsoReportedAs.evidence: readStco: `chunkOffset: view.readArray(UINT, 4, entryCount)`. readStsz: `entrySize: sampleSize === 0 ? view.readArray(UINT, 4, sampleCount) : undefined`. readStss: `entries: view.readEntries<SyncSample>(entryCount, () => ({ sampleNumber: view.readUint(4) }))`, with `type SyncSample = { sampleNumber: number }`. readPrsl: `view.readEntries<Entity>(numEntitiesInGroup, () => ({ entityId: view.readUint(4) }))`. The spec syntax of stss is one `unsigned int(32) sample_number` for each entry, the same form as stco. `readArray` starts with `const value = []` and grows the array with `push`, although the count is known. A non-fragmented file has one stsz entry for each sample.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Rule for 2.0.0: a table with one integer column is a typed array, created once with the known count and filled in a loop. `stco.chunkOffset: Uint32Array`, `stsz.entrySize?: Uint32Array`, `stss.sampleNumber: Uint32Array` (replaces `entries`), `prsl.entityId: Uint32Array` (replaces `entities`), `sdtp.sampleDependencyTable: Uint8Array` as a view. A table with more than one column (stts, ctts, stsc, elst, sidx, tfra, subs, ssix) keeps an array of objects, created with `new Array(count)` and one object literal for each entry. Cost for adopters: a box built by hand needs `new Uint32Array([...])`. Measure the heap of both forms on a long non-fragmented file before the decision.

fact.reason:
Every factual statement holds at HEAD (paths under libs/iso-bmff).

stss: src/boxes/SyncSample.ts:6-8 is `export type SyncSample = { sampleNumber: number }`. src/boxes/SyncSampleBox.ts:12 is `entries: SyncSample[]`. src/readers/readStss.ts:24-26 is `entries: view.readEntries<SyncSample>(entryCount, () => ({ sampleNumber: view.readUint(4) }))`, so the reader allocates one object for each entry. The spec syntax (14496-12-2015.txt:2825-2832) has one field for each entry: `unsigned int(32) sample_number`.

prsl: src/boxes/Entity.ts:6-9 is `export type Entity = { /** Entity ID */ entityId: number }`. src/boxes/PreselectionGroupBox.ts:27 is `entities: Entity[]`. src/readers/readPrsl.ts:22-24 is `view.readEntries<Entity>(numEntitiesInGroup, () => ({ entityId: view.readUint(4) }))`. The three spec text files have no EntityToGroupBox or prsl, so I did not check the spec field name.

Plain arrays elsewhere: ChunkOffsetBox.ts:12 `chunkOffset: number[]`, SampleSizeBox.ts:12 `entrySize?: number[]`, SampleDependencyTypeBox.ts:10 `sampleDependencyTable: number[]`, SampleAuxiliaryInformationOffsetsBox.ts:13 `offset: number[]`, TrackReferenceTypeBox.ts:8 `trackIds: number[]`. Also ChunkLargeOffsetBox.ts:11, CompactSampleSizeBox.ts:12, DegradationPriorityBox.ts:10, SingleItemTypeReferenceBox.ts:9. readStco.ts:29 and readStsz.ts:33 use `view.readArray(UINT, 4, ...)`.

Refutation attempt: a grep of every `readEntries` call in src/readers shows that stss and prsl are the only two callers with an object of one field. All others (stts, ctts, stsc, elst, tfra, sidx, ssix, subs, trun) have two or more fields. Both types are public exports (config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md:197, 810, 1360, 1368). I found no prior decision in CHANGELOG.md, rfc/*.md, or the git log of the two type files (they date from the first writers commit d615e5bf0 and the v1 commit 8ac3ef9b9).

Two additions, not errors. (1) The break also reaches the writers: writeStss.ts:27-28 reads `entry.sampleNumber` and writePrsl.ts:55-56 reads `entity.entityId`, so the writer input changes too. (2) The proposed plural names `sampleNumbers` and `entityIds` follow `trackIds`, but most lists in the package use the singular spec field name (`chunkOffset`, `entrySize`, `offset`, `priority`, `toItemId`). `sampleNumber: number[]` would match that majority and the spec field `sample_number`. Pick one rule. I did not reproduce the heap measurement in the duplicate report F87.

value.reason:
The facts are correct. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/SyncSample.ts:6-8 is `export type SyncSample = { sampleNumber: number }`. src/readers/readStss.ts:24-26 creates one object for each entry. src/boxes/Entity.ts:6-9 and src/readers/readPrsl.ts:22-24 do the same for `prsl`. src/writers/writeStss.ts:27-29 and src/writers/writePrsl.ts:55-57 read the same objects. The other tables with one column are plain arrays under the spec field name: `chunkOffset: number[]` for stco and co64 (config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md:51, 58), `entrySize` for stz2 and stsz (api.md:69, 1181), `offset` for saio (api.md:1126), `sampleInfoSize` for saiz, `sampleDependencyTable` for sdtp (api.md:1142), `trackIds` (api.md:1490). The spec syntax of stss is one field for each entry: 14496-12-2015.txt:2829-2831 `for (i=0; i < entry_count; i++) { unsigned int(32) sample_number; }`. The 2015 spec text has no EntityToGroupBox and no `prsl`, so I did not check the `prsl` field name against spec text.

Prior decision: none found. `git log -S'SyncSample'` and `-S'entityId'` show only the first import (8ac3ef9b9, CML Version 1, #265), the writers commit (d615e5bf0), and two unrelated prsl fixes (#627, #634). CHANGELOG.md has no entry about the form of these lists. No RFC in rfc/ discusses it. `gh issue list` returns only issue 624 (prsl empty tag), which is unrelated. The current form is an inherited form, not a choice.

Measurement (my own scratch run, Node, 100000 entries, forced GC): the object form retains 4117448 heap bytes and the `number[]` form retains 917008. This result matches the number in F87. The gain in a player is small, because stss is empty or absent in fragmented content. The main gain is one consistent form and two fewer public types, one of them with the very general name `Entity`.

The proposal does not conflict with a settled decision. The cursor RFC already replaces `view.readEntries(...)` with a loop in the reader (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:189), so both readers and both writers change in 2.0.0 in any case. The extra cost of this fix is close to zero.

The proposal needs one change: the names. `sampleNumbers` and `entityIds` add a plural form, but the existing plain arrays use the spec field name in the singular (`chunkOffset`, `entrySize`, `offset`, `sampleInfoSize`). `trackIds` is plural only because the spec name is `track_IDs`. The typed-array rule of F300 is a separate decision: co64 values can be bigint under the int64 option, a box built by hand becomes harder to write, and no measurement on a real file exists.
value.correction: Use the spec field name, as stco, stsz, stz2, saio, and saiz do. `SyncSampleBox` becomes `{ type: 'stss'; entryCount: number; sampleNumber: number[] }` (spec: `sample_number`, 14496-12:2015 clause 8.6.2.2). `PreselectionGroupBox.entities: Entity[]` becomes `entityId: number[]`, if the current edition of the spec names the field `entity_id`. The 2015 text does not contain the box, so confirm the name against the current edition first. Remove the exported types `SyncSample` and `Entity`. `writeStss` and `writePrsl` write the numbers directly. Changelog migration: replace `box.entries.map((e) => e.sampleNumber)` with `box.sampleNumber`, and `box.entities.map((e) => e.entityId)` with `box.entityId`. If a different audit finding changes all one-column lists to plural names, apply that rule to these two fields too, so the package keeps one rule. Do not include the `Uint32Array` change of F300 in this fix. That change needs its own decision and a heap measurement on a long non-fragmented file.

confirmed.title: Only emsg has a literal type for `version`. The other 55 full box types use `number`, and the emsg helper type exposes an internal type parameter.
confirmed.breakingReason: A narrower `version` type on more boxes rejects hand-built boxes with other versions at compile time.
confirmed.evidence: FullBox.ts:7 `version: number`. tsc reports that emsg is the only IsoBoxMap member whose `version` is not `number`. sidx, prft, ctts, tfdt, mvhd, tkhd, mdhd, elst, mehd, tfra, pssh, subs, and tenc also change their layout by version, and the settled rule is that a writer follows the version. `const sidx: SegmentIndexBox = { ..., version: 7, ... }` compiles. EventMessageBox.ts:50 `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersionNumber<A extends number[] = [0, 1]>` builds a tuple of 256 elements by recursion, and its TSDoc says "Do not set this parameter."
confirmed.proposal: Keep `version: number` as the general rule, because a reader returns the value of the file. Move the range type into one internal helper and export `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersionNumber` with no parameter. Reuse the same helper if another box gets a version union later. Do not add literal versions to other boxes unless the reader also returns a distinct shape for each version, as emsg does.

fact.reason: Every code fact holds at HEAD 8ce63c212. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/FullBox.ts:7 is `version: number`. A grep for `version:` in src/boxes finds only EventMessageBox.ts:27 (`version: 0`), :39 (`version: 1`) and :65 (`version: EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersionNumber`). 56 files in src/boxes contain `FullBox &`, one of them is EventMessageBox.ts, so 55 other full box types is correct. I did not run tsc, the grep shows the same result. EventMessageBox.ts:50-53 has the parameter `A extends number[] = [0, 1]` and recurses until `A['length'] extends 256`, and line 46 says "Do not set this parameter." The parameter is public: config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md:223 shows it. The 13 readers named do branch on version (readSidx.ts:21, readPrft.ts:27, readCtts.ts:21 and :25, readTfdt.ts:26, readMvhd.ts:22, readTkhd.ts:20, readMdhd.ts:20, readElst.ts:20, readMehd.ts:24, readTfra.ts:30, readPssh.ts:27, readSubs.ts:21, readTenc.ts:35). SegmentIndexBox is `FullBox & {...}` with no `version` override, so `version: 7` compiles. Small errors: SegmentIndexBox.ts:11 is `type: 'sidx'`, the declaration is line 10. The main error is the `breaking: true` flag. Its reason describes narrower versions on other boxes, which the proposal itself rejects. The actual proposal only removes the accumulator parameter of a type that is still under `## [Unreleased]` (CHANGELOG.md:29, package.json version 1.0.7, npm latest 1.0.7). No published adopter can break.
fact.correction: The fix is not breaking. `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersionNumber` is unreleased, so the parameter can go before the type ships. Proposal detail to fix: a helper that is not exported from the entry point produces an `ae-forgotten-export` warning in the API report (the report already has one for `ReadableStreamBase` at cml-iso-bmff.api.md:479). Either export the helper with an `@internal` tag or accept the warning. The file reference for sidx is SegmentIndexBox.ts:10, not :11.
fact.priorDecision: PR 676 (commit 755330372, issue 667) added the literal 2 to 255 version for emsg on purpose: unknown versions keep the known fields with empty values, with no compile break for adopters. test/int64.types.test.ts:844-854 pins the 2 to 255 range. The literal emsg version is intentional. The exposed accumulator parameter is an implementation detail of that PR, not a decision.
