Remove the type parameter before the release that first publishes the type. The change then breaks no adopter. Keep the exported name and the values 2 to 255:

type ByteValue<A extends number[] = []> = A['length'] extends 256 ? A[number] : ByteValue<[...A, A['length']]>
export type EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersionNumber = Exclude<ByteValue, 0 | 1>

`ByteValue` stays out of the entry point. The API report then shows a second `ae-forgotten-export` warning next to the one for `ReadableStreamBase`. If the maintainers want no new warning, write the union of 2 to 255 as literal numbers in the exported type. The type test at libs/iso-bmff/test/int64.types.test.ts:846-851 passes with both forms. Do not add literal versions to other boxes, and keep `FullBox.version: number`.

confirmed.title: With the `bigint` option, an emsg box of an unrecognized version has `presentationTime` as a `number`, which differs from the documented rule that each field has one type for every version.
confirmed.breakingReason: The field type of `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersion.presentationTime` and the returned value change for callers of the `bigint` option.
confirmed.evidence: EventMessageBox.ts:63-68 `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersion = EventMessageBoxBase & { version: ...; presentationTimeDelta: number; presentationTime: number }` has no `V`, while `EventMessageBoxV1<V>` has `presentationTime: V`. readEmsg.ts:70 `presentationTime: 0`. The guide states at reading-boxes.md:164: "Each field has one type for every version of its box." With `readInt64AsBigInt`, `presentationTime` is a `bigint` for version 1 and the number 0 for version 2 or above.
confirmed.proposal: Either give the type the parameter (`EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersion<V>` with `presentationTime: V`, and the reader gets the zero through the `int64` function), or add one sentence on this exception to the table section of the reading guide. The decision to keep the known fields with empty values does not change.

fact.reason:
Every cited fact holds at HEAD. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/EventMessageBox.ts:64-68 declares `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersion = EventMessageBoxBase & { version: ...; presentationTimeDelta: number; presentationTime: number }` with no type parameter, while line 38-41 has `EventMessageBoxV1<V>` with `presentationTime: V`. libs/iso-bmff/src/readers/readEmsg.ts:70 returns `presentationTime: 0` for a version of 2 or above. libs/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md:164 states "Each field has one type for every version of its box." So with `readInt64AsBigInt`, `presentationTime` is a `bigint` for version 1 and the number 0 for version 2 to 255. The public API report matches (config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md:216-220).

Two details weaken the finding. First, the state is a recorded and tested trade-off, not an oversight. The description of PR 676 lists it under "These cases compile differently", and libs/iso-bmff/test/int64.types.test.ts:831 pins it with `expectType<Equal<typeof box.presentationTime, bigint | number>>(true)`. Second, the first proposal does not work as written. `IsoInt64Reader` (src/IsoInt64Reader.ts) is `(view, size, signed) => V`, a function that reads bytes at the cursor of the view. The reader has no zero bytes to read for a version of 2 or above, and PR 676 gives exactly that reason. The guide is also less contradictory than the finding says: the table row at docs/reading-boxes.md:111 limits the option to "`presentationTime` of a version 1 box". The sentence at line 164 is still literally false for `emsg`, and the row dates from PR 645, before the type for versions 2 to 255 existed.
fact.correction: The mismatch is real, but it is a known trade-off of PR 676 with a type test, not an unnoticed defect. The proposal "the reader gets the zero through the `int64` function" is not possible with the current `IsoInt64Reader` contract, because that function reads bytes from the view and returns no constant. A typed zero needs one of three things: a scratch view over 8 zero bytes (an allocation and extra bytes for every such box), a new zero member in the option contract (which conflicts with the settled rules of rfc/uint64-reader-config.md), or the removal of `presentationTime` and `presentationTimeDelta` from the type for versions 2 to 255 (which touches the settled rule that unknown versions keep the known fields). The option that fits the settled decisions is the documentation one: add one sentence after docs/reading-boxes.md:164 that an `emsg` box of version 2 or above has `presentationTime` as the number 0 in every mode. That change is not breaking. If the cursor API of the RFC gives readers direct access to the `int64` function, the typed zero can be reconsidered there.
fact.priorDecision: PR 676 (commit 755330372, fixes issue 667). The PR description states: "With the `bigint` mode of the `int64` option, `presentationTime` in that branch has the type `bigint | number`. The reader cannot create a zero of the type of the `int64` option, because the option is a function that reads bytes. The `int64` option is not released yet." The type test libs/iso-bmff/test/int64.types.test.ts:831 pins this type.

value.reason:
The facts are right. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/EventMessageBox.ts:64-68 declares `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersion` with no `V` and `presentationTime: number`. EventMessageBox.ts:38-41 has `presentationTime: V` for version 1. libs/iso-bmff/src/readers/readEmsg.ts:70 returns `presentationTime: 0`. libs/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md:164 states "Each field has one type for every version of its box" with no exception.

The current state is intentional. The description of PR 676 (commit 755330372, fixes issue 667) names this exact case and gives the reason: the reader cannot create a zero of the option type, because the option is a function that reads bytes. libs/iso-bmff/test/int64.types.test.ts:827-832 asserts the behavior: `presentationTime` is `number` for a version other than 0 or 1, and `bigint | number` after `version !== 0`.

The first option of the proposal is wrong. `IsoInt64Reader` (libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoInt64Reader.ts:21-25) takes a view, a size, and a sign, and reads bytes at the view position. To get a zero through that function, `readEmsg` must build a second view over 4 zero bytes for each such box, or read the first bytes of `messageData`, which gives a wrong value. The first way adds an allocation and bundle bytes to `readEmsg` (264 bytes min + gzip today, per PR 676) for a box version that no specification defines. Issue 667 states that no real file with such a box is known. The settled rules keep the `int64` function signature (rfc/uint64-reader-config.md, and rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:241 keeps the names and rules), so a second "zero" parameter is not available. The mixed type also fails at compile time (`bigint | number`), so adopters get no silent wrong value.

The second option of the proposal is right: the guide sentence at reading-boxes.md:164 is too absolute. The table at reading-boxes.md:111 already limits the field to "`presentationTime` of a version 1 box", so one sentence closes the gap. That change is documentation only and breaks nothing. The settled decision (unknown emsg versions keep the known fields with empty values) does not change.

The reader cannot create a zero of the type of the `int64` option, because the option is a function that reads bytes." value.correction: Do not add a type parameter to `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersion` and do not change `readEmsg`. Keep `presentationTime: number` and the literal 0. Fix the documentation only: after the sentence at libs/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md:164, add one sentence, for example: "One exception exists. An `emsg` box of a version other than 0 or 1 has no `presentationTime` field in the syntax, so the reader returns the number 0." Optionally add the same fact to the TSDoc of `EventMessageBoxUnrecognizedVersion` (EventMessageBox.ts:55-63), which now says only "the numbers are 0". confirmed.title: The package exports no names for the flag bits, although the writers decide the written fields from `flags`.
confirmed.breakingReason: The change only adds exports.
confirmed.evidence: The flag values exist only as literals inside readers and writers: readTfhd.ts:25-29 `0x01`, `0x02`, `0x08`, `0x10`, `0x20`. readTrun `0x1`, `0x4`, `0x100`, `0x200`, `0x400`, `0x800`. readSchm.ts:23 `0x000001`. readPrsl.ts:25 `0x1000`, `0x2000`, `0x4000`. `grep '^export const' src` finds only CONTAINERS and the six field constants. A caller who builds a trun box must write `flags: 0x000b05` from the specification, and a field set without its flag bit is silently not written (settled rule). AGENTS.md asks for "union and literal types, so autocomplete guides adopters to valid values" and names the const enum pattern.
confirmed.proposal: Export one const object for each box with optional fields, in the pattern of CmcdObjectType: `TfhdFlags`, `TrunFlags`, `SchmFlags`, `PrslFlags`, `DataEntryFlags`, with member names from the specification text, for example `TrunFlags.DATA_OFFSET_PRESENT = 0x000001`. Measure the bundle cost of an object against separate constants before the choice. The objects are additive, so they can also ship in a minor version.

fact.reason:

Evidence read:

- libs/iso-bmff/src/readers/readPrsl.ts:25-27: `0x1000`, `0x2000`, `0x4000`. Same in src/writers/writePrsl.ts:25, 26, 34, 64.

Details that are wrong or incomplete:
1. writeTrun.ts:28 is `const samplesSize = sampleSize * box.sampleCount`, not a flag test. The flag tests are at lines 19-26 and 37-56.
2. The grep result is seven constants in IsoBoxFields.ts, not six: the six field constants plus the `IsoBoxFields` object (line 51), then `CONTAINERS`.

The tkhd flags (14496-12-2015.txt:1966-1975) are in the same position.
4. The prsl flag values are not in the 2015 edition, so I could not check those three values or their names against spec text.

I found no prior decision: no mention in rfc/, in libs/iso-bmff/CHANGELOG.md, or in a GitHub issue search for flag constants.
fact.correction: The package exports no name for a flag bit. The literals are in readTfhd.ts:25-29 and writeTfhd.ts:23-59, readTrun.ts:21-41 and writeTrun.ts:19-56 (not line 28), readSchm.ts:23 and writeSchm.ts:19, readPrsl.ts:25-27 and writePrsl.ts:25-64, writeUrl.ts:19, and readLabl.ts:21. `grep '^export const' src` finds `CONTAINERS`, the six field constants, and the `IsoBoxFields` object. Take the prsl names from a newer edition of 14496-12, because the 2015 text does not contain that box. Prefer separate `export const` values or measure a const object first: a bundler keeps a whole object when a caller reads one member through a namespace or a dynamic key, and tree-shakeability ranks above developer experience in this project. The change is additive and does not need the major version.

For size 0, document that a child box extends to the end of its parent. When writeIsoBoxes copies a raw box with size 0, write the real size into the header.

Every factual statement holds at HEAD 8ce63c212.

Code: libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:383-384 has `} else if (size === 0) { actualSize = bytesRemaining }`. Line 369 requires `bytesRemaining >= 8` before the header read, so 1 to 7 bytes set `truncated` and throw `Truncated box` (lines 390-393). The iterator at lines 476-479 stops on that error. `bytesRemaining` (line 142) is relative to the view, and a child view is a slice of the parent, so a size 0 child ends at the end of its parent.

Test: libs/iso-bmff/test/readIsoBoxes.test.ts:42-47 `should exit if garbage is zero` reads 1500 zero bytes and asserts `boxes.length === 1` and `boxes[0].size === 0`.

Probe (script in the scratchpad, run against src with node --experimental-transform-types, no repo file changed): a `moov` box with a `free` child and N zero bytes. N = 0, 1, 4, 7 returns only `free`. N = 8, 9, 12, 16 returns `free` and a box with type `\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000` and size 0 that takes all the remaining bytes. The same result occurs at the top level. The current `writeIsoBoxes` already writes that box back (8 or 12 bytes) and writes nothing for 4 zero bytes. So the write asymmetry exists today, not only with the raw box of the RFC.

Guide: libs/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md:91 says a size of 0 `means that the box extends to the end of the data`. Line 93 documents the 4 zero bytes case. The sentence `A write therefore omits those bytes` is on line 95, not 93. That is a small citation offset, and the statement is correct.

RFC: rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:87 says a box with no reader becomes a raw box and `writeIsoBoxes` copies a raw box unchanged. The inference (8 zero bytes are kept, 4 are dropped) follows.

Spec: 14496-12-2015.txt:941-943 has the quoted text `if size is 0, then this box is the last one in the file, and its contents extend to the end of the file (normally only used for a Media Data Box)`.

I could not refute any statement. One nuance: line 93 of the guide says `The same rule applies to the child boxes of a container`, so a reader can infer that "the data" means the parent for a child box. The guide does not state it directly.
fact.correction: The proposal needs two changes. (1) Do not rewrite the header of every raw box with size 0. A size 0 `mdat` box as the last box of a file follows the specification, and the RFC contract says a raw box is copied unchanged. A rewrite changes the bytes of a compliant box and needs a 16-byte header above 4 GB. Limit the proposal to documentation: a raw box with size 0 is only valid as the last box of the output, and a size 0 child box extends to the end of its parent. (2) The write asymmetry exists in the current code, not only with the raw box of the RFC: `writeIsoBoxes` writes the null-type box back today. The sentence about omitted bytes is on line 95 of the guide.
fact.priorDecision: No decision covers 8 or more zero bytes. Related records: issue 650 (CHANGELOG.md:81) defined the stop rule only for 1 to 7 bytes, based on QuickTime files with 4 zero bytes. Issue 663 (CHANGELOG.md:85-86) added the stop for a size below the header size. The test `should exit if garbage is zero` (test/readIsoBoxes.test.ts:42, present since the CML version 1 commit 8ac3ef9b9) pins the current result of one size 0 box, and the guide line 91 states that a size of 0 is valid. The facts are correct. The main proposal (stop before a header with four zero type bytes) is wrong for adopters.

Code read: libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:368 `if (bytesRemaining >= cursor)` and :383 `} else if (size === 0) { actualSize = bytesRemaining }`. Fewer than 8 bytes cannot be a header, so the read stops. Eight zero bytes are a complete header with size 0, so the box extends to the end of the view. `bytesRemaining` is the parent view for a child box, so a child with size 0 ends at its parent.

Probe against src/index.ts (node, no build), a `moov` box with a `free` child plus N zero bytes, read then written with the default configs:
- N=4: children `free`, source 24 bytes, written 20
- N=7: children `free`, source 27, written 20
- N=8: children `free`, `\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000` (size 0), source 28, written 28
- N=12: same two children, source 32, written 32
So today the 8-byte case is the lossless one. libs/iso-bmff/src/utils/writeBox.ts:33 `} else if ('view' in box) { view = box.view }` copies the box unchanged. The proposed reader rule would turn that case into a lossy one. The guide itself warns that dropped bytes shift the chunk offsets (docs/reading-boxes.md:95). The raw box of the RFC keeps the lossless result (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:87 "`writeIsoBoxes` copies a raw box unchanged").

Spec: 14496-12-2015.txt:941-943, "if size is 0, then this box is the last one in the file, and its contents extend to the end of the file". The type field has no rule against zero bytes ("normally four printable characters", line 944). The current read is the literal syntax. The proposal admits that its rule "is not in the specification", which conflicts with the project rule not to invent extensions. shaka-player does the same as CML: lib/util/mp4_parser.js:158 `case 0: size = reader.getLength() - start`.

The 1 to 7 byte result is a deliberate decision of PR 661 (commit 7d67e217a): "The parsed box does not record those bytes, so a write omits them." A field for those bytes would break the settled rule about boxes that break the spec. The difference between 7 and 8 bytes therefore follows from the header size and is not an accident.

What is real: (1) docs/reading-boxes.md:91 says a size of 0 "means that the box extends to the end of the data". For a child box the code stops at the end of the parent. (2) The RFC contract (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:193-198) says only "`readIsoBoxes` stops before a truncated box, as in version 1" and does not state the size 0 rule or the result for zero bytes. (3) A raw box with size 0 is valid only as the last box, and no document says so.

The header rewrite for a raw box with size 0 is a matter of taste. It ends the byte-exact copy of a compliant file (`ftyp`, `moov`, `mdat` with size 0) and breaks the RFC sentence "copies a raw box unchanged". A box of 2^32 bytes or more would also need a `largesize` header, which moves every byte after it. The gain exists only when an adopter writes a box after a size 0 box.
value.priorDecision: PR 662 (commit 6c788e430, issue 663) states "A `size` of 0 stays valid" and adds the tests `should read a last box with the size 0 to the end of the data` and `should read a last box with the size 0 and no body` (libs/iso-bmff/test/incompleteBoxHeader.test.ts:208, :222). PR 661 (commit 7d67e217a, issue 650) chose to stop before fewer than 8 bytes, to record no field for those bytes, and to let a write omit them. The test `should exit if garbage is zero` (libs/iso-bmff/test/readIsoBoxes.test.ts:42) pins one box of size 0 for 1500 zero bytes since the first version of the readers. No decision covers the wording of the guide for a child box with size 0.
value.correction:
Keep the reader as it is. Do not add a rule for a type of four zero bytes. Make three documentation changes, none of which breaks adopters:
1. docs/reading-boxes.md:91: state that a `size` of 0 extends the box to the end of the data, and to the end of the parent box for a child box. Add that 8 or more zero bytes after the last box are therefore one box with size 0 and a type of four null characters, and that a write keeps those bytes.
2. rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md, section Contract: state the same two rules next to "`readIsoBoxes` stops before a truncated box". Bytes that cannot form a header (1 to 7) are not in the result and a write omits them. A header with size 0 becomes a raw box (or a typed box whose writer computes the real size) that covers the bytes to the end of the enclosing box.
3. Same section and docs/writing-boxes.md: state that `writeIsoBoxes` copies a raw box with size 0 unchanged, so that box must stay the last box of the output. Record the header rewrite as an open question of the RFC and not as a requirement. If the maintainers want it, limit it to boxes below 2^32 bytes and write the 4 size bytes in the output array, so the raw input stays untouched.

confirmed.evidence: The package root exports `UTF8`, `UINT`, `TEMPLATE`, `STRING`, `INT`, `DATA`, the object `IsoBoxFields` and the type `IsoFieldTypeMap`. Their only use is the `type` argument of `readArray` and `writeArray`. The RFC replaces both methods with a loop and does not list these exports. `writeArray` accepts every key of IsoFieldTypeMap but handles three: `type === UINT ? this.writeUint : type === TEMPLATE ? this.writeTemplate : this.writeInt`, so 'string', 'utf8' and 'data' are written as integers. `ParsedBox` exists to add `view`, `size`, `largesize` and `usertype`, which the RFC removes. The name `IsoBoxReadViewConfig` refers to a class that the RFC removes. The comment `// TODO: Change all sizes from bits to bytes` is out of date, because the sizes are bytes.

Keep one named type for that element (keep `ParsedIsoBox<V>` with a new definition, or state a rename in the RFC) and update docs/reading-boxes.md:239-247. fact.priorDecision: No decision keeps these exports for their own sake. The cursor RFC (Drawbacks) says the names of that RFC "do not change", and the settled list for this audit names only the int64 option, `IsoInt64`, `IsoInt64Reader`, `readInt64AsBigInt`, and `createInt64OverflowReader`. A rename of `IsoBoxReadViewConfig` therefore needs an explicit line in the cursor RFC.

Commit d395df3ce (PR 673) is an ancestor of HEAD, and the RFC commit 8ce63c212 was written after it, so the RFC text is a regression in wording, not a new decision. The RFC has no text that argues for a reversal, and rfc/iso-bmff-container-readers-writers.md:42 and :148 define automatic container handling only for the 19 types in `CONTAINERS`. The read side has the same split in version 1: isContainer.ts:29 is `'boxes' in box || CONTAINERS.includes(box.type)`, and the commit message of PR 673 keeps `isContainer` unchanged on purpose for traverseIsoBoxes. In version 1 a parsed `meta` box or sample entry with a reader and no writer writes its `view` bytes (writeBox.ts:32 to 33). The RFC removes `view` (line 199), and only a box with no reader is a raw box with `bytes` (line 87). So in version 2 that box has no source bytes and must throw. The RFC does not state this change.

confirmed.title: The write view has three string methods with two encodings, the built-in writers use none of the two terminated methods, and the method with the short name writes Latin-1 that the built-in readers decode as UTF-8.
confirmed.breakingReason: Method names change and the one-byte methods are removed. The RFC already replaces these methods with field functions.
confirmed.evidence: `writeString` and `writeTerminatedString` write `value.charCodeAt(c)` in one byte. `writeUtf8TerminatedString` encodes UTF-8. No method writes UTF-8 with no terminator. The read side uses `readString(size)` and `readUtf8(size)` with the size -1 for a terminated string, so the names of the two sides do not match.
confirmed.proposal: 2.0.0 has one encoding for text, UTF-8, and the same names on both sides: `readUtf8(cursor, length)` and `writeUtf8(cursor, value)` for a string with no terminator, `readUtf8Terminated(cursor)` and `writeUtf8Terminated(cursor, value)` for a null-terminated string. Every factual statement holds at HEAD 8ce63c212.

Source read:
- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxWriteView.ts:226-230 `writeString` and :242-248 `writeTerminatedString` both call `this.writeUint(value.charCodeAt(c), 1)`. :255-261 `writeUtf8TerminatedString` uses `encodeText(value)` and then `this.writeUint(0, 1)`. The class has no UTF-8 method without a terminator.

No writer calls them. `writeString` is called only for four-character codes: IsoBoxWriteView.ts:326/330 (box type), writeHdlr.ts:33, writeFtyp.ts:23/27, writeStyp.ts:23/27.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/writers/writeKind.ts:27-30 is `writer.writeBytes(schemeUriBytes)`, `writer.writeUint(0, 1)`, `writer.writeBytes(valueBytes)`, `writer.writeUint(0, 1)`. Fourteen writers import `encodeText` and follow the same pattern.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:267 `readString = (size: number)` and :304 `readUtf8 = (size: number = Infinity)`. Lines 187-199 handle `size === -1` as the terminated form for both types.
- Readers: every terminated string is `readUtf8(-1)` (readKind.ts:18-19, readHdlr.ts:22, readUrl, readUrn, readSchm, readElng, readLabl, readPrsl, readVlab, readIden, readSttg, readPayl, readEmsg.ts:37-38/56-57). `readString` is called only with 4 (readFtyp.ts:17, readHdlr.ts:20) plus `readArray(STRING, 4, length)` in readFtyp.ts:20. No `readString(-1)`.

Runtime check (script in the scratchpad, imports src, no repo change):
- `writeTerminatedString('é')` writes `e9 00`. `readUtf8(-1)` returns U+FFFD.
- `writeString('€uro')` writes `ac 75 72 6f`.
- `writeKind({schemeUri: 'a\0b', value: 'v'})` writes `61 00 62 00 76 00`. `readKind` returns `schemeUri: 'a'`, `value: 'b'`.

Two precision notes that do not change the verdict:
1. "Latin-1" is exact only for code units up to U+00FF. Above that, `setUint8` keeps the low byte (the finding's own `€` example shows `ac`).
2. The built-in pairs have no mismatch today. The built-in writers use `writeString` only for four-character codes, and the readers decode those with `readString(4)`. The mismatch reaches only an adopter who calls `writeString` or `writeTerminatedString` for a text field in a custom writer.

Overlap with the RFC: rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:185 maps `view.readString(size)`, `view.readUtf8(size)` to `readString`, `readUtf8`, and line 193 says the write cursor has the same field functions with the `write` prefix. The RFC therefore already aligns the base names. It does not state the terminated form, the fate of size -1, or the removal of the one-byte text writer. That part of the finding is new.

The core facts hold. libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxWriteView.ts:226-230 (`writeString`) and :242-248 (`writeTerminatedString`) write `this.writeUint(value.charCodeAt(c), 1)`. `writeUtf8TerminatedString` at :255-261 calls `encodeText`. No method writes UTF-8 without a terminator: libs/iso-bmff/src/writers/writeVttC.ts uses `encodeText(box.config)` and `writer.writeBytes(configBytes)`. A grep of `src` finds no caller of `writeTerminatedString` or `writeUtf8TerminatedString` outside the class. Every terminated string in the built-in readers is `view.readUtf8(-1)` (readKind.ts:18-19, readHdlr.ts:22, readEmsg.ts:37-38 and others). No reader calls `readString(-1)`.

One claim in the title is wrong. `writeString` has five callers: writeHdlr.ts:33 (`handlerType`), writeFtyp.ts:23 and :27, writeStyp.ts:23 and :27. All five write four-character codes. The readers read them with `view.readString(4)` (readHdlr.ts:20, readFtyp.ts:17) and `readArray(STRING, 4, length)` (readFtyp.ts:20), which also use one byte for each character. So the built-in reader and writer pairs agree. The encoding mismatch exists only for a custom writer that calls `writeTerminatedString` or `writeString` for a text field.

The current state is a v1 limit, not a choice to keep. PR 633 (b6cedb096) replaced `writeUtf8TerminatedString` with `encodeText` plus `writeBytes` because each v1 writer needs the byte length for its size code. The RFC removes that size code. The commit of PR 643 (6b2a23c36) states: "No built-in writer calls IsoBoxWriteView.writeTerminatedString after this change, so a new test file calls the method directly." The method stayed only because it is public.

Spec check, 14496-12:2015 text: line 2247 (`hdlr` name), 3190 (`url `, `urn `), 5739 (`schm`) and the sample entry strings define null-terminated UTF-8. Line 2413: "All string fields shall be null-terminated". One exception exists: `cprt` notice at line 4686 allows UTF-8 or UTF-16. The package has no `cprt` reader, and a custom reader can use the byte function. A four-character code is not UTF-8 text (box types such as `©nam` have a byte above 0x7F), so the one-byte decode must stay for that function.

The proposal breaks no settled decision. The draft RFC rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:185 maps `view.readString(size)`, `view.readUtf8(size)` to `readString`, `readUtf8` and line 191 gives the write cursor "the same field functions with the `write` prefix". The RFC does not define the terminated form, the size -1, or the three v1 write methods, so this finding fills a real gap in the RFC. The break is real but small, because the RFC already changes every custom reader and writer. The bytes of the built-in writers do not change.
value.priorDecision: No decision keeps the current state. Issue 631 and PRs 637 (aecfdfa19) and 643 (6b2a23c36) moved every built-in text field to UTF-8 and left `writeTerminatedString` and `readString(-1)` in place only as public v1 methods. PR 633 (b6cedb096, issue 632) is the reason the writers call `encodeText` and `writeBytes`: one encode for the v1 size code. Two read rules are settled and must survive the rename: a terminated read with no null byte stops at the end of the box (issue 635, PRs 639 and 642), and issue 647 (`hdlr` name with no null byte) is closed as not planned.
value.correction:
Correct the statement: the built-in pairs agree, because `writeString` and `readString(4)` are used only for four-character codes (hdlr handlerType, ftyp and styp brands). The trap is for custom writers only.

Corrected proposal, as an amendment to row 185 and line 191 of rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:
1. `readUtf8(cursor, length)` and `writeUtf8(cursor, value)` for text with no terminator. `length` is required. A reader that needs the rest of the box passes `cursor.end - cursor.pos` (readVttC). A length past `cursor.end` throws, as the RFC contract states.
2. `readUtf8Terminated(cursor)` and `writeUtf8Terminated(cursor, value)`. The size -1 is removed. `readUtf8Terminated` keeps the rule of issue 635: with no null byte, the function stops at `cursor.end` and does not throw. Without this exception the RFC contract would make `hdlr` boxes with no terminator throw (issue 647).
3. `readFourCc(cursor)` and `writeFourCc(cursor, value)` replace `readString(4)` and `writeString`. Both keep one byte for each character, with no length parameter. No generic one-byte string function is exported. A custom reader with another fixed-size field uses `readBytes`.
4. `writeString`, `writeTerminatedString` and `writeUtf8TerminatedString` have no successor with those names. The built-in writers call `writeUtf8Terminated`, because the growing buffer removes the need for the byte length that caused PR 633.
5. The TSDoc of the two write functions states that the writer does not check for a null character in the value. No throw, in line with the settled writer rules.
Out of scope for this finding, but related: `schm.schemeType` and `frma.dataFormat` are numbers from `readUint(4)` (readSchm.ts, readFrma.ts), while brands and `handlerType` are strings. A `readFourCc` name makes that difference visible, so decide it in the same RFC pass.

confirmed.breakingReason: `defaultIsEncrypted` is removed, `defaultIsProtected` becomes required, and `defaultIvSize` is renamed. A box with a constant IV and a condition that is false is written with no constant IV.
confirmed.evidence: The type has `defaultIsEncrypted` (`The 3 bytes that precede default_Per_Sample_IV_Size`), and also `defaultIsProtected`, `defaultCryptByteBlock`, and `defaultSkipByteBlock`, which are parts of those 3 bytes. Writer: `(defaultIsEncrypted & 0xff00ff) | (((box.defaultCryptByteBlock ?? defaultIsEncrypted >> 12) & 0xf) << 12) | ...`. The pattern fields replace the old bits. `defaultIsProtected` does not: the type says `writeTenc does not write the field`, and a test is named `should write the lowest byte of defaultIsEncrypted and not defaultIsProtected`. The constant IV: `if (defaultConstantIvSize !== undefined) { writer.writeUint(defaultConstantIvSize, 1) ...`. ISO/IEC 23001-7:2016 clause 8.2.2 has `if (default_isProtected ==1 && default_Per_Sample_IV_Size == 0) { unsigned int(8) default_constant_IV_size; ...`. Read-only run of the source: a box with `defaultIsEncrypted: 1`, `defaultIvSize: 8`, `defaultConstantIv: [1, 2]` writes 35 bytes, and `readTenc` returns no `defaultConstantIv`. Remove `defaultIsEncrypted` and `defaultConstantIvSize`. The writer writes the constant IV only when `defaultIsProtected` is 1 and `defaultPerSampleIvSize` is 0, as the other writers follow the control fields of the box. The changelog gives the mapping from `defaultIsEncrypted`. This proposal replaces the rule of PR 658 that kept `defaultIsEncrypted` for compatibility. It needs a decision.

confirmed.title: The writing guide has wording errors and an example that fails at runtime
confirmed.evidence: (1) "In TypeScript, cast raw box objects to a box type for type safety. There are two ways." The first example is a type annotation (`const box: FileTypeBox = {...}`), not a cast. A third way follows: "You can also get a box type from `IsoBoxMap`". (2) Both examples run `for (const byteArray of byteArrays) { sourceBuffer.appendBuffer(byteArray); // wait for updateend event }`. `appendBuffer` throws an `InvalidStateError` while the previous append is in progress, so the loop fails on the second array. (3) "It takes an array of streamable items". The parameter is `Iterable<IsoBoxStreamable<IsoInt64>>`.
confirmed.proposal: (1) "In TypeScript, give a box object a box type. There are three ways." and name the third way in the list. A `satisfies FileTypeBox` example is a fourth option that keeps the literal types. (2) Await the event in the loop: `await new Promise((resolve) => sourceBuffer.addEventListener("updateend", resolve, { once: true }))`. With the single array of the cursor RFC, the loop goes away. (3) "It takes an iterable of streamable items".

fact.reason:
I read libs/iso-bmff/docs/writing-boxes.md at HEAD. All three claims hold and every cited line number matches.

(1) Line 212: "In TypeScript, cast raw box objects to a box type for type safety. There are two ways." The first example (lines 217-222) is `const box: FileTypeBox = {...}`, a type annotation and not a cast. Line 225 names "The second way". Line 236 then adds a third way: "You can also get a box type from `IsoBoxMap` with the box's FourCC". The count "two" is wrong.

(2) Lines 47-50 and 87-90 both contain `for (const byteArray of byteArrays) { sourceBuffer.appendBuffer(byteArray); // wait for updateend event }`. `sourceBuffer` is a real `SourceBuffer` (writing-boxes.context.d.ts: `declare const sourceBuffer: SourceBuffer`). Per the MSE spec, `appendBuffer` throws `InvalidStateError` while `updating` is true, so the loop as written throws on the second array. Both examples produce two or three arrays, so the second iteration is reached. Nuance: the comment `// wait for updateend event` shows that the author knew about the wait and left it out. The defect is real for a reader who copies the block, which is the project's stated standard ("copy-pasteable examples", "No pseudocode").

(3) Line 8: "It takes an array of streamable items". The signature in libs/iso-bmff/src/writeIsoBoxes.ts:20-23 is `boxes: Iterable<IsoBoxStreamable<IsoInt64>>`, and config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md:1699 shows the same.

The proposal is sound. The guide already uses top-level `await` (line 122), so an awaited `updateend` promise typechecks in the example check. `satisfies` needs TypeScript 4.9, below the documented 5.7 minimum.

confirmed.title: The docs of createInt64OverflowReader do not state that the all-ones duration of ISO/IEC 14496-12 reports an overflow
confirmed.evidence: `if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) { onOverflow(new RangeError(...)) }`. ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 for `mvhd`, `tkhd`, and `mdhd`: "If the duration cannot be determined then duration is set to all 1s." A version 1 box with that duration reads as 2^64, which is not a safe integer. The writing guide knows the value: "ISO/IEC 14496-12 uses that value for a duration that cannot be determined." The reading guide says only: "When a 64-bit value is outside the safe integer range, the callback receives a `RangeError`... If the callback throws, the read stops with that error." A callback that throws therefore stops the read of a valid init segment with an unknown duration in a version 1 header box.
confirmed.proposal: Add to the guide section and to the TSDoc: "A version 1 `mvhd`, `tkhd`, or `mdhd` box can have a `duration` with all bits set. ISO/IEC 14496-12 uses that value for a duration that cannot be determined. The callback receives a `RangeError` for that value too. Do not throw from the callback if your code reads such boxes."

fact.reason:
Every factual statement holds at HEAD 8ce63c212.

Code: libs/iso-bmff/src/createInt64OverflowReader.ts:26-28 is `if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) { onOverflow(new RangeError('64-bit value is outside the safe integer range')) }`. The TSDoc at lines 3-21 (line 8: "When a value is outside the safe integer range, the function calls `onOverflow` with a `RangeError`", line 10: "When `onOverflow` throws, the read stops with that error") does not mention the all-ones duration.

The value reaches the check: src/utils/readUint.ts:30-32 computes `s1 * Math.pow(2, 32) + s2`, which is 2^64 for all bits set. readMvhd.ts:31 (`duration: readWideUint(size)`), readTkhd.ts:30 and readMdhd.ts:23 read `duration` through `readWideUint`, and IsoBoxReadView.ts:96 routes that call to the `int64` function. The test test/createInt64OverflowReader.test.ts:63-68 ("should report the largest unsigned value") pins the behavior: value 2 ** 64, one error.

Docs: docs/reading-boxes.md:172 has the quoted sentences and no word about the all-ones duration. The table at docs/reading-boxes.md:113 lists `duration` of `mvhd`, `mdhd`, `tkhd` as a covered field. docs/writing-boxes.md:173 has the quoted sentence "ISO/IEC 14496-12 uses that value for a duration that cannot be determined." A grep of docs/, README.md, the TSDoc and rfc/uint64-reader-config.md finds that statement only in the writing guide.

Spec: 14496-12-2015.txt lines 1852-1853 (mvhd) and 2199-2200 (mdhd) have the quoted sentence verbatim. Line 1991-1992 (tkhd) reads "If the duration of this track cannot be determined then duration is set to all 1s", so the quote differs by three words for tkhd, with the same meaning.

One note on scope: the report fires only for a version 1 box (8-byte field). A version 0 box with duration 0xFFFFFFFF does not report (test line 95). The proposal text already says "version 1".
fact.priorDecision: The behavior is intentional, only the documentation gap is open. rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:151 states "A callback that throws stops the read", line 269 fixes the check as `Number.isSafeInteger`, and line 428 rejects a throw by default because "A thrown error at a `tfdt` read stops playback of a valid stream". The test at test/createInt64OverflowReader.test.ts:63-68 pins the report for 0xffffffffffffffff. No RFC text, changelog entry or guide discusses the all-ones duration on the read path.
fact.correction: The spec sentence for `tkhd` is "If the duration of this track cannot be determined then duration is set to all 1s" (14496-12-2015.txt:1991-1992). The quote in the finding is verbatim for `mvhd` and `mdhd` only. The fix is documentation only: add the note to docs/reading-boxes.md after line 172 and to the TSDoc of createInt64OverflowReader. Do not change the check.

value.reason:
The facts hold. libs/iso-bmff/src/createInt64OverflowReader.ts:26 tests `!Number.isSafeInteger(value)` and line 10 states "When `onOverflow` throws, the read stops with that error." The `duration` fields go through the option: src/readers/readMvhd.ts:31 `duration: readWideUint(size)`, src/readers/readTkhd.ts:30, src/readers/readMdhd.ts:23. The spec text (14496-12-2015.txt lines 1852-1853, 1991-1992, 2199-2200) says "If the duration cannot be determined then duration is set to all 1s" for mvhd, tkhd, and mdhd. docs/reading-boxes.md:172 describes the callback and does not name that value. docs/writing-boxes.md:173 does name it. Neither the TSDoc, the reading guide, nor rfc/uint64-reader-config.md mentions the all-ones value for the overflow reader (grep for "all 1s", "cannot be determined", "all bits" found only writing-boxes.md:173, CHANGELOG.md:96, and IsoBoxWriteView.ts:56-57).

The behavior itself is intentional, so only the documentation gap is a finding. test/createInt64OverflowReader.test.ts:63-68 has the test "should report the largest unsigned value" (0xffffffffffffffff reads as 2^64 with one error). rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:274 defines the rule as a plain `Number.isSafeInteger` test with no exception, and line 428 rejects a built-in throw because "A thrown error at a `tfdt` read stops playback of a valid stream". The RFC therefore already knows that a throwing callback stops valid streams, but it reasons only about `tfdt`. No issue, PR, or RFC text decides to leave the all-ones case out of the docs. Issue 653 and PR 669 (67bd8d7af) cover only the write side.

The proposal is documentation only and breaks no settled decision. It changes no name, type, value, or byte. The proposed text needs two changes. First, the report for all ones is technically correct, because 2^64 is not the stored value 2^64 - 1, so the text should say that the report does not mean a damaged file. Second, the text should tell the adopter how to recognize the case (the field equals 2 ** 64 after the read), not only "do not throw". Suggested guide text: "A version 1 `mvhd`, `tkhd`, or `mdhd` box can have a `duration` with all bits set. ISO/IEC 14496-12 uses that value for a duration that cannot be determined. The callback receives a `RangeError` for that value too, and the field reads as `2 ** 64`. That report does not mean that the file is damaged. If your code reads such boxes, do not throw from the callback." Link the sentence in docs/writing-boxes.md:173 to that paragraph instead of a second explanation. Do not add a special case to the function: an exception for all ones costs bytes on every adopter of the function, and the stored value 2^64 - 1 is in fact rounded. Carry the note into the guide text that the cursor API RFC rewrites.

Two parts of the finding are weaker than stated. (1) The context files are check tooling, not documentation. The site copies only `.md` files (site/scripts/packages.ts:36), the npm package ships only `dist` (libs/iso-bmff/package.json:22), and the lint ignores `*.context.d.ts` (AGENTS.md:25). No adopter sees the two types, and both compile because `readIsoBoxes(raw: IsoBoxData)` takes `ArrayBufferLike | ArrayBufferView` (config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md:360, :938). (2) The undeclared names are the documented convention of PR 573 (commit e7db0e39e), which added these files. AGENTS.md:80 says a block may use a value that the reader's code provides and that the context file declares it. The convention does not forbid a sentence that names the value, so the sentence is a valid addition, not a reversal.

The proposed type is wrong. The reading guide shows `r.arrayBuffer()` at :20, so the visible type of `buffer` is `ArrayBuffer`. A change to `Uint8Array` makes the hidden declaration disagree with the only declaration the reader sees. No spec text or settled decision applies. gh search found no issue on this topic, only PR 573.
value.priorDecision: PR 573 (commit e7db0e39e, "docs: make every README and guide example block typecheck") added the context files, and AGENTS.md:80 records the rule: a block may use a value from the reader's code, declared in `<guide>.context.d.ts`. That decision makes the undeclared names intentional. It does not decide the type mismatch or forbid an explanatory sentence.
value.correction: Use `ArrayBuffer` in utilities.context.d.ts, not `Uint8Array` in all three files. `ArrayBuffer` matches the `r.arrayBuffer()` declaration that reading-boxes.md:20 shows. Add the sentence only where no block declares the name: utilities.md before line 15 ("In the examples, `buffer` holds the bytes of a segment.") and writing-boxes.md before the first use of `sourceBuffer`, `transport` and `buffer`. reading-boxes.md needs no sentence because its first two blocks declare `buffer`. The cursor API RFC rewrites the writing guide (`writeIsoBoxes` returns one array, `IsoBoxStreamable` goes away), so add the sentence in that rewrite and not as a separate change.

value.correction:
Keep the fixture read with `readFile`. Remove only the temporary file and the Node stream adapter, in both tests (lines 42-45 and 152-155).

Stream example: `new Response(stream).arrayBuffer()` works, but it buffers the whole output, which is the job of `writeIsoBoxes`. An example that shows the streaming use is better: pipe to a web `WritableStream` sink, as the guide does. For example: `const chunks: Uint8Array[] = []` then `await stream.pipeTo(new WritableStream({ write(chunk) { chunks.push(chunk) } }))`, then compare the joined chunks with the fixture bytes. Traverse example: the proposal is good. Use a small literal tree, or the fixture, and assert the order of the types, for example `const types = Array.from(traverseIsoBoxes(boxes), box => box.type)` with a `moof` that has `mfhd` and `traf` children. confirmed.title: Four-character-code fields are a `string` in three boxes and a `number` in the others.
confirmed.breakingReason: The public type and the returned value of `dataFormat`, `schemeType`, `auxInfoType`, and `groupingType` change from `number` to `string`. `fourCcToUint32` loses its purpose.
confirmed.evidence: String: `majorBrand: string`, `compatibleBrands: string[]` (`view.readString(4)`), `handlerType: string` (`view.readString(4)`), and the box `type`. Number: `dataFormat: number` (`view.readUint(4)`), `schemeType: number` (`view.readUint(4)`), `auxInfoType?: number` (saio, saiz), `groupingType: number` (sbgp, sgpd). The spec gives all of them the same syntax, `unsigned int(32)`: `unsigned int(32) major_brand;`, `unsigned int(32) handler_type;`, `unsigned int(32) data_format = codingname;`, `unsigned int(32) scheme_type; // 4CC identifying the scheme`. Adopters pay for the difference: the test writes `schemeType: 0x63656e63, // cenc`, and the drm package has `schemeType = 1667591779` and `dataFormat: fourCcToUint32(entry.type)`. The package exports `fourCcToUint32` and no inverse function. On the write side, `writeString` writes `value.length` bytes with no check, so a brand or handler type that is not 4 characters shifts every field after it.
confirmed.proposal: One rule: a field that the spec describes as a four-character code is a `string` of 4 characters. Change `dataFormat`, `schemeType`, `auxInfoType`, and `groupingType` to `string`. In the cursor API, add one field function pair for the code, such as `readFourCc` and `writeFourCc`, and make the writer always write exactly 4 bytes. Remove `fourCcToUint32` from the public API, or keep it with an inverse function if adopters still compare integers.

confirmed.title: The package uses the name "template" for fixed-point values, the RFC keeps the name, and no helper reads a signed fixed-point value.
confirmed.breakingReason: Public names change: `readTemplate`, `writeTemplate`, `TEMPLATE`, and the `readTemplate16` and `readTemplate32` names that the RFC proposes.
confirmed.evidence: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 clause 6.2.2 defines the word: "Fields shown as \"template\" in the box descriptions are optional in the specifications that use this specification". The word marks a field with a default value. Fixed-point is a separate definition in the same clause. Many template fields are plain integers that the package reads with `readUint` or `readInt`: `template int(16) layer = 0;`, `template unsigned int(16) graphicsmode = 0;`, `template unsigned int(16) frame_count = 1;`. The package uses the word for fixed-point: "Reads an unsigned fixed-point value" on `readTemplate`, and `TEMPLATE = 'template'` is "The fixed-point field type". The RFC table keeps it: `view.readTemplate(size)` becomes `readTemplate16`, `readTemplate32`. The helper is unsigned only, so four readers divide by hand: `rate: readInt(4) / 65536`, `volume: readInt(2) / 256` (mvhd), `volume: view.readInt(2) / 256` (tkhd), `balance: view.readInt(2) / 256` (smhd), plus the matrix `.map`. The unsigned fields use the helper: `width: view.readTemplate(4)`, `samplerate: readTemplate(4)`. The write side has one method for both signs.
confirmed.proposal: In the RFC, name the field functions after what they do: `readFixed16` (8.8) and `readFixed32` (16.16) for signed values, `readUfixed16` and `readUfixed32` for unsigned values, and the same four with the `write` prefix. Use them in mvhd, tkhd, smhd, and the sample entries so that no reader divides by hand. State in the RFC that `IsoBoxFields`, the six field constants, and `IsoFieldTypeMap` go away with `readArray`.

The facts hold. Spec text line 1270 to 1279 (clause 6.2.2 of 14496-12:2015) defines "Fixed-point numbers" in one paragraph and "template" fields in the next paragraph as fields with a default value. Template fields that are plain integers: `template int(16) layer = 0;` (line 1952), `template unsigned int(16) frame_count = 1;` (line 9339), `template unsigned int(16) channelcount = 2;` (line 9590). The package uses the word for the number format: libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxFields.ts:17-22 ("The fixed-point field type", `TEMPLATE = 'template'`), libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:272-280 ("Reads an unsigned fixed-point value"), libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxWriteView.ts:302-314 (stores a negative value as two's complement, `const shift = size === 4 ? 16 : 8`). libs/iso-bmff/src/utils/readTemplate.ts:5-6 reads both halves with `readUint`. The signed fields divide by hand: readMvhd.ts:32-33, readTkhd.ts:34, readSmhd.ts:18. The writers of the same fields call `writeTemplate`: writeMvhd.ts:54-55, writeTkhd.ts:63, writeSmhd.ts:25. rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:184 keeps the name as `readTemplate16`, `readTemplate32`, and the RFC has no line about `IsoBoxFields`, the field constants, or `IsoFieldTypeMap` (grep returns nothing), although line 189 replaces `readArray` with a loop.

Prior decisions: `git log -S` shows the name arrived with 8ac3ef9b9 (CML Version 1, #265), inherited from codem-isoboxer. No commit, issue, or RFC chooses the name on purpose. `gh issue list` finds no issue on the name. PR 620 (a13db9ace) chose two things on purpose for version 1: `readTemplate` stays unsigned, and the three readers divide by hand. PR 620 also measured a shared helper for the 2.30 matrix entries as larger than the inline expression (1320 B and 1331 B against 1314 B). RFC question 5 (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:275) says the field function names are proposals. The settled rule "spec first, never codem-isoboxer parity" supports the rename. The RFC already removes `view.readTemplate`, so the rename adds no migration cost beyond the cursor API.

The proposal needs three changes. (1) No box in src/ has an unsigned 8.8 field. The only 2-byte uses are `volume` (mvhd, tkhd) and `balance` (smhd), all signed. `readUfixed16` and `writeUfixed16` would be exports with no use case. (2) "No reader divides by hand" cannot cover the matrix. The entries u, v, w are 2.30 (readMvhd.ts:37, readTkhd.ts:39, writeMvhd.ts:60, writeTkhd.ts:67), and PR 620 measured the inline expression as the smallest form. (3) `readFixed32` is ambiguous in a box that has both 16.16 and 2.30 fields in 32 bits.
value.priorDecision: PR 620 (commit a13db9ace, merged 2026-11-10) kept `readTemplate` unsigned on purpose ("readTemplate stays unsigned, because width, height, the resolutions, and samplerate are unsigned") and chose the hand division in readMvhd, readTkhd, and readSmhd. The same PR measured an inline 2.30 matrix expression as smaller than a shared helper. That decision covers the sign split in version 1 only. No decision covers the name `template`: it came from codem-isoboxer in 8ac3ef9b9 (#265), and RFC question 5 of rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md leaves the field function names open.
value.correction: Rename in the cursor RFC before 2.0.0 exports the names, with three read functions and no more: signed 8.8 (`volume`, `balance`), signed 16.16 (`rate`), and unsigned 16.16 (`width`, `height`, `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, `samplerate`). Do not add an unsigned 8.8 function, because no box uses one. Put the format in the name, for example `readFixed8_8`, `readFixed16_16`, `readUfixed16_16`, because `readFixed32` can mean 16.16 or 2.30 in `mvhd` and `tkhd`. If the RFC prefers the bit-width suffix of `readUint16`, then `readFixed16`, `readFixed32`, `readUfixed32` is the fallback, with the format stated in the TSDoc. The write side follows the RFC rule of one `write` function for each read function. The stored bytes are the same for both signs, so the signed and unsigned 16.16 writers can share one body. Keep the matrix expression inline in the four mvhd and tkhd functions unless a new measurement in the cursor build shows a helper is smaller (PR 620 measured the helper as 6 to 17 B larger). State in the RFC that `IsoBoxFields`, the six field constants (`UINT`, `INT`, `TEMPLATE`, `STRING`, `DATA`, `UTF8`), and `IsoFieldTypeMap` leave the public API with `readArray` and `writeArray`. Remove the word "template" from the TSDoc of the fixed-point functions.

confirmed.title: Field names follow two casing rules: camelCase on word boundaries in most boxes, and the unbroken lowercase of the spec in six boxes.
confirmed.breakingReason: Public field names of the sample entries, vmhd, and hmhd change.
confirmed.evidence: Lowercase runs copied from the spec: `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate` (audio sample entry), `horizresolution`, `vertresolution` (visual sample entry), `graphicsmode`, `opcolor` (vmhd), `maxPDUsize`, `avgPDUsize`, `maxbitrate`, `avgbitrate` (hmhd). The same type breaks its own rule: the spec has `string[32] compressorname;` and the package has `compressorName`. The same words are camelCase elsewhere: `sampleSize` and `sampleCount` (stsz, trun), `frameCount`, `timescale` aside. So an adopter writes `entry.samplesize` in one box and `box.sampleSize` in another. Acronyms are lower camel everywhere (`trackId`, `schemeUri`, `defaultKid`, `defaultIvSize`, `sapType`) except `maxPDUsize` and `avgPDUsize`. Abbreviations differ too: `ntpTimestampSec`, `ntpTimestampFrac` against `mediaRateFraction`. One count name differs from the spec for no reason: `rangesCount` for `range_count`.
confirmed.proposal: One rule: the spec name, split on English word boundaries, in lower camel case, with acronyms as words. Rename to `channelCount`, `sampleSize`, `sampleRate`, `horizResolution`, `vertResolution`, `graphicsMode`, `opColor`, `maxPduSize`, `avgPduSize`, `maxBitrate`, `avgBitrate`, and `rangeCount`. List the renames in one changelog table.

alsoReportedAs.title: The field names of the sample entry types mix two casing rules: `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate`, `horizresolution`, `vertresolution` next to `compressorName`, `frameCount`, `dataReferenceIndex`.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: AudioSampleEntryBox.ts:20-24 `channelcount: number`, `samplesize: number`, `samplerate: number`. VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:24-28 `horizresolution: number`, `vertresolution: number`, `frameCount: number`, `compressorName: number[]`. The spec syntax spells `compressorname` in one word (`string[32] compressorname;`, 12.1.3.2), exactly like `horizresolution` and `channelcount`. So the package applies camel case to `compressorname` and not to the other one-word names. The semantics clause 12.2.3.3 itself writes `ChannelCount`, `SampleSize`, `SampleRate`. The same one-word names exist in `vmhd` (`graphicsmode`, `opcolor`) and `hmhd` (`maxbitrate`, `avgbitrate`), outside my scope.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Choose one rule and apply it to every box. Recommended: camel case by word, so `channelCount`, `sampleSize`, `sampleRate`, `horizResolution`, `vertResolution`, `compressorName`, `frameCount`. An adopter then never has to remember which spec names have an underscore. The alternative is the literal spec rule, which renames only `compressorName` to `compressorname`.

alsoReportedAs.title: The visual sample entry type (encv) mixes the lower-case spec names horizresolution and vertresolution with camel-case names for the other fields
alsoReportedAs.evidence: `horizresolution: number`, `vertresolution: number` next to `compressorName`, `frameCount`, and `dataReferenceIndex`. The spec names are `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, and `compressorname`. The package changed `compressorname` to camel case and kept the other two names as one lower-case word.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Rename to `horizResolution` and `vertResolution`, to match `compressorName`. Record the rule in the docs: a field name is the spec name in camel case, with a word break where the spec name joins two words.

alsoReportedAs.title: `compressorName` splits a one-word spec name, but `horizresolution` and `vertresolution` in the same type do not.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Type: `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, `frameCount`, `compressorName`. Spec: `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, `frame_count`, `compressorname`. `AudioSampleEntryBox` keeps the one-word spec names `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate`. The rule in the package is: an underscore in the spec name becomes a capital letter, and a name with no underscore stays as written. `compressorName` is the only field in these types that breaks the rule.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Rename the field to `compressorname` in the same change that makes the field a string. The alternative is one readable form for all (`horizResolution`, `vertResolution`, `channelCount`, `sampleSize`, `sampleRate`), but that form needs five renames and departs from the spec names.

alsoReportedAs.title: `VisualSampleEntryBox.compressorName` breaks the field name rule that its sibling fields follow.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Spec: `string[32] compressorname;`, `template unsigned int(32) horizresolution`, `unsigned int(16) frame_count`. Package: `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, `channelcount`, `samplerate`, `graphicsmode` keep the spec spelling, and `frameCount` converts an underscore. `compressorName` has a capital letter that no underscore justifies.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: `compressorname`, to follow the rule "convert snake case to camel case and change nothing else". Fix it together with the change of the field to a string.

alsoReportedAs.title: VisualSampleEntryBox mixes two naming rules for spec fields that have no underscore.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:24-28: `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, then `compressorName`. Spec 12.1.3.2: `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, `string[32] compressorname`. The package keeps `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate` (AudioSampleEntryBox.ts:20-24), `graphicsmode`, `opcolor` (VideoMediaHeaderBox.ts:10-11) and `maxPDUsize`, `maxbitrate` (HintMediaHeaderBox.ts:10-13) as the spec writes them. `compressorName` is the one exception.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: State one rule in the README: a spec name with underscores becomes camel case, a spec name with no underscore stays as written. Under that rule rename `compressorName` to `compressorname`. If the project prefers readable names, rename all of them in one pass instead (`channelCount`, `sampleRate`, `graphicsMode`, `opColor`, `horizResolution`, `vertResolution`, `maxPduSize`). Do not keep both rules.

alsoReportedAs.title: The field names of the sample entries follow two casing rules, and four names differ from shaka-player and from the rule of the other boxes.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate`, `horizresolution`, `vertresolution` are single lowercase words, as in the spec and in codem-isoboxer. In the same types, `compressorName` has a capital letter, although the spec name `compressorname` is also one word. Every other field of the package is camelCase with word breaks (`dataReferenceIndex`, `frameCount`, `sampleCount`, `sampleSize` in stsz). shaka-player returns `channelCount` and `sampleRate` (lib/util/mp4_box_parsers.js:313 to 331). An adopter sees `sampleSize` on stsz and `samplesize` on mp4a.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: `channelCount`, `sampleSize`, `sampleRate`, `horizResolution`, `vertResolution`, and keep `compressorName`. State the rule once in the docs: spec name, camelCase at each word.

fact.reason:
I read all eight type files, the readers and writers that use them, and the 2015 spec text. The core claim holds.

Lowercase one-word names copied from the spec:
- libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/AudioSampleEntryBox.ts:20,21,24 `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate` (spec 14496-12 lines 9590 to 9594, same spelling).
- libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:24,25 `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, and line 28 `compressorName: number[]`. Spec line 9340 has `string[32] compressorname;`, so the type breaks its own rule. Line 27 `frameCount` comes from `frame_count` (spec line 9339), which fits the underscore rule.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/VideoMediaHeaderBox.ts:10,11 `graphicsmode`, `opcolor` (spec lines 9296, 9297).
- libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/HintMediaHeaderBox.ts:10 to 13 `maxPDUsize`, `avgPDUsize`, `maxbitrate`, `avgbitrate` (spec lines 10094 to 10097).

Contrast names hold: `sampleSize` and `sampleCount` at SampleSizeBox.ts:10,11, `sampleSize` at TrackRunSample.ts:8, `sampleCount` at TrackRunBox.ts:14. The spec semantics clause writes `ChannelCount`, `SampleSize`, `SampleRate` (lines 9630 to 9632).

Acronym claim holds. A search of src/boxes for a field name with two or more capital letters in a row returns only `maxPDUsize` and `avgPDUsize`. `trackId`, `schemeUri`, `defaultKid` (TrackEncryptionBox.ts:22), `defaultIvSize` (:19), and `sapType` (SegmentIndexReference.ts:13) are lower camel.

`rangesCount` holds: Subsegment.ts:9, against `unsigned int(32) range_count;` at spec line 6810. `ntpTimestampSec` and `ntpTimestampFrac` (ProducerReferenceTimeBox.ts:12,13) against `mediaRateFraction` (EditListEntry.ts:12) holds. The spec has one field `unsigned int(64) ntp_timestamp` (line 6865), so both prft names are package inventions.

Details that are wrong or missing:
1. The title says six boxes. The lowercase names are in four type definitions: AudioSampleEntryBox, VisualSampleEntryBox, VideoMediaHeaderBox, HintMediaHeaderBox. A list of every all-lowercase field name in src/boxes shows no fifth type, apart from `timescale`, which is one word in the spec.
2. The breaking reason omits `Subsegment.rangesCount` (ssix), which the proposal also renames.
3. `HintMediaHeaderBox` has no reader and no writer in src. The hmhd renames change a type only.

The names are used in readers and writers: readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:28 to 32, writeAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:54 to 58, readVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:35 to 39, writeVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:68 to 72, readVmhd.ts:19,20, writeVmhd.ts:26,27, readSsix.ts:18 to 23, writeSsix.ts:23,34. No package outside iso-bmff uses the names.
fact.correction: The lowercase spec names are in four type definitions, not six: AudioSampleEntryBox, VisualSampleEntryBox, VideoMediaHeaderBox, and HintMediaHeaderBox. The breaking change also covers `Subsegment.rangesCount` (ssix), so the reason must read: public field names of the sample entries, vmhd, hmhd, and ssix change. `HintMediaHeaderBox` has no reader or writer, so its four renames touch the type only. The proposal leaves two points open: `ntpTimestampSec` and `ntpTimestampFrac` are not spec names (the spec has one 64-bit `ntp_timestamp`), and the rule keeps `timescale` as one word. The changelog must warn JavaScript adopters without type checks: a writer does not throw for a missing field, so a box that still has `channelcount` or `graphicsmode` may write a wrong value with no error.
fact.priorDecision: None found. The names come from the first import (commit 8ac3ef9b9, "feat: CML Version 1 (#265)") and the first writers commit (d615e5bf0). No RFC, README, or guide states a field name rule. CHANGELOG.md:72 mentions `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, and `samplerate` only as a list of fixed-point fields.

value.reason:
Facts confirmed in src. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/AudioSampleEntryBox.ts:20-24 has `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate`. VisualSampleEntryBox.ts:24-28 has `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, then `frameCount`, `compressorName`. VideoMediaHeaderBox.ts:10-11 has `graphicsmode`, `opcolor`. HintMediaHeaderBox.ts:10-13 has `maxPDUsize`, `avgPDUsize`, `maxbitrate`, `avgbitrate`. Subsegment.ts:9 has `rangesCount`. SampleSizeBox.ts:10 has `sampleSize`. I listed every unique field name in src/boxes: these eleven names are the only joined lowercase names, and `maxPDUsize`/`avgPDUsize` are the only names with an upper-case acronym (against `trackId`, `defaultKid`, `defaultIvSize`, `schemeUri`). The count of affected types is four (audio sample entry, visual sample entry, vmhd, hmhd) plus `Subsegment`, not six.

Spec (14496-12-2015.txt): lines 9590-9594 `channelcount`, `samplesize`, `samplerate`; 9336-9340 `horizresolution`, `vertresolution`, `string[32] compressorname`; 9296-9297 `graphicsmode`, `opcolor`; 10094-10097 `maxPDUsize`, `avgPDUsize`, `maxbitrate`, `avgbitrate`; 6810 `range_count`. The spec is not consistent with itself: the semantics clause 12.2.3.3 (lines 9630-9632) writes `ChannelCount`, `SampleSize`, `SampleRate`, and the BitRateBox (lines 2455-2456) writes `maxBitrate`, `avgBitrate` for the same quantity that hmhd writes as `maxbitrate`. So a literal-spelling rule copies the inconsistency of the spec into the API. The proposed names stay 1:1 traceable to the spec names, so spec accuracy is not reduced.

Prior decision search: `git log -S` for channelcount, horizresolution, compressorName, graphicsmode, maxPDUsize, rangesCount shows only the initial port (8ac3ef9b9 CML Version 1 #265, d615e5bf0 writers, alpha.2/alpha.3) and the fixed-point fix a13db9ace (#620), which did not touch names. `git log --grep` for camel/rename found no naming decision. CHANGELOG.md has no entry about field casing (line 72 only lists the names for the readTemplate fix). No RFC in rfc/ states a field naming rule (grep of rfc/*.md for camel, field name, channelcount: no hit). gh issue search returned no result. The lowercase names are inherited from the codem-isoboxer port, and parity with codem-isoboxer is not a reason. No settled decision is affected.

Value: zero cost for performance, bundle size, and written bytes. The gain is developer experience: `samplesize` on mp4a against `sampleSize` on stsz and trun is a real trap, and shaka-player already uses `channelCount`/`sampleRate` (~/dev/shaka-player/lib/util/mp4_box_parsers.js:317-325). In-repo impact is small: 4 readers, 4 writers, 6 test files, the api report, and the skills reference. `HintMediaHeaderBox` has no reader or writer (only a type in IsoBoxMap.ts:122 and MediaInformationBox.ts:17), so its rename is type-only. The rename must go in the major version because it breaks every adopter that reads or builds a sample entry.
value.correction: Keep the proposed rule and renames: `channelCount`, `sampleSize`, `sampleRate`, `horizResolution`, `vertResolution`, `graphicsMode`, `opColor`, `maxPduSize`, `avgPduSize`, `maxBitrate`, `avgBitrate`, and keep `compressorName`. Reject the alternative from F46, F181, and F351 (rename `compressorName` to `compressorname`): it makes one more name unreadable and keeps the spec's own inconsistency. Three adjustments. (1) The affected types are four plus `Subsegment`, not six. (2) `rangesCount` to `rangeCount` only matters if the count field survives the major version. If another finding removes count fields that duplicate an array length, drop this rename and remove the field instead. (3) Write the rule once in the README, with the exceptions stated: a field name is the spec name in lower camel case, split at each English word, acronyms as words (`Id`, `Kid`, `Iv`, `Uri`, `Pdu`), and `timescale` stays one word. `ntpTimestampSec` and `ntpTimestampFrac` are not a casing problem: the spec has one 64-bit `ntp_timestamp`, so treat that split as a separate finding under the int64 rules. Put all renames in one changelog table with old and new names as the migration guide.

confirmed.title: The sample entry readers take any box type and the sample entry writers take only the built-in types, and the reader parameters are in the reverse order of `IsoBoxReader`.
confirmed.breakingReason: The signature of `readAudioSampleEntryBox` and `readVisualSampleEntryBox` changes, the writer type parameter widens, and the two `create*Reader` functions may go.
confirmed.evidence: Reader: `readAudioSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>(type: T, view: IsoBoxReadView<IsoInt64>)`. The doc of `createAudioSampleEntryReader` shows `'ac-3': createAudioSampleEntryReader('ac-3')`. Writer: `writeAudioSampleEntryBox<T extends AudioSampleEntryType = AudioSampleEntryType>(box: AudioSampleEntryBox<T>, ...)` with `AudioSampleEntryType = 'mp4a' | 'enca'`. A box that the package reads as `AudioSampleEntryBox<'ac-3'>` is a compile error for the only writer that can write it. The visual pair has the same difference. Parameter order: the reader contract is `(view: IsoBoxReadView<V>, type: T) => B`, and the view calls `parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type)`. The two sample entry functions take `(type, view)`. That order is the only reason for the two factories and for the nine wrappers (`readMp4a`, `readEnca`, `readAvc1` to `readAvc4`, `readHev1`, `readHvc1`, `readEncv`). The RFC removes the `type` argument from `IsoBoxReader` (`(cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<V>) => B`), so this family needs a decision before the rewrite.
confirmed.proposal: Widen both writers to `T extends IsoBoxType`. In the cursor API, keep a way for a reader to know the type of the box it reads (a `type` field on the read cursor, or the second argument of today), and give the two generic readers the reader signature. Then `readers: { 'ac-3': readAudioSampleEntry }` works with no factory, and the two `create*Reader` functions can go.

alsoReportedAs.title: `readAudioSampleEntryBox` and `readVisualSampleEntryBox` take `(type, view)`, the reverse of `IsoBoxReader`, so they cannot go into a `readers` map and two factories exist only to adapt them.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: IsoBoxReader.ts:16 `(view: IsoBoxReadView<V>, type: T) => B`, and IsoBoxReadView.ts:466 calls `parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type)`. readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:17-19 `readAudioSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>(type: T, view: IsoBoxReadView<IsoInt64>)`. tsc on a scratch file: `readers: { 'ac-3': readAudioSampleEntryBox }` fails with `Types of parameters 'type' and 'view' are incompatible`. createAudioSampleEntryReader.ts:32 is only `return (view) => readAudioSampleEntryBox<T>(type, view)`. The names also differ: the factory is `createAudioSampleEntryReader` and the reader is `readAudioSampleEntryBox`. The cursor RFC drops the `type` argument (line 157 `(cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<V>) => B`), which keeps the factories necessary.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Give the generic readers the reader signature: `readAudioSampleEntry(cursor, type)` and `readVisualSampleEntry(cursor, type)`. Keep `type` as the second argument of `IsoBoxReader` in the cursor RFC. An adopter then writes `readers: { 'ac-3': readAudioSampleEntry, av01: readVisualSampleEntry }` with no closure. Remove `createAudioSampleEntryReader` and `createVisualSampleEntryReader`. The named readers `readAvc1` to `readAvc4`, `readMp4a`, and `readEnca` stay as they are.

alsoReportedAs.title: The generic sample entry writers accept only the closed unions `AudioSampleEntryType` and `VisualSampleEntryType`, but the readers and the box types accept every box type.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: writeAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:21 `writeAudioSampleEntryBox<T extends AudioSampleEntryType = AudioSampleEntryType>`. writeVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:21 `<T extends VisualSampleEntryType = VisualSampleEntryType>`. readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:17 `<T extends IsoBoxType>` and AudioSampleEntryBox.ts:17 `AudioSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType = AudioSampleEntryType>`. tsc on a scratch file: `writeVisualSampleEntryBox(av01, config)` with `av01: VisualSampleEntryBox<'av01'>` fails with `Type '"av01"' is not assignable to type 'VisualSampleEntryType'`. The same error occurs for `AudioSampleEntryBox<'ac-3'>`. So a box that `createVisualSampleEntryReader('av01')` returns has no typed writer. The writer body uses only `box.type`, so the limit has no runtime reason.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Constrain both writers with `T extends IsoBoxType`, as the readers do. Document `writers: { av01: writeVisualSampleEntryBox, 'ac-3': writeAudioSampleEntryBox }` next to the reader example.

alsoReportedAs.title: readVisualSampleEntryBox accepts every box type, but writeVisualSampleEntryBox accepts only the seven built-in types
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Reader: `readVisualSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>(type: T, view)`. Factory doc: `'vp09': createVisualSampleEntryReader('vp09')`. Writer: `writeVisualSampleEntryBox<T extends VisualSampleEntryType = VisualSampleEntryType>(box: VisualSampleEntryBox<T>, config)`, where `VisualSampleEntryType = 'avc1' | 'avc2' | 'avc3' | 'avc4' | 'hev1' | 'hvc1' | 'encv'`. A `VisualSampleEntryBox<'vp09'>` from the documented factory therefore fails the constraint of the writer (read from the signatures, not compiled). The writer body uses only `box.type`, so the constraint has no purpose. The package also has a reader factory and no matching writer factory, and the reader takes `(type, view)` while the readers map calls `(view, type)`.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Widen the writer to `T extends IsoBoxType`. Then one generic pair covers custom sample entry types, and `createVisualSampleEntryReader` can go if the reader takes the type from the map call. Decide the argument order once for the cursor API.

alsoReportedAs.title: readVisualSampleEntryBox takes `(type, view)`, the reverse of the `IsoBoxReader` contract `(view, type)`, so the package needs a factory and one wrapper for each box type.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Contract: `(view: IsoBoxReadView<V>, type: T) => B`. Call site: `parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type)`. Reader: `readVisualSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>(type: T, view: IsoBoxReadView<IsoInt64>)`. The factory only swaps the arguments: `return (view) => readVisualSampleEntryBox<T>(type, view)`. `readHev1` and `readHvc1` do the same with a literal. The writer needs no factory because it takes the type from `box.type`. The RFC type `IsoBoxReader<B, V> = (cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<V>) => B` drops the `type` argument, so the factory would stay necessary in version 2.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Change the signature to `readVisualSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>(view, type: T)`, so the function is a valid map entry: `readers: { av01: readVisualSampleEntryBox }`. Keep the `type` argument in the reader type of the RFC, or put `type` on the read cursor. Then remove `createVisualSampleEntryReader`. `readHev1` and `readHvc1` can stay as typed names. The same change applies to `readAudioSampleEntryBox` and `createAudioSampleEntryReader` (src/readers/readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:17).

alsoReportedAs.title: The visual sample entry reader accepts every box type, but the writer accepts only the seven types of `VisualSampleEntryType`.
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Reader: `readVisualSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>`. Factory: `createVisualSampleEntryReader<T extends IsoBoxType>`. Writer: `writeVisualSampleEntryBox<T extends VisualSampleEntryType = VisualSampleEntryType>(box: VisualSampleEntryBox<T>, ...)`. A box from `createVisualSampleEntryReader('av01')` has the type `VisualSampleEntryBox<'av01'>`, and a direct call of the writer with that box does not satisfy the constraint. The test entry `dvh1: writeVisualSampleEntryBox` compiles only because `IsoBoxWriterMap` is `Record<string, IsoBoxWriter<any>>`. I did not run the compiler.
alsoReportedAs.proposal: Declare the writer as `writeVisualSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>(box: VisualSampleEntryBox<T>, ...)`. Apply the same change to `writeAudioSampleEntryBox` (src/writers/writeAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:21).

alsoReportedAs.title: The generic sample entry writers reject box types that the generic readers accept
alsoReportedAs.evidence: Reader: `readAudioSampleEntryBox<T extends IsoBoxType>`, and the TSDoc example is `createAudioSampleEntryReader('ac-3')`. Writer: `writeAudioSampleEntryBox<T extends AudioSampleEntryType = AudioSampleEntryType>`, where `AudioSampleEntryType = 'mp4a' | 'enca'`. No config flag and no `offset` or `size` field on parsed boxes. Amend the RFC before acceptance:

1. Contract: state the coordinates of the read cursor. `pos` and `end` are byte offsets in `cursor.view`. `createIsoBoxReadCursor` builds the view over the input, so the offsets are relative to the input (version 1 `view.byteOffset` is relative to the ArrayBuffer). For the cursor that a reader receives and for the cursor from `seekIsoBox`, `end` is the first byte after the box. That value is the sidx anchor point.

2. Add `start` to `IsoBoxReadCursor`: the first byte of the box header. `pos - 8` is not reliable, because a header has 8, 16, 24, or 32 bytes (largesize, uuid). The cost is one assignment for each box. `start` gives the moof base for trun and the complete pssh bytes: `new Uint8Array(view.buffer, view.byteOffset + start, end - start)`. If the maintainers reject `start`, list the question under Unresolved questions.

3. Guide: show that an adopter keeps a position by wrapping a reader, with the capture before the read: `sidx: c => { const end = c.end; return { ...readSidx(c), end } }`. Show the same for `moof` with `start`, and the pssh bytes case. Only the adopter who needs a position pays for it, and the built-in readers and box types do not change.

4. Drawbacks line 238: name this replacement for `view.byteOffset` and `size`, and note that a raw box already has `bytes.byteOffset` and `bytes.byteLength`.

The change is additive to the RFC design, so it breaks no adopter beyond the removal that the RFC already declares. It can ship after 2.0.0 as well, but the migration text of 2.0.0 needs it.

- Spec: 14496-12:2015 clause 8.8.3.1 defines the 32-bit sample flags layout (spec text lines 3706-3717): reserved 4 bits, is_leading, sample_depends_on, sample_is_depended_on, sample_has_redundancy, sample_padding_value (3 bits), sample_is_non_sync_sample, sample_degradation_priority (16 bits). A flags helper has a spec basis.

Prior decision search: no issue, PR, RFC or changelog entry accepts or rejects sample resolution helpers. `git log -S'left to resolve for the user'` returns only 8ac3ef9b9 (CML Version 1, PR 265), the initial port. `gh issue list` for "sample flags", "sdtp", "trex defaults", "fragment duration" returns nothing relevant. rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md lists no sample helper under Future possibilities (lines 278-281). So the current state is the original scope, not a recorded choice.

Why the proposal needs a change:
1. The change is additive and breaks nothing, so the major version gives it no benefit. The cursor RFC already touches 87 readers and 85 writers (rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:243). AGENTS.md requires an RFC for a public API change, and says not to add an export without a clear use case.
2. `iterateIsoSamples(traf, trex?, moofOffset)` does not cover the spec rules. Clause 8.8.7.1 (spec lines 3846-3871): the base offset is tfhd base_data_offset if flag 0x000001 is set, else the moof start if default-base-is-moof (0x020000) is set, else the moof start for the first traf and the end of the data of the preceding traf for later ones. A trun without data_offset continues after the previous run. first_sample_flags replaces the flags of the first sample only (line 3922). dash.js ignores the trex fallback and these offset rules, so it is not a model. The iterator also needs a rule for a missing tfdt and for bigint `baseMediaDecodeTime` under the int64 option.
3. A generator that yields one object per sample allocates per sample. Performance is priority 1. hls.js does this work on raw bytes for that reason. The design needs a measurement.
4. The names in the proposal come from hls.js and omit sample_padding_value and sample_degradation_priority. The spec comes first.

One item does touch the major version: the stored fields `sampleFlags`, `firstSampleFlags` and `defaultSampleFlags` must stay numbers. A change to an object type would break adopters, would allocate per sample, and is not what the finding proposes.
