confirmed.title: Scope growth: the package has no function that converts a sidx box to segment references with times and byte ranges.
confirmed.evidence: readSidx returns the fields of the box. The three players each convert them to a list of `{ startTime, duration, startByte, endByte }`: hls.js parseSegmentIndex (src/utils/mp4-tools.ts:498 to 575), shaka-player Mp4SegmentIndexParser (lib/dash/mp4_segment_index_parser.js:95 to 150), dash.js SegmentBaseLoader (src/dash/SegmentBaseLoader.js:296 to 314). Each needs the end position of the sidx box as the anchor, which the package does not return after the RFC (see the gap on box position). Each also treats `referenceType === 1` as a special case.
confirmed.proposal: Possible addition: `getIsoSegmentReferences(sidx, anchorOffset)`, which returns the list and leaves hierarchical references to the caller. The function is about 20 lines and removes one copy of the logic from each player.

fact.reason:
Core claim holds. The package has no sidx-to-segment-list function. `readSidx` (libs/iso-bmff/src/readers/readSidx.ts:18-57) returns only the box fields: `referenceId`, `timescale`, `earliestPresentationTime`, `firstOffset`, `reserved`, `references`. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/SegmentIndexBox.ts:11 is `type: 'sidx'`. README.md:11 lists `readSidx` for "the segment index". A grep of config/cml-iso-bmff.api.md for `getSegment|SegmentReference|toSegments` returns nothing, and no other package under libs/ converts a sidx box (cmaf-ham only has an unrelated `segmentIndex` field). The RFC statement also holds: rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:199 says a parsed box has only `type` and its fields, so `view` and `size` (the current way to get the box end) disappear.

Player evidence, read in the local checkouts (hls.js cd338d2fa, shaka-player 2ed47645f, dash.js 2dc34a251):
- hls.js src/utils/mp4-tools.ts: `parseSegmentIndex` is lines 498 to 574 (finding says 575). Anchor is `let startByte = sidx.length + firstOffset`, relative to the payload, not an absolute position. `referenceType === 1` returns null with a warning.
- shaka-player lib/dash/mp4_segment_index_parser.js: `parseSIDX_` is lines 84 to 176 (finding cites 95 to 150, a subset). Anchor is `anchorOffset + box.size + firstOffset`. `referenceType == 1` throws MP4_SIDX_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED at line 146.
- dash.js src/dash/SegmentBaseLoader.js: `getSegmentsForSidx` is lines 293 to 322 (finding cites 296 to 314). Anchor is `info.range.start + sidx.offset + sidx.first_offset + sidx.size`. The `reference_type === 1` case is at line 226, outside the cited range, and starts a recursive load.

Wrong details:
1. hls.js does not produce `{ startTime, duration, startByte, endByte }`. It pushes `{ referenceSize, subsegmentDuration, info: { duration, start, end } }` with no start time. Its only call site (mp4-tools.ts:1600-1607) reads `ref.info.duration` and `earliestPresentationTime` only. The byte range is unused there.
2. The three outputs differ in units and shape: shaka uses seconds plus `timestampOffset` and builds `SegmentReference` objects, dash.js keeps unscaled `startTime`, `duration`, `timescale` and a `mediaRange` string, hls.js uses seconds for duration. "Removes one copy of the logic from each player" is therefore optimistic. Each player would still map the result, and hls.js would gain nothing for its byte range.
3. The "about 20 lines" estimate ignores the `int64` option. `earliestPresentationTime` and `firstOffset` have type `V extends IsoInt64` (SegmentIndexBox.ts:14-15), so the function must accept number and bigint values and define the result type.

No prior decision against the addition was found. Issue search for "sidx" returns only 670 (version 2 syntax) and unrelated items.
fact.correction: The package has no function that converts a parsed `sidx` box to a segment list. shaka-player (`parseSIDX_`, lib/dash/mp4_segment_index_parser.js:84 to 176) and dash.js (`getSegmentsForSidx`, src/dash/SegmentBaseLoader.js:293 to 322) each build start time, duration, and byte range from the box end plus `first_offset`. hls.js (`parseSegmentIndex`, src/utils/mp4-tools.ts:498 to 574) builds duration and a payload-relative byte range with no start time, and its only caller uses the durations. All three special-case `referenceType === 1` (hls.js returns null, shaka-player throws, dash.js loads recursively at line 226). A helper is an additive, tree-shakeable export that needs no major version. It must return unscaled values plus `timescale` (the players disagree on units), take the anchor offset from the caller, and handle the `IsoInt64` type of `earliestPresentationTime` and `firstOffset`. It is a new feature, not a fix of an inconsistency, so it belongs in a separate issue and not in the 2.0.0 audit list. If the cursor RFC removes `view` and `size`, the box position gap must be solved first, because the helper is useless without an anchor.

The facts hold. `readSidx` returns only the fields of the box (libs/iso-bmff/src/readers/readSidx.ts:19 to 56). The package exports no function that derives values from a parsed box: index.ts lines 24 to 40 export only read, write, find, filter, traverse, and guard functions. I read the three player copies. hls.js: `let startByte = sidx.length + firstOffset` and `if (referenceType === 1) { logger.warn(...); return null }` (~/dev/hls.js/src/utils/mp4-tools.ts:498 to 575). shaka-player: `let startByte = anchorOffset + box.size + firstOffset`, with a throw for `referenceType == 1` and an `indexIsExternal` case (~/dev/shaka-player/lib/dash/mp4_segment_index_parser.js:128 to 150). dash.js: `let start = info.range.start + sidx.offset + sidx.first_offset + sidx.size` (~/dev/dash.js/src/dash/SegmentBaseLoader.js:296 to 314). The spec agrees with a caller-supplied anchor: "the anchor point for a Segment Index box is the first byte after that box. If there are two files, the anchor point in the media file is the beginning of the top-level segment" (14496-12-2015.txt:6564 to 6566).

No prior decision exists. `git log -S'SegmentReference'` and `--grep='segment reference'` return nothing. `--grep=sidx` returns only PR 674 and PR 645. The gh search returns issues 670, 678, 611, none about a conversion function. No RFC names one.

The finding is wrong on three points. (1) It is not a major-version item: the function is additive and tree-shakeable, so the 2.0.0 release gives no reason to add it now, and the user asked for fixes, not new features. (2) It cannot go in as an audit fix: rfc/README.md:16 says "A small addition to a package's public API surface still needs an RFC ... 'Small' is not an exception", and AGENTS.md:55 says "do not add a public export unless it serves a clear use case". (3) The proposed signature is incomplete, see the correction. The three players also disagree on output: hls.js and shaka-player divide by the timescale, dash.js keeps ticks plus the timescale, and each has a different reaction to `referenceType === 1` (return null, throw, ignore). One function does not replace the three copies without adopter input.
value.correction: Keep the item out of the 2.0.0 audit list. File it as a feature issue, and write a short RFC if a player maintainer asks for it. The RFC must settle four points that the proposal skips. (1) The int64 option: `SegmentIndexBox<V>` has `earliestPresentationTime: V` and `firstOffset: V` (libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/SegmentIndexBox.ts:14 to 15), so the function must be generic over `V extends IsoInt64` and must not mix number and bigint. (2) Time units: return `startTime` and `duration` in ticks of `sidx.timescale`, as dash.js does. A division inside the function loses the exact value that the int64 option exists to keep. (3) Hierarchical references: an entry with `referenceType` 1 still uses bytes and time, so each returned item must include `referenceType`. The function must not drop the entry, throw, or log. (4) The anchor: keep it a caller argument, documented with the two spec cases (first byte after the sidx box, or the start of the media segment for an index in a separate file). The dependency to solve in the 2.0.0 work is the other finding: after the cursor RFC a parsed box has no position or size, so an adopter cannot compute the anchor for a sidx found through `readIsoBoxes`. That gap is the part with a claim on the major version, not this function.

confirmed.title: Scope growth: the package has no function that lists the pssh boxes of a buffer with their complete bytes, and none that builds a pssh box from a system ID, key IDs and data.
confirmed.evidence: EME takes complete pssh boxes as init data, and players select a box by its system ID. hls.js has parseMultiPssh and mp4pssh(systemId, keyIds, data) (src/utils/mp4-tools.ts:2183 and 2114). shaka-player has the Pssh class with `data` (complete boxes) and `systemIds`, plus Pssh.createPssh(data, systemId, keyIds, version) (lib/util/pssh.js:24 and 93). dash.js has parsePSSHList in src/streaming/protection/CommonEncryption.js, which returns the box bytes for each system ID. With the package, an adopter gets the fields of the box as `number[]` and gets the box bytes only through `box.view`, which the RFC removes. To build a box, the adopter must fill `kidCount`, a flat `kid` array and `dataSize` by hand.
confirmed.proposal: After the type fix for pssh, writePssh already serves as the builder: `{ type: 'pssh', version, flags, systemId, kids, data }`. Add one small function that returns each pssh box of a buffer as `{ systemId, bytes }` through seekIsoBox, or document the recipe with raw boxes.

confirmed.title: A number that does not fit its field is written with no error and with three different results, and a bigint in the same field throws a RangeError.
confirmed.breakingReason: A fix adds a thrown RangeError for a number, or changes the written bytes.
confirmed.evidence: Run with defaultWriterConfig. `{type:'tfdt',version:0,baseMediaDecodeTime:2**32+5}` writes `00000010746664740000000000000005`, and a read returns 5. The same box with `2n**32n+5n` throws `RangeError: writeWideUint: value must be in the range 0 to 2^32 - 1`. Result 1, modulo: `dataView.setUint32(cursor, value)` (mfhd sequenceNumber 2**32 reads back 0, elst v0 mediaTime 2**31 reads back -2147483648). Result 2, all bits set: `if (s1 > 0xffffffff) { s1 = s2 = 0xffffffff }` (tfdt v1 with 2**65 or with -1 writes ffffffffffffffff). Result 3, mask: `ref.referencedSize & 0x7fffffff` (sidx referencedSize 2**31 reads back 0, ssix rangeSize 2**24 reads back 0). writeInt with 8 bytes has no limit: elst v1 mediaTime 2**63 reads back -9223372036854776000. The guide states the rule (`A writer does not check the range of a number`), so the behavior is documented. The error message of the bigint case names the internal method and not the box or the field.
confirmed.proposal: State one overflow rule in the contract of rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md. Minimum: `writeWideUint` and `writeWideInt` throw the same RangeError for a `number` as for a `bigint`, because the version of the box decides the width of these fields. The message names the box type, the field, the range and the received value. For the fixed-size functions, document the modulo result of DataView in the TSDoc of each function.

The current state is intentional, and three sources show it:
1. PR 669 (commit 67bd8d7af, merged 2026-11-16, fixes issue 653). The commit body states "The number path still has no range check." The PR description states "The maintainer chose this option from three measured options" and "A negative value or NaN writes as before." It also states that the signed path of writeInt stays unchanged on purpose. The PR added the all-bits-set branch and the guide sentence at libs/iso-bmff/docs/writing-boxes.md:173.
2. rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:260 (accepted RFC 613) defines the rule: "A `number` goes to `writeUint(value, size)` ... Throws `RangeError` when a `bigint` does not fit the size." The rules of that RFC are settled.
3. rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:202 states "A writer follows the same rules as in version 1."

The minimum proposal (the same RangeError for a `number` as for a `bigint`) is wrong for three reasons:

Result 3 (the mask) is not an overflow rule. The mask protects the adjacent bit field (`referenceType`) in a packed word, so it is correct code.

The real part of the finding is documentation. The rule exists only in the guide. The TSDoc of writeUint and writeInt (IsoBoxWriteView.ts:57-65 and 130-135) does not state the modulo result, and the Contract section of the cursor RFC does not state the rule for the new field functions. confirmed.title: A readers map with the exported type IsoBoxReaderMap makes every box of the readIsoBoxes result lose `type`, so drm builds its map through a second variable.
confirmed.breakingReason: The fix changes the public types `IsoBoxReader`, `IsoBoxReaderMap` or `IsoBoxReaderReturn`. Code that fails to compile today then compiles. A custom reader typed to return a value with no `type` field can stop compiling.
confirmed.evidence: `IsoBoxReaderMap` is `Record<IsoBoxType, IsoBoxReader<unknown, IsoBoxType, V>>` (IsoBoxReaderMap.ts:10-13). `IsoBoxReaderReturn` maps each reader to `ParsedBox<B, V>` with the inferred `B` (IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts:38-50). For `B = unknown`, `ParsedBox` is only `{ view; size; largesize?; usertype? }` (ParsedBox.ts:11-18). A type check of `const readers: IsoBoxReaderMap = { stsd: readStsd }` and `readIsoBoxes(bytes, { readers })[0].type` against the source gave: "TS2339: Property 'type' does not exist on type 'IsoBoxReaderReturn<IsoBoxReaderMap, number>'". drm avoids the error with an alias: `const map = { stsd: readStsd }`, `const dynamic: IsoBoxReaderMap = map`, `audioTypes.forEach(type => (dynamic[type] = createAudioSampleEntryReader(type)))`, `return map` (ensureEncryptedInit.ts:38-44). The static type of the map then has 1 reader and the run-time map has 17. The writers map uses the same alias (lines 48-59). The RFC keeps the cause: `type IsoBoxReader<B = unknown, V ...>` (RFC line 157).
confirmed.proposal: Constrain the reader result in 2.0: `type IsoBoxReader<B extends { type: IsoBoxType } = { type: IsoBoxType }, V extends IsoInt64 = number>`. In `IsoBoxReaderReturn`, return the plain union (`IsoBox<V>` or a raw box) when `string extends keyof T`. Add a type test with a map of the type `IsoBoxReaderMap`. drm can then build the map with a plain loop and delete the alias.

2. "drm avoids the error with an alias" is an inference, and it is only half of the reason. The alias arrived in PR 585 (facd7ba42) as the replacement for `(readers as any)[type] = ...`. Without the alias, a direct assignment into the inferred map fails with TS7053 (no index signature). The alias avoids that error and also keeps `stsd: readStsd` in the static type for the narrowing at lines 122-130. A fully typed `IsoBoxReaderMap` would hit TS2339 at line 122, so the finding's link is plausible, but no commit states it.

The finding misses that the static type is wrong against the run-time value. libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:461-466 reads the header into `box` (with `type`) and then does `Object.assign(box, parser(view, type))`. Every result box has `type` at run time, whatever the reader returns. So the missing `type` is a typing defect, not a reader contract defect.

Only an explicitly annotated `IsoBoxReaderMap` passed as `{ readers }` hits the error. No README or guide shows that pattern.

confirmed.title: The RFC removes the `type` argument of a reader without a statement, and that argument is the only way to delete the two sample entry factories that drm calls 16 times.
confirmed.breakingReason: The proposal removes `createAudioSampleEntryReader` and `createVisualSampleEntryReader` and changes the signature of the two generic sample entry readers.
confirmed.evidence: Version 1: `(view: IsoBoxReadView<V>, type: T) => B` (IsoBoxReader.ts:16), called as `parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type)` (IsoBoxReadView.ts:466). RFC line 157: `(cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<V>) => B`. The RFC sections Drawbacks and Contract do not name the removal. The RFC also does not say if the tree reader or the reader sets `type` on the result. No built-in reader uses the second argument. The two readers that need the type take it first: `readAudioSampleEntryBox<T>(type: T, view)` (readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:17-20). So the package needs a factory, `return (view) => readAudioSampleEntryBox<T>(type, view)` (createAudioSampleEntryReader.ts:32), and 9 one-line wrappers such as `return readAudioSampleEntryBox('mp4a', view)` (readMp4a.ts:15). drm calls the factories for 6 audio and 10 video types (ensureEncryptedInit.ts:22-35, 42-43), `mp4a` included.
confirmed.proposal: Decide the rule in the RFC. Recommended: the read cursor has a `type` field that the tree reader and `seekIsoBox` set from the box header. Then export two plain readers for any type, `readAudioSampleEntry(cursor)` and `readVisualSampleEntry(cursor)`, which return `type: cursor.type`. Remove both factories. The 9 named wrappers become aliases or are removed. drm then writes `dynamic[type] = readAudioSampleEntry`.

fact.reason:
Checked at HEAD 8ce63c212. The core facts hold.

- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReader.ts:12-16: `IsoBoxReader<B, T extends IsoBoxType, V> = (view: IsoBoxReadView<V>, type: T) => B`.
- libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxReadView.ts:466: `Object.assign(box, parser(view as IsoBoxReadView, type))`. This line is the only reader call in src.
- rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:157: `type IsoBoxReader<B = unknown, V extends IsoInt64 = number> = (cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<V>) => B`. The `type` argument and the `T` type parameter are gone. The cursor type (lines 142-148) has no `type` field.
- RFC Contract (lines 193-203) and Drawbacks (lines 234-242) do not name the removal. Drawbacks only says "Every custom reader and custom writer changes" with the example `view.readUint(4)` becomes `readUint32(cursor)`.
- No built-in reader takes a second argument. In src/readers, only `readAudioSampleEntryBox(type, view)` (readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:17-20) and `readVisualSampleEntryBox(type, view)` (readVisualSampleEntryBox.ts:20-23) have two parameters, and both take `type` first.
- Factories: createAudioSampleEntryReader.ts:32 and createVisualSampleEntryReader.ts:32 return `(view) => read...SampleEntryBox<T>(type, view)`.
- Nine one-line wrappers exist: readMp4a, readEnca, readAvc1, readAvc2, readAvc3, readAvc4, readEncv, readHev1, readHvc1.
- libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:22 lists 6 audio types with `mp4a`, lines 24-35 list 10 video types, lines 42-43 call the two factories for each type. drm is the only caller in libs outside the iso-bmff tests.

Three details are wrong or too strong.
1. The title says the argument is "the only way" to delete the factories. That statement is false. The finding's own proposal uses a `type` field on the cursor, not the argument. A third way also exists: the tree reader sets `type` on the result, as version 1 does with `Object.assign(box, ...)`, and a generic reader returns no `type`. Version 1 has the argument today and still has the factories, because the two generic readers take `type` first.
2. The quote `return readAudioSampleEntryBox('mp4a', view)` is at readMp4a.ts:16, not line 15.
3. "The RFC does not say who sets `type`" holds only for an explicit rule. The RFC example at lines 104-112 shows the reader returning `type: 'mfhd'`, and line 87 shows the tree reader creating `{ type, bytes }` for a raw box. The RFC implies the version 1 pattern and does not state it.
fact.correction: Title: "The RFC removes the `type` argument and the `T` type parameter of `IsoBoxReader` without a statement. The RFC gives a generic reader no other source for the box type, so the two sample entry factories that drm calls 16 times must stay." The argument is not the only way to remove the factories. Three options exist: keep the second argument and reverse the parameter order of the two generic readers, add a `type` field to the read cursor, or let the tree reader set `type` and have the generic readers omit it. The RFC must choose one and state it in Contract. The RFC example already shows that a reader returns `type` itself, so the open point is only the generic reader. The readMp4a quote is at line 16. Note for the proposal: removal of the nine named wrappers conflicts with the RFC Summary line "The built-in readers and writers keep their names", so keep them as wrappers or aliases.
fact.priorDecision: Weak only. rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:246 (accepted) names both factories and notes that drm builds its readers map with them, and rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md:238 says the names and rules of that RFC do not change. Neither text decides that the factories must stay or that the `type` argument must go. CHANGELOG.md:248 records the factories as a deliberate addition for custom sample entry types.

The RFC sections Contract (lines 193-203) and Drawbacks (lines 236-244) do not name the removal, and no line says who sets `type` on the result. The RFC example at lines 104-111 returns `type: 'mfhd'` from the reader. A grep of libs/iso-bmff/src shows no built-in reader with a second parameter. readAudioSampleEntryBox.ts:17-20 takes `(type, view)`, so createAudioSampleEntryReader.ts:32 and the wrappers such as readMp4a.ts:15 exist only to adapt the argument order. libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:42-43 calls the factories for 6 audio and 10 video types. The writer side has no factory: drm assigns `writeAudioSampleEntryBox` directly (ensureEncryptedInit.ts:56-57).

Prior decision: the second argument is intentional. The factories are older (alpha.4, CHANGELOG.md:248) and were not removed after PR 290. No issue, PR, or RFC decides to keep the factories over a plain reader. gh search for `createAudioSampleEntryReader` returned only issue 651, which is unrelated. The recommended fix has three problems.

The factory returns `AudioSampleEntryBox<T>` with the literal `T`. `IsoBoxReaderReturn` (src/IsoBoxReaderReturn.ts:37-55) builds the union from the return type of each reader, not from the map key. test/int64.types.test.ts:1056-1066 asserts that `box.type === 'ec-3'` narrows to the sample entry. CHANGELOG.md:234 (alpha.6) fixed the inference of the factories on purpose. A reader that returns `type: cursor.type` has the wide type `IsoBoxType` (src/IsoBoxType.ts:6, a template of four strings). That member then matches every `box.type === '...'` check, because `Box` defaults to `type: never` (src/boxes/Box.ts:8) and no wide member exists today.

No spec text is involved. No settled decision is broken.
value.priorDecision: PR 290 (commit d429da2d2, 1.0.0-alpha.8, CHANGELOG.md:214 "Updated box reader functions to allow a type parameter to be passed in") added the second `type` argument of a reader on purpose. The factories come from 1.0.0-alpha.4 (CHANGELOG.md:248), and alpha.6 fixed their type inference (CHANGELOG.md:234). The accepted RFC rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:246 names both factories and the drm assignment as a supported case. No decision keeps the factories over a plain reader, and the pending cursor RFC does not state the removal of the argument.
value.correction:
State the rule in rfc/iso-bmff-cursor-api.md (types, Contract, Drawbacks). Keep the second argument that PR 290 added, and do not add a `type` field to the cursor: `type IsoBoxReader<B = unknown, T extends IsoBoxType = IsoBoxType, V extends IsoInt64 = number> = (cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<V>, type: T) => B`. The tree reader passes the type from the box header. Also state that the reader returns `type`, as the RFC example already does.

Change the argument order of the two generic readers to match that signature: `readAudioSampleEntry<T extends IsoBoxType>(cursor, type: T): AudioSampleEntryBox<T>` and `readVisualSampleEntry<T extends IsoBoxType>(cursor, type: T): VisualSampleEntryBox<T>`. drm then writes `dynamic[type] = readAudioSampleEntry` with no closure, and a direct call after `seekIsoBox` passes the literal and gets the literal type.

Keep the 9 named readers as one-line functions (`readMp4a(cursor)` calls `readAudioSampleEntry(cursor, 'mp4a')`). They keep the literal return type, they match the named writers, and a bundler removes the unused ones.

Remove `createAudioSampleEntryReader` and `createVisualSampleEntryReader` only if `IsoBoxReaderReturn` takes the literal from the map key when the return type of a reader has the wide `type`. Without that change, `{ 'ec-3': readAudioSampleEntry }` loses the narrowing that test/int64.types.test.ts:1056-1066 asserts, and the factories must stay as the typed form. That type change is not tried yet, so the RFC should list it as an open question.

[]))` (utils.ts:135-137) and `const uuidBox = box as unknown as UuidParsedBox` (validateC2paMerkleSegment.ts:42). Keep the proposal for iso-bmff: `systemId: Uint8Array`, `kids: Uint8Array[]` (one 16-byte view for each key ID, empty for version 0), `data: Uint8Array`, and decide `kidCount` and `dataSize` with the count-field finding (issue 625). Apply the same type to `defaultKid` of `TrackEncryptionBox` (TrackEncryptionBox.ts:22) so that all key IDs have one type. Drop the sentence about `getPsshData`, or file it as a separate drm item: `readPssh` takes a read view and not a buffer, `getPsshData` returns an `ArrayBufferLike` copy to the end of the buffer, and a switch changes the public return type of a drm function and its bundle cost.
fact.priorDecision: PR 657 (commit 83716b139, issue 649) kept the flat list on purpose in a minor version: "The kid field stays a number[] with 16 numbers for each key ID, so the type ProtectionSystemSpecificHeaderBox does not change." libs/iso-bmff/CHANGELOG.md:89 documents that layout. The facts are correct. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/ProtectionSystemSpecificHeaderBox.ts:10-19 has `systemId: number[]`, `kidCount: number`, `kid: number[]`, `dataSize: number`, `data: number[]`. readPssh.ts:29 reads `readArray(UINT, 1, kidCount * 16)` and readPssh.ts:33 reads `data` one number for each byte. writePssh.ts:24-26 takes both sizes from `box.kidCount` and `box.dataSize`. ISO/IEC 23001-7:2016 clause 8.1.2 (spec text lines 674-693) defines `unsigned int(8)[16] KID` repeated `KID_count` times, so a list of 16-byte values is the literal shape.

The category "spec-compliance" is too strong. The bytes that the reader and the writer handle are correct since PR 657. The problem is the shape of the parsed value (developer experience and performance), not a spec violation.

Prior decision: PR 657 (fix for issue 649, merged 2026-11-13) kept the flat list on purpose. Its description says: "`kid` stays a `number[]` with 16 numbers for each key ID. The type `ProtectionSystemSpecificHeaderBox` does not change, so the change does not break the public API." The CHANGELOG.md:89 entry documents the flat layout. That choice was a constraint of a minor version, not a preference for the flat shape, so a major version may change it. The same PR says: "`box.kidCount` stays the source of the count in `writePssh`. Issue #625 covers that question." Issue 625 is still OPEN with no rule chosen.

Value: the type change is a clear gain. The package already uses `Uint8Array` views for opaque bytes: `messageData` (EventMessageBox.ts:18), `data` of mdat, free, imda (MediaDataBox.ts:8, FreeSpaceBox.ts:8, IdentifiedMediaDataBox.ts:9), and `initializationVector` (EncryptedSample.ts:9). `IsoBoxReadView.readData` (IsoBoxReadView.ts:291) returns a view with no copy. A PlayReady `pssh` payload has several thousand bytes, and `number[]` costs one DataView read and one array slot for each byte. EME takes a BufferSource, so `data: Uint8Array` passes to `generateRequest` with no conversion.

Three parts of the proposal need a change:
1. The proposal covers pssh only. `TrackEncryptionBox` has the same shape for the same kind of value: `defaultKid: number[]` (TrackEncryptionBox.ts:22) and `defaultConstantIv?: number[]` (TrackEncryptionBox.ts:57). A change to pssh alone creates a new inconsistency between the two Common Encryption boxes. `ensureEncryptedInit` in drm has the public option `defaultKid: number[]` (libs/drm/src/ensureEncryptedInit.ts:94, 119, 174) and passes it to the `tenc` box, so drm is affected.
2. "`getPsshData` can then return `readPssh(...).data`" is wrong. `getPsshData(pssh: ArrayBufferLike): ArrayBufferLike` (libs/drm/src/cenc/getPsshData.ts:12-26) takes a complete box with its header, has no import, and returns a copy made by `pssh.slice`. `readPssh` takes a view positioned after the box header and would return a `Uint8Array` view. The rewrite changes a public return type of drm and adds the reader code to a 10-line function with no dependency. It hurts tree-shaking for no gain.
3. The removal of `kidCount` and `dataSize` depends on the rule of issue 625, which is not decided. For pssh the counts carry no information (`kids.length` and `data.byteLength` give the same values), so removal fits the first rule of that issue. The removal must follow the package rule and not precede it.

The name `kids` is a smaller point. The package names most lists with the singular spec name (`chunkOffset` in ChunkOffsetBox.ts:12, `entrySize` in SampleSizeBox.ts:12, `offset` in SampleAuxiliaryInformationOffsetsBox.ts:13), and `trackIds` (TrackReferenceTypeBox.ts:8) is the exception. The plural name needs one package-wide rule, not a pssh-only choice.

No settled decision is broken: the writer still follows `version` to decide whether it writes the key ID list.

value.correction:
Change the opaque byte fields of both Common Encryption boxes in 2.0, as one rule: a field that the spec defines as `unsigned int(8)[n]` opaque bytes is a `Uint8Array` view over the source.

A missing export is a compile error, not wrong data. The item is also not a 2.0 API item: it concerns a generator for all 20 packages and breaks no adopter. confirmed.title: The RFC cursor type is invariant in `V`, so a reader of either mode accepts no cursor and the accepted `int64` rule fails to compile.
confirmed.breakingReason: The cursor type is a draft and is not published. The fix changes only the RFC text.
confirmed.evidence: RFC line 146 puts `readers?: IsoBoxReaderMap<V>` on the public cursor, and line 157 makes a reader `(cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<V>) => B`. `V` is then in a parameter position and in a return position (`int64?: IsoInt64Reader<V>`). The accepted RFC names this exact problem at line 370: "The view therefore stores its readers as `IsoBoxReaderMap`, the default instantiation ... If the private field were `IsoBoxReadViewConfig<V>`, the readers would put `V` in a parameter position and make the view invariant." The source follows that rule: `private config: { readers?: IsoBoxReaderMap; int64?: IsoInt64Reader<V> }`. I compiled a model of RFC lines 142 to 159 with TypeScript 6.0.3 in strict mode. Results: `IsoBoxReadCursor<bigint>` and `IsoBoxReadCursor<number>` are both not assignable to `IsoBoxReadCursor<IsoInt64>` (TS2322). A reader `(cursor: IsoBoxReadCursor<IsoInt64>) => ...` is not assignable to `IsoBoxReaderMap<bigint>` or `IsoBoxReaderMap<number>`. `cursor.int64(cursor, 8, false)` inside a generic field function is TS2345. The 54 readers that "accept a view of either mode" (uint64 RFC line 244) and both exported `int64` functions depend on that assignment. RFC line 241 states that "the names and the rules of both RFCs do not change".
confirmed.proposal: Type the field as `readers?: IsoBoxReaderMap` (the default instantiation, as the private field does today), or keep the readers map out of the public cursor type. The same model compiles with no error after that one change. Add the three assignments above to the type tests, as `test/int64.types.test.ts` does for the view.

confirmed.evidence: RFC: "`beginIsoBox(cursor, type)` | Writes a box header with no size. Returns the start position." and "`endIsoBox(cursor, start)` | Writes the size into the header at `start`." ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 clause 4.2 has `else if (size==0) { // box extends to end of file }`, and the reader of this package follows it: `} else if (size === 0) { actualSize = bytesRemaining }`. A custom writer that omits `endIsoBox`, or passes the `start` of another box, produces bytes that read back as one box that contains every later box, with no error. In version 1 a wrong size ends in a `RangeError` from the `DataView` or in visible zero bytes. The RFC also does not state the result for a box above 2^32 - 1 bytes. The header has 8 bytes when the box begins, and `largesize` needs 8 more bytes before the body. Version 1 has that branch: `const isLarge = size > 0xffffffff`.
confirmed.proposal: State in the contract that `writeIsoBoxes` and `writeIsoBox` check each box after its writer returns and throw when the size field at the start of the box is still 0. Benefit: the reader cannot return a value outside the union, so no throw is needed, a `switch` is exhaustive, and the writer rejects a bad value at compile time and no longer needs the mask. confirmed.title: List fields follow two naming rules: a list of numbers keeps the singular spec name, a list of records gets a plural name, and three lists follow neither rule.

So `box.offset`, `box.priority` and `box.kid` read as one value. Plural name: `entries` in 12 types (stts, ctts, stsc, stss, stsh, elst, dref, stsd, sbgp, sgpd, subs, tfra) and a specific plural in sidx `references`, ssix `subsegments` and `ranges`, subs `subsamples`, trun and senc `samples`, prsl `entities`, iloc `items` and `extents`, ftyp and styp `compatibleBrands`, `trackIds`. The record lists follow one hidden rule, the plural of the stem of the count field: `entry_count` and `number_of_entry` give `entries`, `reference_count` gives `references`, `sample_count` gives `samples`. confirmed.proposal: State one rule in the README and apply it. Every array field has a plural name. A record list uses the plural of the stem of the count field, as it does today. A number list uses the plural of the spec element name: `chunkOffsets`, `entrySizes`, `priorities`, `offsets`, `sampleInfoSizes`, `toItemIds`, `kids`. If stss and prsl become plain arrays (already reported), name them `sampleNumbers` and `entityIds`. Rename senc `subsampleEncryption` to `subsamples`. Fixed-length values such as `matrix` and `opcolor` are one value with components and keep the singular name. Each rename is a break. Give the old and new names in one migration table.

rejected.title: A `number` that does not fit its field is written with silent wrap, but a `bigint` with the same value throws a `RangeError`.

fact.reason:
Every factual statement holds at HEAD 8ce63c212.

Code, in libs/iso-bmff/src/IsoBoxWriteView.ts:
- Line 55 (doc of `writeUint`, method at line 66): `The method does not check the value.`
- Lines 178 to 191 (`writeWideUint`): `if (typeof value !== 'bigint') { this.writeUint(value, size) }`, and at line 184 `if (BigInt.asUintN(32, value) !== value) { throw new RangeError(...) }`.
- Lines 204 to 219 (`writeWideInt`) have the same split: a `number` goes to `writeInt`, a `bigint` gets the `BigInt.asIntN` check.
- Lines 310 to 314 (`writeTemplate`) pass `Math.round(value * 2^shift)` to `writeUint` with no check.
- Lines 93 to 97: in 8 bytes, `s1 > 0xffffffff` writes all bits set. In 4 bytes, `setUint32` applies ToUint32.

Docs, libs/iso-bmff/docs/writing-boxes.md:
- Line 171: `A writer throws a RangeError for a bigint that does not fit the field.`
- Line 173: `A writer does not check the range of a number.`

Runtime, read-only run of the source on Node 24.22.3. All results match the finding:
- `writeTfdt` version 0 with `2 ** 32 + 5` writes `00 00 00 05`. The same value as a bigint throws `RangeError writeWideUint: value must be in the range 0 to 2^32 - 1, received 4294967301`.
- `writeUint(256, 1)` writes `00`. `writeUint(1.9, 4)` writes `00 00 00 01`. `writeUint(NaN, 4)` writes 0. `writeUint(-1, 4)` writes `ff ff ff ff`.
- `writeTemplate(65536, 4)` writes 0.
- `writeUint(2 ** 64, 8)` writes all bits set. `writeUint(2 ** 32, 4)` writes 0.
- Extra: `writeWideInt(2 ** 31, 4)` writes `80 00 00 00` (a negative value), and the same bigint throws.

Spec: 14496-12-2015.txt lines 1255 to 1262, clause 6.2.2: values `do not 'wrap' to 0 when the maximum value that can be stored in their field is reached; appropriately large fields must be used for all values`. The quote and the clause number are correct.

Two cautions for the proposal, neither changes the facts:
1. The current rule is deliberate and documented (see priorDecision). The task lists the int64 rules of rfc/uint64-reader-config.md as settled, so the proposal amends an accepted RFC row and needs an explicit decision.
2. The proposal can collide with the settled rule that a writer does not throw for a missing field. 18 of the 20 built-in call sites pass the field with no default, for example writeTfdt.ts:28 `writer.writeWideUint(box.baseMediaDecodeTime, size)`. Today a missing field (`undefined`) writes 0 (verified: `writeTfdt({type:'tfdt',version:0,flags:0})` writes `0 0 0 0`). A range check written as `!(value >= 0 && value <= max)` would throw for `undefined` and `NaN`. The check must let a missing value write 0, or the writers must add `?? 0`.

Cost: the check is two comparisons on a `number` per wide field. `writeElst`, `writeTfra`, and `writeSidx` call the methods per entry, so measure before the decision.
fact.priorDecision: rfc/uint64-reader-config.md:260 (accepted RFC, PR 613, implemented in PR 645) defines the current rule: "A `number` goes to `writeUint(value, size)`. ... Line 264 adds that `writeUint` and `writeInt` "do not change". libs/iso-bmff/docs/writing-boxes.md:173 documents the result for adopters: "A writer does not check the range of a `number`." libs/iso-bmff/CHANGELOG.md:96 (issue 653, PR 669) chose to write all bits set for a `number` of 2^64 or more in 8 bytes, not to throw. The asymmetry is therefore intentional and documented, not an oversight. No decision was found that states a reason to keep the 4-byte wrap for a `number`.

The proposal is wrong for stsz and saiz, for four reasons.

1. The two cases differ in meaning. A version 0 pssh has no key ID list and `kidCount` is 0, so `[]` agrees with the count. With `entrySize: []` and `sampleCount: 3`, the count and the list length disagree. Issue 625 already names stsz as the box where the list is legitimately absent.

2. The optional type is a compile-time guard. With `entrySize?: number[]`, the code `stsz.entrySize[i]` does not compile under strict mode, so the adopter must read `sampleSize`. With a required `[]`, the same code compiles and returns `undefined` for every sample of a constant-size track. AGENTS.md states that incorrect usage should fail at compile time. The `stsz.entrySize ?? []` example in the finding is the wrong usage: the loop reads no sizes for a track that has samples.

3. The rule "a list field is always an array" also covers two optional lists that the finding does not name. libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/TrackEncryptionBox.ts:57 has `defaultConstantIv?: number[]`, and libs/iso-bmff/src/boxes/EncryptedSample.ts:10 has `subsampleEncryption?: SubsampleEncryption[]`. PR 658 set this rule on purpose. An always-present `[]` makes `writeTenc` write a constant IV size byte of 0 for every box.

4. The cost is real and the gain is small. A writer input for a constant-size stsz must contain `entrySize: []`, or the package needs separate input and output types. Two types add public API for no adopter task.

The ctts and emsg cases are not evidence for the array rule. PR 674 and PR 676 concern versions outside the defined syntax, and the stated reason was no compile break in a minor version. The stsz and saiz conditions are inside the defined syntax.

Do not change the stsz or saiz types. State the existing rule in the package docs, which is not a breaking change and can land at any time:

- A list with its own count field is always an array. The list is empty when the syntax has no list for the version, and the count is then 0. Example: `kid` of a version 0 pssh.
- A list that the syntax omits for a flag or a field value, while a sample count stays valid, is an optional field. The field is absent. Examples: `entrySize` of stsz, `sampleInfoSize` of saiz, `defaultConstantIv` of tenc, `subsampleEncryption` of a senc sample.
